title.zh: 卷三十三 列傳第二十一: 李靈 李順 李孝伯 李裔 李義深
title.raw: 卷三十三 列傳第二十一: 李靈 李順 李孝伯 李裔 李義深 Volume 33 Biographies 21:

sentences.zh: 李靈 李順 李孝伯 李裔 李義深

translations.literal: Li Ling, Li Shun, Li Xiaobo, Li Yi, Li Yishen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ling, Li Shun, Li Xiaobo, Li Yi, and Li Yishen.

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十一

translations.literal: Biography number twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 21

sentences.zh: 李靈曾孫元忠渾弟子璨璨曾孫德饒公緒李順玄孫元操李孝伯兄孫謐謐弟子士謙李裔子子雄李義深弟幼廉

translations.literal: Li Ling's great-grandson Yuanzhong; Hun's brother's son Can; Can's great-grandson Derao; Gongxu; Li Shun's great-great-grandson Yuancao; Li Xiaobo's elder brother's grandson Mi; Mi's younger brother's son Shiqian; Li Yi's son Zixiong; Li Yishen's younger brother Youlian.
translations.idiomatic: Included in this account are Yuanzhong, great-grandson of Li Ling; Can, nephew of Hun; Derao, great-grandson of Can; Gongxu; Yuancao, great-great-grandson of Li Shun; Mi, grandson of Li Xiaobo's elder brother; Shiqian, nephew of Mi; Zixiong, son of Li Yi; and Youlian, younger brother of Li Yishen.

sentences.zh: 李靈，字武符，趙郡平棘人也。

translations.literal: Li Ling, styled Wufu, was a native of Pingji in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ling, whose style name was Wufu, came from Pingji in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父勰，字小同，恬靜好學，有聲趙、魏間。

translations.literal: His father Xie, styled Xiaotong, was tranquil and fond of learning, and had a reputation between Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie, styled Xiaotong, was quiet and devoted to study, and won renown throughout Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 道武平中原，聞其已亡，哀惜之，贈宣威將軍、蘭陵太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu pacified the Central Plains, he heard that Xie had already died and mourned him, posthumously appointing him General Who Proclaims Might and Administrator of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu conquered the Central Plains, he learned that Xie was already dead and grieved for him, posthumously granting him the titles General Who Proclaims Might and Administrator of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 神蒨中，太武征天下才俊，靈至，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: In the Shenqi era, Emperor Taiwu summoned talented men from throughout the realm; Ling arrived and was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenqi reign, Emperor Taiwu called up outstanding men from across the empire; Ling came forward and was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 再遷淮陽太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to serve as Administrator of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Administrator of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 以學優，選授文成皇帝經，加中散、內博士，賜爵高邑子。

translations.literal: Because of his excellence in learning, he was selected to instruct the future Emperor Wencheng in the classics, was additionally made Central Scattered Courtier and Inner Erudite, and was granted the title Viscount of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: On account of his scholarly distinction, he was chosen to tutor the future Emperor Wencheng in the classics, was further appointed Central Scattered Courtier and Inner Erudite, and received the enfeoffment of Viscount of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 文成踐阼，卒于洛州刺史，贈定州刺史、钜鹿公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: When Wencheng ascended the throne, Ling died while serving as Governor of Luozhou; he was posthumously made Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Julu, with the posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, Ling died in office as Governor of Luozhou; he was posthumously appointed Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Julu, with the posthumous epithet Jian.

sentences.zh: 子恢襲，以師傅子，拜長安鎮副將，進爵為侯，假钜鹿公。

translations.literal: His son Hui succeeded him; as the son of an imperial tutor, he was appointed Deputy General of Chang'an Garrison, advanced in rank to Marquis, and given the provisional title Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui inherited his line; as the son of an imperial tutor, he was appointed Deputy General of the Chang'an garrison, raised to marquis, and granted the provisional title Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 後東平王道符謀反，遇害，贈定州刺史、钜鹿公，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Later, when Prince of Dongping Daofu rebelled, Hui was killed in the affair; he was posthumously made Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Julu, with the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Prince of Dongping, Daofu, rose in rebellion, Hui was killed in the turmoil; he was posthumously appointed Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Julu, with the posthumous epithet Zhen.

sentences.zh: 恢弟綜，事見於後。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Zong is treated later in this account.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Zong is discussed later in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 長子悅祖，襲爵高邑侯，例降為伯，卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yuezu inherited the title Marquis of Gaoyi, which by regulation was reduced to Baron, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yuezu inherited the rank of Marquis of Gaoyi, which was reduced by precedent to baron, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 悅祖子瑾，字伯瓊，襲，位大司農卿。

translations.literal: Yuezu's son Jin, styled Boqiong, succeeded and rose to Minister of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezu's son Jin, styled Boqiong, inherited the line and rose to Minister of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 瑾淳謹好學，老而不倦。

translations.literal: Jin was pure, careful, and fond of learning, and did not weary of it even in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was upright, conscientious, and devoted to learning, and never tired of study even in his later years.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 悅祖弟顯甫，豪俠知名，集諸李數千家于殷州西山，開李魚川方五六十里居之，顯甫為其宗主。

translations.literal: Yuezu's younger brother Xianfu was famed as a bold knight-errant; he gathered several thousand households of the Li clan on the western hills of Yinzhou, opened the Li Fish River valley some fifty or sixty li square for them to settle in, and Xianfu became their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezu's younger brother Xianfu was renowned as a man of heroic spirit; he gathered several thousand Li households on the western hills of Yinzhou, opened the Li Fish River valley—some fifty or sixty li across—for them to inhabit, and served as their clan leader.

sentences.zh: 以軍功賜爵平棘子，位河南太守，贈安州刺史，諡曰安。

translations.literal: For military merit he was granted the title Viscount of Pingji, rose to Administrator of Henan, and was posthumously made Governor of Anzhou with the posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: For military achievement he received the enfeoffment of Viscount of Pingji, served as Administrator of Henan, and at death was posthumously appointed Governor of Anzhou with the posthumous epithet An.

sentences.zh: 子元忠，少厲志操。

translations.literal: His son Yuanzhong in youth cultivated resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanzhong in his youth cultivated firm purpose and moral discipline.

sentences.zh: 粗覽書史及陰陽術數，有巧思，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: He had a rough acquaintance with books, histories, and the arts of yin-yang and numerology, possessed ingenious ideas, and was known for filial piety during mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He had some acquaintance with historical writings and with yin-yang lore and divination, showed a gift for ingenious contrivance, and won renown for filial devotion during mourning.

sentences.zh: 襲爵平棘子，魏清河王懌為營明堂大都督，引為主簿。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Viscount of Pingji; when the Wei Prince of Qinghe, Yi, served as Grand Commander for the construction of the Bright Hall, he recruited Yuanzhong as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Viscount of Pingji; when the Wei Prince of Qinghe, Yi, was appointed Grand Commander for the construction of the Bright Hall, he took Yuanzhong on as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂去任，歸李魚川。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he left his post and returned to Li Fish River.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he resigned his office and returned to Li Fish River.

sentences.zh: 嘗亡二馬，既獲盜，即以與之。

translations.literal: Once he lost two horses; when the thief was caught, he simply gave the horses to him.
translations.idiomatic: He once lost two horses; when the thief was apprehended, he simply let the man keep them.

sentences.zh: 在母喪，哭泣哀動旁人，而飲酒騎射不廢，曰：「禮豈為我？

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother he wept so mournfully as to move those around him, yet he did not give up drinking, riding, or archery, saying, "Is ritual made for me?"
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he wept so bitterly as to move all who heard him, yet he never stopped drinking, riding, or shooting, saying, "Was ritual made for me?"

sentences.zh: 」初元忠以母多患，專心醫藥，遂善方技，性仁恕，無貴賤皆為救療。

translations.literal: " Earlier, because his mother suffered frequent illness, Yuanzhong had devoted himself to medicine and pharmacy and thus became skilled in medical techniques; by nature he was benevolent and forgiving, and treated the sick without regard to rank.
translations.idiomatic: " From early on, because his mother was often ill, Yuanzhong had devoted himself to medicine and thereby became skilled in healing arts; by nature he was kind and forgiving, and treated the sick without distinction of high or low.

sentences.zh: 家素富，在鄉多有出貸求利，元忠焚契免責，鄉人甚敬之。

translations.literal: His family had long been wealthy and in the countryside had many loans out at interest; Yuanzhong burned the contracts and released the debtors, and the villagers greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been wealthy and had many loans outstanding in the countryside; Yuanzhong burned the contracts and released the debtors from obligation, and the people of the district held him in deep respect.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，盜賊蜂起，清河有五百人西戍；

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaozhuang, bandits rose everywhere; five hundred men from Qinghe were garrisoned in the west.
translations.idiomatic: In the reign of Emperor Xiaozhuang, bandits swarmed everywhere; five hundred men from Qinghe had been posted to western garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 還經南趙郡，以路梗，共投元忠，奉絹千餘匹。

translations.literal: On their return they passed through Southern Zhao commandery; because the roads were blocked, they all turned to Yuanzhong together and presented more than a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: On their way home they passed through Southern Zhao commandery; the roads being impassable, they all sought refuge with Yuanzhong and presented him with more than a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 元忠唯受一匹，殺五牛以食之，遣奴為導，曰：「若逢賊，但道李元忠遣。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong accepted only one bolt, slaughtered five oxen to feed them, and sent a servant to guide them, saying, "If you meet bandits, simply say you were sent by Li Yuanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong accepted only one bolt, slaughtered five oxen to feast them, and sent a servant to guide them, saying, "If you meet bandits, simply tell them Li Yuanzhong sent you."

sentences.zh: 」如言，賊皆舍避。

translations.literal: " As he said, the bandits all let them pass.
translations.idiomatic: " It happened as he said: the bandits all stood aside and let them go.

sentences.zh: 及葛榮起，元忠率宗黨作壘以自保，坐於大槲樹下，前後斬違命者凡三百人。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong rose in rebellion, Yuanzhong led the clan to build fortifications for self-defense; seated beneath a great oak tree, he executed those who disobeyed orders, three hundred in all before and after.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong rose in rebellion, Yuanzhong led the clan to build fortifications for their defense; seated beneath a great oak tree, he executed those who defied his orders—three hundred men in all, before and after.

sentences.zh: 賊至，元忠輒卻之。

translations.literal: Whenever bandits came, Yuanzhong drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the rebels came, Yuanzhong beat them back.

sentences.zh: 葛榮曰：「我自中山至此，連為趙李所破，則何以能成大事？

translations.literal: Ge Rong said, "From Zhongshan to here I have been repeatedly defeated by the Zhao Lis—how then can I accomplish great things?"
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong said, "From Zhongshan to here I have been beaten again and again by the Li clan of Zhao—how can I hope to accomplish anything great?"

sentences.zh: 」乃悉眾攻圍，執元忠以隨軍。

translations.literal: " He then mustered all his forces to besiege them, seized Yuanzhong, and took him along with the army.
translations.idiomatic: " He then gathered his entire force to lay siege, seized Yuanzhong, and carried him off with the army.

sentences.zh: 賊平，就拜南趙郡太守。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was immediately appointed Administrator of Southern Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were suppressed, he was promptly appointed Administrator of Southern Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 好酒，無政績。

translations.literal: He loved wine and achieved nothing in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of drink and left no record of achievement in office.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝幽崩，元忠棄官，潛圖義舉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was secretly put to death, Yuanzhong abandoned his post and secretly plotted a righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang died under suspicious circumstances, Yuanzhong resigned his office and secretly planned a loyal uprising.

sentences.zh: 會齊神武東出，元忠便乘露車載素箏濁酒以奉迎。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu marched east, Yuanzhong took an open cart loaded with a plain zither and muddy wine to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan of Northern Qi marched east, Yuanzhong rode out in an open cart bearing a plain zither and a jar of coarse wine to greet him.

sentences.zh: 神武聞其酒客，未即見之。

translations.literal: Shenwu heard that he was a wine-bibber and did not receive him at once.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan heard that he was a notorious drinker and did not receive him immediately.

sentences.zh: 元忠下車獨坐，酌酒擘脯食之，謂門者曰：「本言公招延俊傑，今聞國士到門，不能吐哺輟洗，其人可知。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong alighted, sat alone, poured wine, tore dried meat and ate, and told the gatekeeper, "It was said that my lord invites outstanding men; now I hear that a man of the realm has come to the gate, yet he cannot spit out his mouthful and stop washing—such a man is plain to see."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong stepped down from his cart, sat alone, poured wine, tore off dried meat and ate, and told the gatekeeper, "Your master claims to seek out men of talent; yet when a true man of the realm comes to his gate, he cannot even interrupt his meal to receive him—the sort of man he is, I think, is clear enough."

sentences.zh: 還吾刺，勿復通也。

translations.literal: Return my calling card and do not announce me again.
translations.idiomatic: Return my card and do not announce me again.

sentences.zh: 」門者以告，神武遽見之。

translations.literal: " The gatekeeper reported this, and Shenwu hurried out to see him.
translations.idiomatic: " When the gatekeeper reported this, Gao Huan rushed out to receive him.

sentences.zh: 引入，觴再行，元忠車上取箏鼓之，長歌慷慨。

translations.literal: He was brought in; after two rounds of wine Yuanzhong took the zither from his cart and played it, singing a long song with passionate force.
translations.idiomatic: He was ushered in; after two rounds of wine Yuanzhong took the zither from his cart and played, singing a long, impassioned song.

sentences.zh: 歌闋。

translations.literal: When the song ended.
translations.idiomatic: When the song ended,

sentences.zh: 謂神武曰：「天下形勢可見，明公猶欲事爾硃乎？

translations.literal: he said to Shenwu, "The trend of the realm is plain to see—does my lord still wish to serve the Erzhu?"
translations.idiomatic: he said to Gao Huan, "The shape of the realm is plain to see—does my lord still mean to serve the Erzhu clan?"

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「富貴皆由他，安敢不盡節。

translations.literal: " Shenwu said, "Wealth and honor all come from them—how would I dare not give my utmost loyalty?"
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan said, "Wealth and rank all come from them—how could I dare not serve them with my whole heart?"

sentences.zh: 」元忠曰：「非英雄也。

translations.literal: " Yuanzhong said, "You are no hero."
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanzhong said, "Then you are no hero."

sentences.zh: 高乾邕兄弟曾來未？

translations.literal: Have the brothers Gao Gan and Gao Yong come yet?
translations.idiomatic: Have the brothers Gao Gan and Gao Yong come to see you yet?

sentences.zh: 」是時，高乾邕已見，神武因紿曰：「從叔輩粗，何肯來？

translations.literal: " At that time Gao Gan and Gao Yong had already come; Shenwu therefore deceived him, saying, "Those uncouth fellows from my clan—why would they come?"
translations.idiomatic: " By then Gao Gan and Gao Yong had already visited him; Gao Huan therefore lied, saying, "Those rough cousins of mine—why would they come?"

sentences.zh: 」元忠曰：「雖粗，並解事。

translations.literal: " Yuanzhong said, "Rough though they are, they both understand affairs."
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanzhong said, "Rough they may be, but they both know how to get things done."

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「趙郡醉！

translations.literal: " Shenwu said, "The man from Zhao commandery is drunk!"
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan cried, "The Zhao man is drunk!"

sentences.zh: 」使人扶出，元忠不肯起。

translations.literal: " He had men help him out, but Yuanzhong would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: " He had men help Yuanzhong out, but Yuanzhong refused to get up.

sentences.zh: 孫騰進曰：「此君天遣來，不可違也。

translations.literal: Sun Teng stepped forward and said, "This gentleman was sent by Heaven—he must not be turned away."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng stepped forward and said, "This man was sent by Heaven—you cannot turn him away."

sentences.zh: 」神武乃復留與言，元忠慷慨流涕，神武亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: " Shenwu then kept him again to talk; Yuanzhong wept freely in passionate grief, and Shenwu too was overcome with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan then kept him and spoke with him further; Yuanzhong wept freely in impassioned grief, and Gao Huan too was overcome with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 元忠進從橫之策，深見嘉納。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong advanced strategies of alliance and opposition and was deeply praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong offered strategies of alliance and maneuver, and Gao Huan warmly embraced his counsel.

sentences.zh: 又謂神武曰：「殷州小，無糧仗，不足以注大事。

translations.literal: He also said to Shenwu, "Yinzhou is small and lacks grain and arms—it is not enough to stake great affairs upon."
translations.idiomatic: He also told Gao Huan, "Yinzhou is small and lacks grain and arms—it is not enough to anchor a great enterprise."

sentences.zh: 冀州大籓，若向冀州，高乾邕兄弟必為明公主人。

translations.literal: Jizhou is a great frontier region; if you turn toward Jizhou, the brothers Gao Gan and Gao Yong will surely make you their master.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou is a great stronghold; if you march on Jizhou, the brothers Gao Gan and Gao Yong will surely make you their lord.

sentences.zh: 殷州便以賜委。

translations.literal: Let Yinzhou be granted to me as a charge.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yinzhou, grant it to me as my charge.

sentences.zh: 冀、殷合，滄、瀛、幽、定自然弭從。

translations.literal: With Jizhou and Yinzhou united, Cang, Ying, You, and Ding will naturally submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jizhou and Yinzhou are united, Cang, Ying, You, and Ding will naturally fall in line.

sentences.zh: 唯劉誕黠胡，或當乖拒，然非明公之敵。

translations.literal: Only Liu Yan, a cunning barbarian, may resist—but he is no match for my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liu Yan, a wily barbarian, may hold out against you—but he is no match for my lord.

sentences.zh: 」神武急握元忠手而謝焉。

translations.literal: " Shenwu hastily grasped Yuanzhong's hand and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan seized Yuanzhong's hand in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 時殷州刺史爾硃羽生阻兵據州，元忠聚眾與大軍禽斬之。

translations.literal: At that time the Governor of Yinzhou, Erzhu Yusheng, held the province with rebellious troops; Yuanzhong gathered forces and, with the main army, captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Governor of Yinzhou, Erzhu Yusheng, held the province with rebel troops; Yuanzhong raised a force and, together with the main army, captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 神武即令行殷州事。

translations.literal: Shenwu immediately had him administer the affairs of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan immediately put him in charge of Yinzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷太常卿、殷州大中正。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Ceremonies and Senior Rectifier of Yinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Minister of Ceremonies and Senior Rectifier of Yinzhou.

sentences.zh: 後以從兄瑾年長，以中正讓之。

translations.literal: Later, because his cousin Jin was older, he yielded the rectifier post to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because his cousin Jin was the elder, he yielded the rectifier post to him.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武帝納神武女為後，詔元忠致娉于晉陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei took Shenwu's daughter as empress, Yuanzhong was ordered to deliver the betrothal gifts in Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei took Gao Huan's daughter as empress, Yuanzhong was ordered to deliver the betrothal gifts at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 每宴席論舊事，元忠曰：「昔日建義，轟轟大樂，比來寂寥無人問，更欲覓建義處。

translations.literal: At every banquet when old affairs were discussed, Yuanzhong said, "In the days of the righteous rising there was thunderous rejoicing; lately it has been lonely with no one asking after me—I want to find that place of righteous rising again."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever old times came up at banquets, Yuanzhong would say, "In the days of our righteous rising there was thunderous celebration; lately it has been lonely, with no one asking after me—I am ready to go looking for that righteous rising again."

sentences.zh: 」神武撫掌笑曰：「此人逼我起兵。

translations.literal: " Shenwu clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "This man drove me to raise the army."
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "This man is the one who drove me to take up arms."

sentences.zh: 」賜白馬一匹。

translations.literal: " He was given one white horse.
translations.idiomatic: " He was given a white horse.

sentences.zh: 元忠戲曰：「若不與侍中，當更覓建義處。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong jested, "If you do not make me Attendant-in-Ordinary, I shall go looking for that place of righteous rising again."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong jested, "If you do not make me Attendant-in-Ordinary, I shall go looking for that righteous rising again."

sentences.zh: 」神武曰：「建義處不慮無，止畏如此老翁不可遇耳。

translations.literal: " Shenwu said, "I do not worry that there will be no place of righteous rising—only that such an old fellow as this cannot be met again."
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan said, "I do not worry that there will be no place for a righteous rising—only that an old fellow like this cannot be found again."

sentences.zh: 」元忠曰：「止為此翁難遇，所以不去。

translations.literal: " Yuanzhong said, "It is precisely because such an old fellow is hard to meet that I do not leave."
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanzhong said, "It is precisely because such an old fellow is hard to find that I stay."

sentences.zh: 」因捋神武須大笑。

translations.literal: " He then tugged Shenwu's beard and laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he tugged Gao Huan's beard and laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 神武悉其雅意，深重之。

translations.literal: Shenwu fully understood his refined intent and held him in deep esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan fully understood his playful spirit and held him in deep regard.

sentences.zh: 後神武奉送皇后，仍田于晉澤，元忠馬倒，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: Later, when Shenwu escorted the empress, he went hunting at Jin Marsh; Yuanzhong's horse fell, and only after a long while did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gao Huan escorted the empress, he went hunting at Jin Marsh; Yuanzhong's horse fell, and he lay unconscious for a long while before coming to.

sentences.zh: 神武親自撫視，封晉陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Shenwu personally attended to him and enfeoffed him as Baron of Jinyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan personally tended to him and enfeoffed him as Baron of Jinyang county.

sentences.zh: 後為光州刺史，時州境災儉，人皆菜色，元忠表求賑貸，被報聽用萬石。

translations.literal: He later served as Governor of Guangzhou; at the time the province suffered famine and distress, and the people were gaunt with hunger; Yuanzhong memorialized requesting relief grain and was approved for ten thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Governor of Guangzhou; famine had struck the province and the people were wasted with hunger; Yuanzhong memorialized requesting relief grain and was authorized ten thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 元忠以為少，遂出十五萬石賑之。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong thought this too little and therefore issued one hundred fifty thousand piculs for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong thought this too little and distributed one hundred fifty thousand piculs for relief.

sentences.zh: 事訖，表陳，朝廷嘉而不責。

translations.literal: When the matter was finished he memorialized the court, which praised him and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When the relief was complete he reported to the court, which commended him and imposed no penalty.

sentences.zh: 徵拜侍中。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 元忠雖處要任，初不以物務幹懷，唯以聲酒自娛，大率常醉。

translations.literal: Although Yuanzhong held an important post, he never let official business occupy his mind and amused himself only with music and wine, for the most part constantly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Although Yuanzhong held high office, he never let affairs of state weigh on his mind and amused himself only with music and wine, and was for the most part perpetually drunk.

sentences.zh: 家事大小，了不關心。

translations.literal: Great or small matters of the household he paid no attention to at all.
translations.idiomatic: Great or small matters of the household he ignored entirely.

sentences.zh: 園庭羅種果藥，親朋尋詣，必留連宴賞。

translations.literal: His garden and courtyard were planted with fruit and medicinal herbs; when kin and friends came to visit, he always detained them for feasting and enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: His garden and courtyard were planted with fruit trees and medicinal herbs; whenever kin and friends came to call, he always kept them for long feasts.

sentences.zh: 每挾彈攜壺，遊遨里閈。

translations.literal: He would carry a pellet-bow and wine flask and roam through the lanes of the neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: He would carry a pellet-bow and wine flask and roam the lanes of his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 每言寧無食，不可使我無酒；

translations.literal: He often said, "Better no food than no wine for me."
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of saying that he could go without food, but never without wine.

sentences.zh: 阮步兵吾師也，孔少府豈欺我哉。

translations.literal: Master Ruan the Infantry Colonel is my teacher—would Junior Administrator Kong deceive me?
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji, Master of the Infantry, is my teacher—would Kong Rong the Junior Administrator have lied to me?

sentences.zh: 後自中書令復求為太常卿，以其有音樂而多美酒故。

translations.literal: Later he resigned as Director of the Secretariat and asked again to be Minister of Ceremonies, because that office had music and abundant fine wine.
translations.idiomatic: Later he stepped down from Director of the Secretariat and asked to be made Minister of Ceremonies again, because that office offered music and abundant fine wine.

sentences.zh: 神武欲用為僕射，文襄言其放達常醉，不可委以台閣。

translations.literal: Shenwu wished to appoint him Vice Director of the Secretariat, but Wenxiang said that he was unrestrained and constantly drunk and could not be entrusted with the central offices.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan wished to appoint him Vice Director of the Secretariat, but Gao Cheng said that he was too free-spirited and constantly drunk to be entrusted with the central administration.

sentences.zh: 其子搔聞之，請節酒。

translations.literal: His son Sao heard of this and asked him to moderate his drinking.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sao heard of this and begged him to drink less.

sentences.zh: 元忠曰：「我言作僕射不勝飲酒樂；

translations.literal: Yuanzhong said, "When I speak of becoming Vice Director, it cannot compare with the pleasure of drinking."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong said, "When I speak of becoming Vice Director, it cannot compare with the joy of drinking."

sentences.zh: 爾愛僕射時，宜勿飲酒。

translations.literal: When you love the Vice Directorship, you ought not to drink.
translations.idiomatic: When you care about the Vice Directorship, you ought not to drink.

sentences.zh: 」每言于執事，雲年漸遲暮，乞在閑冗，以養餘年，乃除驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: " He often told those in charge that his years were gradually drawing to evening and begged for a leisurely post to nourish his remaining years; he was therefore appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Bearer of the Three Insignia of Peerage.
translations.idiomatic: " He often told those in charge that his years were drawing toward evening and begged for a leisurely post to spend his remaining days; he was therefore appointed General of Agile Cavalry with the Three Insignia of Peerage.

sentences.zh: 曾貢文襄王蒲桃一盤，文襄報以百縑，其見賞重如此。

translations.literal: Once he presented Prince Wenxiang with a tray of grapes; Wenxiang returned the gift with a hundred bolts of silk—such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Once he presented Prince Wenxiang with a tray of grapes; Gao Cheng returned the gift with a hundred bolts of silk—such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 孫騰司馬子如嘗詣元忠，逢其方坐樹下，葛巾擁被，對壺獨酌。

translations.literal: Sun Teng and Sima Ziru once called on Yuanzhong and found him just then seated beneath a tree, wearing a hemp headcloth and wrapped in a quilt, drinking alone facing his wine jar.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng and Sima Ziru once called on Yuanzhong and found him seated beneath a tree in a hemp headcloth, wrapped in a quilt, drinking alone before his wine jar.

sentences.zh: 庭室蕪曠，使婢卷兩褥以質酒肉。

translations.literal: Courtyard and rooms overgrown and deserted; he had a maid roll two quilts to pawn for wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: His courtyard and rooms had gone to ruin; he sent a maid to roll up two quilts and pawn them for wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 呼妻出，衣不曳地。

translations.literal: He called his wife out; her garment did not even trail on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He called his wife out; her dress scarcely reached the floor.

sentences.zh: 二公相視，歎息而去，大餉米絹，受而散之。

translations.literal: The two gentlemen looked at each other, sighed, and left; they sent a large gift of rice and silk, which he accepted and distributed.
translations.idiomatic: The two men looked at each other, sighed, and departed; they sent a large gift of rice and silk, which he accepted and gave away.

sentences.zh: 俄復以本官領衛尉卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Commandant of the Guards while retaining his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed Commandant of the Guards while retaining his former rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，有米三石，酒數斛，書籍藥物，充滿篋架。

translations.literal: When he died he left three piculs of rice, several hu of wine, and books and medicines filling chests and shelves.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he left three piculs of rice, several hu of wine, and books and medicines filling chests and shelves.

sentences.zh: 未及賻至，金蟬質絹，乃得斂焉。

translations.literal: Before condolence gifts arrived, he pawned gold cicadas for silk and only then could be laid in the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Before condolence gifts arrived, he had to pawn gold cicada ornaments for silk before the burial could proceed.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，諡曰敬惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister over the Masses, with the posthumous title Jinghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister over the Masses, with the posthumous epithet Jinghui.

sentences.zh: 初，元忠將仕，夢手執炬入其父墓。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuanzhong was about to take office, he dreamed that he held a torch and entered his father's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yuanzhong was about to enter official life, he dreamed that he held a torch and walked into his father's tomb.

sentences.zh: 中夜驚起，甚惡之。

translations.literal: He started up in alarm in the middle of the night and greatly abhorred it.
translations.idiomatic: He woke in alarm in the middle of the night and was deeply troubled by the dream.

sentences.zh: 旦告其受業師，占云：「大吉，可謂光照先人也。

translations.literal: At dawn he told his teacher of studies, who divined and said, "Great good fortune—this may be called illuminating one's ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he told his teacher, who divined the dream and said, "Great good fortune—this means you will bring glory to your ancestors."

sentences.zh: 」竟如其占。

translations.literal: " In the end it happened just as the divination said.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end events unfolded exactly as the divination had foretold.

sentences.zh: 性甚工彈，彈桐葉常出一孔，擲棗栗而彈之，十中七八。

translations.literal: By nature he was highly skilled with the pellet-bow; shooting at paulownia leaves he often pierced a single hole, and when he tossed jujubes and chestnuts and shot at them, he hit seven or eight out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: He was exceptionally skilled with the pellet-bow; shooting at paulownia leaves he often put a single hole through them, and when he tossed up jujubes and chestnuts to shoot at, he hit seven or eight out of ten.

sentences.zh: 嘗從文襄入謁魏帝，有梟鳴殿上，文襄命元忠彈之，問得幾丸而落，對曰：「一丸奉至尊威靈，一丸承大將軍意氣，兩丸足矣！

translations.literal: Once he accompanied Wenxiang to audience with the Wei emperor; an owl cried in the hall, and Wenxiang ordered Yuanzhong to shoot it and asked how many pellets it would take to bring it down; he replied, "One pellet for the supreme majesty's awesome power, one for the Grand General's spirit—two pellets are enough!"
translations.idiomatic: Once he accompanied Gao Cheng to audience with the Wei emperor; an owl cried in the hall, and Gao Cheng ordered Yuanzhong to shoot it down and asked how many pellets it would take; he replied, "One pellet for the Son of Heaven's august power, one for the Grand General's spirit—two pellets will suffice!"

sentences.zh: 」如其言而落之。

translations.literal: " As he said, he brought it down.
translations.idiomatic: " As he had said, he brought the bird down.

sentences.zh: 子搔嗣。

translations.literal: His son Sao succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sao inherited his line.

sentences.zh: 搔字德沈，少聰敏，有才藝。

translations.literal: Sao, styled Deshen, was clever and quick-witted in youth and had talent in the arts.
translations.idiomatic: Sao, styled Deshen, was clever and quick-witted as a youth and showed talent in the arts.

sentences.zh: 曾采諸聲，別造一器，號曰八弦，時人稱有思理。

translations.literal: He once gathered various tones and separately devised an instrument called the Eight Strings; people of the time praised it as thoughtfully designed.
translations.idiomatic: He once gathered various musical tones and devised a new instrument called the Eight Strings; contemporaries praised it as ingeniously conceived.

sentences.zh: 武定末，自丞相記室除河內太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wuding era he was transferred from Chief Clerk of the Chancellor to Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he was promoted from chief clerk of the chancellor to Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 居數載，流人盡復。

translations.literal: After several years in office, all displaced persons had returned.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office, all displaced persons had been restored to their homes.

sentences.zh: 代至，將還都，父老號泣，追送二百餘里，生為立碑。

translations.literal: When his replacement arrived and he was about to return to the capital, the elders wept and wailed and escorted him for more than two hundred li; while he was still alive they erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: When his successor arrived and he prepared to return to the capital, the elders wept and escorted him for more than two hundred li; they erected a stele in his honor while he was still alive.

sentences.zh: 終於儀曹郎。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Gentleman of the Ceremonial Office.

sentences.zh: 搔妹曰法行，幼好道，截指自誓不嫁，遂為尼。

translations.literal: Sao's younger sister, called Faxing, from youth loved the Way; she cut off a finger and vowed not to marry, and thus became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Sao's younger sister, called Faxing, had loved the Way from childhood; she cut off a finger and vowed never to marry, and became a nun.

sentences.zh: 所居去鄴三百里，往來恆步，在路或不得食，飲水而已。

translations.literal: Her dwelling was three hundred li from Ye; she always walked back and forth, and on the road sometimes had nothing to eat and drank only water.
translations.idiomatic: Her dwelling lay three hundred li from Ye; she always walked the journey on foot, and on the road sometimes had nothing to eat and drank only water.

sentences.zh: 逢屠牽牛，脫衣求贖，泣而隨之。

translations.literal: When she met a butcher leading an ox, she stripped off her garment to ransom it and followed weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When she met a butcher leading an ox to slaughter, she stripped off her garment to ransom it and followed weeping.

sentences.zh: 雉兔馴狎，入其山居房室。

translations.literal: Pheasants and hares grew tame and entered her mountain dwelling and rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Pheasants and hares grew tame and entered her mountain dwelling.

sentences.zh: 齊亡後，遭時大檢，施糜粥于路。

translations.literal: After the fall of Qi, when a great inspection of the times came, she distributed millet gruel by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Northern Qi, during a time of widespread hardship, she distributed millet gruel by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 異母弟宗侃與族人孝衡爭地相毀，尼曰：「我有地，二家欲得者，任來取之，何為輕致忿訟？

translations.literal: Her half-brother Zongkan and the clansman Xiaoheng quarreled over land and slandered each other; the nun said, "I have land—if both families want it, let them come and take it as they please; why lightly stir up angry litigation?"
translations.idiomatic: Her half-brother Zongkan and the clansman Xiaoheng quarreled over land and brought accusations against each other; the nun said, "I have land—if both families want it, let them come and take what they wish; why stir up angry lawsuits over so little?"

sentences.zh: 」宗侃等慚，遂讓為閒田。

translations.literal: " Zongkan and the others were ashamed and yielded it as common land.
translations.idiomatic: " Zongkan and the others were ashamed and left the land as communal ground.

sentences.zh: 渾字季初，靈之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Hun, styled Jichu, was the great-grandson of Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Hun, styled Jichu, was the great-grandson of Li Ling.

sentences.zh: 祖綜，行河間郡，早卒。

translations.literal: Grandfather Zong, acting Administrator of Hejian, died young.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zong served as acting administrator of Hejian and died in middle age.

sentences.zh: 父遵，字良軌，有業尚，為魏冀州征東府司馬。

translations.literal: His father Zun, styled Lianggui, had scholarly attainments and served as Military Affairs Officer of the Eastern Campaign Headquarters in Jizhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun, styled Lianggui, was a man of learning and principle and served as Military Affairs Officer of the Eastern Campaign Headquarters in Jizhou under Wei.

sentences.zh: 京兆王愉冀州起逆，遇害。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, rose in rebellion in Jizhou, Zun was killed in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, rebelled in Jizhou, Zun was killed in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 贈幽州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Youzhou with the posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Youzhou with the posthumous epithet Jian.

sentences.zh: 渾以父死王事，除給事中。

translations.literal: Because his father died in the prince's service, Hun was appointed Supervising Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died in loyal service to the throne, Hun was appointed Supervising Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後以四方多難，求為青州征東司馬，與河間邢邵、北海王昕俱奉老母攜妻子，同赴青、齊。

translations.literal: Later, because troubles were widespread in all directions, he requested to be Eastern Campaign Military Affairs Officer in Qingzhou; together with Xing Shao of Hejian and Wang Xin of Beihai he supported their aged mothers and took their wives and children, all going together to Qing and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with turmoil spreading everywhere, he requested appointment as Eastern Campaign Military Affairs Officer in Qingzhou; together with Xing Shao of Hejian and Wang Xin of Beihai he brought their aged mothers and families and went together to Qing and Qi.

sentences.zh: 未幾而爾硃榮入洛，衣冠殲盡，物論以為知幾。

translations.literal: Before long Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and the gentry were wiped out; public opinion held that Hun had foreseen the times.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and the gentry were slaughtered; public opinion held that Hun had read the times correctly.

sentences.zh: 時河北流移人聚青土，眾逾二十萬，共劫河間邢杲為主，起自北海，襲東陽。

translations.literal: At that time displaced people from north of the Yellow River gathered in Qing territory, numbering more than two hundred thousand; they together seized Xing Gao of Hejian as their leader, rose from Beihai, and attacked Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time displaced people from north of the Yellow River gathered in Qing territory, numbering more than two hundred thousand; they seized Xing Gao of Hejian as their leader, rose in Beihai, and attacked Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 青州刺史元世俊欲謀誅之，府人遂猜貳。

translations.literal: The Governor of Qingzhou, Yuan Shijun, wished to plot their execution, and the staff of the prefecture became divided and suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: The Governor of Qingzhou, Yuan Shijun, wished to plot their destruction, and the prefectural staff became divided and suspicious.

sentences.zh: 渾乃與長史崔光韶具陳禍福，由是歃血而盟，上下還睦。

translations.literal: Hun then, with Chief Clerk Cui Guangshao, fully explained the blessings and disasters involved; thereby they drank blood and made alliance, and superiors and subordinates were harmonious again.
translations.idiomatic: Hun then, together with Chief Clerk Cui Guangshao, fully explained the risks and benefits; they drank blood and swore alliance, and harmony was restored between superiors and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，崔社客反於海岱，攻圍青州，詔渾為都官尚書、東北道行台，赴援。

translations.literal: In the Putai era Cui Sheke rebelled in the Hai-Dai region and besieged Qingzhou; an edict appointed Hun Minister of Justice and Northeast Route Mobile Headquarters to go to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the Putai era Cui Sheke rebelled in the Hai-Dai region and besieged Qingzhou; Hun was appointed Minister of Justice and commander of the Northeast Route Mobile Headquarters to go to the relief.

sentences.zh: 社客諸城各自固保，渾以社客賊之根本，烏合易離，若銜枚夜襲，便可禽殄。

translations.literal: Sheke's cities each held fast in defense; Hun held that Sheke was the root of the bandit force, that a mob gathered easily disperses, and that if they marched with gags by night and made a surprise attack, he could be captured and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheke's followers held their cities in defense; Hun argued that Sheke was the root of the rebel force, that a mob gathered easily disperses, and that a silent night attack would capture and destroy him.

sentences.zh: 如社客就禽，諸郡可傳檄而定。

translations.literal: If Sheke were captured, the various commanderies could be settled by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sheke was captured, the various commanderies could be brought to submission by proclamation alone.

sentences.zh: 諸將尚遲疑，渾乃決行。

translations.literal: The generals still hesitated, but Hun resolved to act.
translations.idiomatic: The generals still hesitated, but Hun resolved to march.

sentences.zh: 果禽社客，斬首送洛陽，海隅清定。

translations.literal: He did indeed capture Sheke, sent his head to Luoyang, and the coastal regions were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He duly captured Sheke, sent his head to Luoyang, and the coastal regions were pacified.

sentences.zh: 天平初，丁母憂，行喪塚側，殆將滅性。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianping era he entered mourning for his mother, observed mourning beside the tomb, and nearly destroyed his own life.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianping era he entered mourning for his mother, kept vigil beside the tomb, and nearly ruined his health in grief.

sentences.zh: 武定初，兼散騎常侍、聘梁使主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Wuding era he was additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and chief envoy on a mission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wuding era he was additionally appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and chief envoy on a mission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁武謂曰：「伯陽之後，久而彌盛，趙李人物，今實居多。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang said to him, "Descendants of Boyang—over time they grow ever more flourishing; men of talent from the Zhao Li clan truly predominate today."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang said to him, "Descendants of Laozi—the Zhao Li clan grows ever more flourishing with time, and men of talent from your house truly predominate today."

sentences.zh: 」使還，為東郡太守。

translations.literal: " When the mission returned, he was made Administrator of Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: " On his return he was appointed Administrator of Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 以贓賄征還。

translations.literal: For bribery and corruption he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled on charges of bribery and corruption.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王使武士提以入，置諸庭。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxiang of Qi had armed men seize and bring him in and set him in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang of Qi had armed men seize him and bring him into the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 渾抗言曰：「將軍今日猶自禮賢邪？

translations.literal: Hun spoke defiantly, saying, "Does my lord still treat worthy men with courtesy today?"
translations.idiomatic: Hun spoke out boldly: "Does my lord still treat men of talent with courtesy today?"

sentences.zh: 」文襄笑而舍之。

translations.literal: " Wenxiang laughed and released him.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng laughed and let him go.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，除太子少保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi he was appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era in Northern Qi he was appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時太常邢邵為少師，吏部尚書楊愔為少傅，論者榮之。

translations.literal: At the time Xing Shao of the Ministry of Ceremonies was Junior Preceptor and Yang Yin, Minister of Personnel, was Junior Tutor; commentators honored the arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xing Shao served as Junior Preceptor and Yang Yin, Minister of Personnel, as Junior Tutor; commentators regarded the arrangement as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 以參禪代儀注，賜爵涇陽縣男。

translations.literal: For participating in the ritual protocols of the dynastic transition he was granted the title Baron of Jingyang county.
translations.idiomatic: For participating in the ritual protocols of the dynastic transition he received the enfeoffment of Baron of Jingyang county.

sentences.zh: 文宣以魏《麟趾格》未精，詔渾與邢邵、崔甗、魏收、王昕、李伯倫等修撰。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan, because the Wei Linzhi Code was not refined, ordered Hun together with Xing Shao, Cui Yan, Wei Shou, Wang Xin, Li Bolun, and others to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Wei Linzhi Code was not yet refined, Emperor Wenxuan ordered Hun, together with Xing Shao, Cui Yan, Wei Shou, Wang Xin, Li Bolun, and others, to revise it.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂魏收曰：「雕蟲小技，我不如卿；

translations.literal: He once said to Wei Shou, "In petty literary craft I am not your equal."
translations.idiomatic: He once told Wei Shou, "In petty literary craft I am not your equal."

sentences.zh: 國典朝章，卿不如我。

translations.literal: In state codes and court regulations you are not my equal.
translations.idiomatic: In state codes and court regulations you are not my equal.

sentences.zh: 」尋除海州刺史。

translations.literal: " Soon he was appointed Governor of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was appointed Governor of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 后土人共圍州城，城中多石無井，常食海水，賊絕其路。

translations.literal: The local people together besieged the prefectural city; the city had much stone and no wells, and they regularly drank seawater; the bandits cut off their routes.
translations.idiomatic: The local people together besieged the prefectural city; the city was stony and had no wells, so the inhabitants regularly drank seawater, and the rebels cut off their supply routes.

sentences.zh: 城內先有一，夏旱涸竭，渾齋戒朝服而祈焉，一朝天雨，泉流湧溢。

translations.literal: In the city there had long been a well; in summer drought it dried up; Hun fasted, put on court dress, and prayed there; in one morning heaven rained, and springs gushed forth in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: The city had long had a well that dried up in the summer drought; Hun fasted, put on court dress, and prayed at it; rain fell within a single morning, and springs gushed forth in abundance.

sentences.zh: 賊以為神，應時駭散。

translations.literal: The bandits took it for a divine sign and at once fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took it for a divine sign and fled in terror at once.

sentences.zh: 渾捕斬渠帥，傳首鄴都。

translations.literal: Hun captured and beheaded the ringleaders and sent their heads to the capital at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Hun captured and beheaded the rebel leaders and sent their heads to the capital at Ye.

sentences.zh: 渾妾郭，在州幹政納貨，坐免，卒於鄴。

translations.literal: Hun's concubine Guo meddled in government and accepted bribes in the province; he was dismissed from office on that account and died at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's concubine Guo meddled in government and accepted bribes while he was in office; he was dismissed on that account and died at Ye.

sentences.zh: 子湛，字處元，涉獵文史，有家風。

translations.literal: His son Zhan, styled Chuyuan, ranged widely in letters and histories and had the family's style.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhan, styled Chuyuan, ranged widely in historical and literary writings and upheld the family tradition.

sentences.zh: 兼通直散騎常侍、聘陳使副，襲爵涇陽男。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and deputy envoy on a mission to Chen, and inherited the title Baron of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and deputy envoy on a mission to Chen, and inherited the title Baron of Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 渾與弟繪、緯俱為聘使主，湛又為使副，是以趙郡人士，目為四使。

translations.literal: Hun and his younger brothers Hui and Wei were all chief envoys on missions, and Zhan was again deputy envoy; therefore the people of Zhao commandery called them the Four Envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Hun and his younger brothers Hui and Wei had all served as chief envoys on diplomatic missions, and Zhan served as deputy envoy as well; people of Zhao commandery therefore called them the Four Envoys.

sentences.zh: 繪字敬文。

translations.literal: Hui, styled Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, styled Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 六歲便求入學，家人以偶年俗忌，不許，遂竊其姊筆牘用之。

translations.literal: At six he asked to enter school; his family, because of the taboo on even-numbered years, did not permit it, so he secretly took his elder sister's writing materials and used them.
translations.idiomatic: At six he asked to go to school; his family, citing the taboo on even-numbered years, refused, so he secretly took his elder sister's writing materials and used them.

sentences.zh: 未逾晦朔，遂通《急就章》，內外以為非常兒。

translations.literal: Before a month had passed he had mastered the Jijiuzhang; inside and outside the family they regarded him as an extraordinary child.
translations.idiomatic: Before a month had passed he had mastered the Jijiuzhang; family and outsiders alike regarded him as an extraordinary child.

sentences.zh: 及長，儀貌端偉，神情朗俊。

translations.literal: When he grew up, his bearing was dignified and imposing and his spirit bright and handsome.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, his bearing was dignified and imposing and his expression bright and handsome.

sentences.zh: 第五舅河間邢晏每與言，歎其高遠，曰：「若披煙霧，如對珠玉，宅相之寄，良在此甥。

translations.literal: His fifth maternal uncle Xing Yan of Hejian, whenever he spoke with him, sighed at his lofty reach and said, "It is like parting the mist and facing pearls and jade—the hope of the clan's dwelling truly rests in this nephew."
translations.idiomatic: His fifth maternal uncle Xing Yan of Hejian, whenever he spoke with him, marveled at his lofty spirit and said, "It is like parting the mist to face pearls and jade—the hope of our clan truly rests in this nephew."

sentences.zh: 」後敕撰五禮，繪與太原王乂同掌軍禮。

translations.literal: " Later, when the Five Rites were ordered compiled, Hui together with Wang Yi of Taiyuan jointly supervised military ritual.
translations.idiomatic: " Later, when the court ordered the compilation of the Five Rites, Hui and Wang Yi of Taiyuan jointly supervised military ritual.

sentences.zh: 魏靜帝於顯揚殿講《孝經》、《禮記》，繪與從弟褰、裴伯茂魏收、盧元明等俱為錄議，簡舉可觀。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites in the Xianyang Hall; Hui together with his cousin Qian, Pei Boma, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others all served as recorders and commentators, selecting what was worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Wei lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites in the Xianyang Hall; Hui, together with his cousin Qian, Pei Boma, Wei Shou, Lu Yuanming, and others, served as recorders and commentators and selected the passages worth noting.

sentences.zh: 曆中書侍郎、丞相司馬。

translations.literal: In succession Vice Director of the Secretariat, Chief Clerk of the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to vice director of the Secretariat and chief clerk of the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 每霸朝文武總集，對揚王庭，常令繪先發言端，為群僚之首。

translations.literal: Whenever the hegemonic court gathered civil and military officials to respond before the royal court, Hui was always made to open the discussion and stood first among the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the ruling court gathered civil and military officials for audience, Hui was always asked to open the discussion and stood first among the officials.

sentences.zh: 音祠辯正，風儀都雅，聽者悚然，文襄益加敬異。

translations.literal: His voice in ritual address was clear and correct, his bearing refined and elegant; listeners were awed, and Wenxiang treated him with still greater respect and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: His voice in ritual address was clear and correct, his bearing refined and elegant; listeners were awed, and Gao Cheng treated him with still greater respect and admiration.

sentences.zh: 又掌儀注。

translations.literal: He also supervised ritual protocols.
translations.idiomatic: He also supervised ritual protocols.

sentences.zh: 武定初，兼散騎常侍，為聘使主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was additionally made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and chief envoy on a mission.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wuding era he was additionally appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and chief envoy on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 梁武問高相今在何處？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang asked where Chancellor Gao was now.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang asked where Chancellor Gao was now.

sentences.zh: 黑獺若為形容？

translations.literal: What is Black Badger's appearance like?
translations.idiomatic: What does Black Badger look like?

sentences.zh: 高相作何經略？

translations.literal: What strategy is Chancellor Gao pursuing?
translations.idiomatic: What strategy is Chancellor Gao pursuing?

sentences.zh: 繪敷對明辯，梁武稱佳。

translations.literal: Hui responded expansively with clear argument; Emperor Wu of Liang praised him as excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Hui answered expansively and with clear argument; Emperor Wu of Liang praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 與梁人泛言氏族，袁狎曰：「未若我本出自黃帝，姓在十四之限。

translations.literal: When speaking generally with the men of Liang about clans and surnames, Yuan Xia said, "It is not like my own origin from the Yellow Emperor, whose surname falls within the fourteen surnames."
translations.idiomatic: When speaking generally with the men of Liang about clans and surnames, Yuan Xia said, "My own line descends from the Yellow Emperor, whose surname falls among the fourteen great surnames."

sentences.zh: 」繪曰：「兄所出雖遠，當共車千秋分一字耳！

translations.literal: " Hui said, "Though your origin is remote, we should share one character with Che Qianqiu!"
translations.idiomatic: " Hui said, "Remote though your origin may be, we should still share one character with Che Qianqiu!"

sentences.zh: 」一坐皆笑。

translations.literal: " The whole company laughed.
translations.idiomatic: " The whole company burst out laughing.

sentences.zh: 前後行人皆通啟求市，繪獨守清尚，梁人重其廉潔。

translations.literal: Envoys before and after all sent notices requesting trade; Hui alone upheld pure integrity, and the people of Liang esteemed his incorruptibility.
translations.idiomatic: Every envoy before and after him traded on official notice, but Hui alone kept his integrity unsullied—and the Liang court respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜高陽內史。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was appointed Inner Scribe of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Inner Scribe of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 郡境舊有三猛獸，人常患之。

translations.literal: Within the commandery there had long been three fierce beasts, which the people constantly feared.
translations.idiomatic: Within the commandery there had long been three fierce beasts that the people constantly feared.

sentences.zh: 繪欲修檻，遂因鬥俱死於郡西。

translations.literal: Hui wished to build cages for them, but they fought each other and all died west of the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: Hui wished to build cages for them, but the beasts fought each other and all died west of the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 咸以為化感所致，皆勸申上。

translations.literal: All held that this was caused by transforming influence and urged him to report it upward.
translations.idiomatic: All held that this was the result of his transforming influence and urged him to report it to the court.

sentences.zh: 繪曰：「猛獸因鬥而斃，自是偶然，貪此為功，人將窺我。

translations.literal: Hui said, "The fierce beasts died from fighting each other—that was mere chance; if I greedily make this my achievement, people will spy on me."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "The beasts died from fighting each other—that was mere chance; if I greedily claim this as my achievement, people will see through me."

sentences.zh: 」竟不聽。

translations.literal: " In the end he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he would not agree.

sentences.zh: 高陽舊多陂澱，繪至後，澱水皆涸，乃置農正，專主勸課，墾田倍增，家給人足。

translations.literal: Gaoyang had long had many marshes and ponds; after Hui arrived the pond waters all dried up; he then appointed an agricultural supervisor to devote himself to encouraging cultivation, and reclaimed fields doubled; households had enough and the people were provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyang had long had many marshes and ponds; after Hui arrived the waters all dried up; he appointed an agricultural supervisor to encourage cultivation, reclaimed fields doubled, and households became self-sufficient.

sentences.zh: 瀛州三郡人俱詣州，請為繪立碑於郡街。

translations.literal: The people of three commanderies in Yingzhou all went to the prefecture and requested that a stele be erected for Hui in the commandery streets.
translations.idiomatic: The people of three commanderies in Yingzhou all went to the prefectural seat and requested that a stele be erected for Hui in the commandery streets.

sentences.zh: 神武東巡郡國，在瀛州城西駐馬久立，使郎中陳元康喻慰之。

translations.literal: Shenwu toured the commanderies eastward; west of Yingzhou city he halted his horse and stood long, sending Gentleman Chen Yuankang to explain and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan toured the eastern commanderies; west of Yingzhou city he halted his horse and stood for a long while, sending Gentleman Chen Yuankang to explain and comfort the people.

sentences.zh: 河間太守崔諶，恃其弟暹勢，從繪乞麋角鴿羽。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Hejian, Cui Chen, relying on his younger brother Xian's power, asked Hui for elk horns and pigeon feathers.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator of Hejian, Cui Chen, relying on his younger brother Xian's influence, asked Hui for elk horns and pigeon feathers.

sentences.zh: 繪答書曰：「鴿有六翮，飛則沖天；

translations.literal: Hui replied in a letter: "The pigeon has six pinions—when it flies it pierces heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Hui wrote back: "A pigeon has six feathers; when it takes wing, it shoots straight into the sky."

sentences.zh: 麋有四足，走便入海。

translations.literal: The elk has four legs—when it runs it goes straight into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: The elk has four legs—when it runs it goes straight into the sea.

sentences.zh: 下官膚體疏懶，手足遲鈍，不能近追飛走，遠事佞人。

translations.literal: This inferior official's body is slack and lazy, his hands and feet slow and dull; I cannot closely pursue what flies and runs, nor serve flatterers from afar.
translations.idiomatic: This humble official's body is slack and lazy, his hands and feet slow and dull; I cannot chase what flies and runs, nor serve flatterers from afar.

sentences.zh: 」時文襄使暹選司徒左長史，暹薦繪，既而不果，咸謂由此書。

translations.literal: " At the time Wenxiang had Xian select the Left Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end it did not come about, and all said it was because of this letter.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Gao Cheng had Xian select the Left Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses; Xian recommended Hui, but in the end the appointment did not come about, and all said it was because of this letter.

sentences.zh: 及文襄嗣業，普代山東諸郡，其特降書征者，唯繪與清河太守辛術二人而已。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded to the enterprise, he replaced the administrators of the eastern commanderies universally; those specially summoned by edict were only Hui and Xin Shu, Administrator of Qinghe, two men alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded to power, he replaced the administrators of the eastern commanderies throughout the region; those specially summoned by imperial edict were only Hui and Xin Shu, Administrator of Qinghe—two men alone.

sentences.zh: 至，補大將軍從事中郎，遷司馬。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was appointed Attendant of the Grand General and was transferred to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival he was appointed Attendant of the Grand General and was promoted to Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 文襄以前司徒侯景進賢冠賜繪曰：「卿但直心事孤，當用卿為三公，莫學侯景叛也。

translations.literal: Wenxiang bestowed on Hui the Cap of Advancing Worth formerly worn by the former Minister over the Masses Hou Jing, saying, "You need only serve me with a straight heart—I shall use you as one of the Three Dukes; do not learn from Hou Jing's rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng bestowed on Hui the Cap of Advancing Worth formerly worn by the former Minister over the Masses Hou Jing, saying, "Serve me with a straight heart and I shall make you one of the Three Dukes—do not follow Hou Jing's example of rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」及文宣嗣事，仍為丞相司馬。

translations.literal: " When Wenxuan succeeded to the enterprise, he remained Chief Clerk of the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Wenxuan succeeded to power, he remained Chief Clerk of the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除司徒右長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he was appointed Right Chief Clerk of the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 繪質性方重，未嘗趣事權門，以此久而沈屈。

translations.literal: Hui's nature was upright and grave; he never sought favor with powerful families, and for this reason remained long in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was upright and grave by nature; he never curried favor with powerful families, and for this reason remained long in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南青州刺史，諡曰景。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously appointed Governor of Southern Qing province, with the posthumous epithet Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Governor of Southern Qing province, with the posthumous epithet Jing.

sentences.zh: 子君道，有父風。

translations.literal: His son Jundao possessed his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jundao possessed his father's character.

sentences.zh: 繪弟緯，字乾經，少聰慧，有才學。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Wei, styled Ganqing, from youth clever and possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wei, styled Ganqing, was bright from childhood and gifted in letters.

sentences.zh: 與舅子河間邢昕少相倫輩，晚不逮之。

translations.literal: In youth he was regarded as a peer of his maternal nephew Xing Xin of Hejian, but in later years he did not match him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was regarded as a peer of his maternal nephew Xing Xin of Hejian, but in later years he did not measure up to him.

sentences.zh: 位中散大夫。

translations.literal: He rose to Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 聘梁使主、侍中李神俊舉緯尚書南主客郎。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun, chief envoy receiving Liang embassies and Palace Attendant, recommended Wei as Director of Southern Reception in the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun, chief envoy receiving Liang embassies and Palace Attendant, recommended Wei for the post of Director of Southern Reception in the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 緯前後接對凡十八人，頗為稱職。

translations.literal: Wei received and answered envoys in all eighteen cases, and performed the duty quite competently.
translations.idiomatic: Wei received and answered envoys on eighteen occasions in all, and performed the duty quite competently.

sentences.zh: 鄴下為之語曰：「學則渾、繪、緯，口則繪、緯、渾。

translations.literal: At Ye a saying circulated: "For learning there are Hun, Hui, and Wei; for speech there are Hui, Wei, and Hun."
translations.idiomatic: At Ye people said: "For scholarship, Hun, Hui, and Wei; for eloquence, Hui, Wei, and Hun."

sentences.zh: 」齊文襄攝選，以緯為司徒諮議參軍，謂曰：「自郎署至此，所謂不次，以卿人才，故有此舉耳。

translations.literal: " When Gao Cheng of Qi took charge of selections, he appointed Wei Staff Officer for Consultation in the Ministry over the Masses and said to him, "From the bureau to this post is what is called an exceptional promotion—it is because of your talent that this appointment was made."
translations.idiomatic: " When Gao Cheng of Qi took charge of official selections, he appointed Wei Staff Officer for Consultation in the Ministry over the Masses and told him, "From the bureau to this post is what is called an exceptional promotion—it is because of your talent that this appointment was made."

sentences.zh: 」梁謝蘭來聘，勞之。

translations.literal: " When Xie Lan of Liang came on an embassy, Wei was assigned to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xie Lan of Liang came on an embassy, Wei was assigned to receive him.

sentences.zh: 蘭問安平諸崔，緯曰：「子玉以還，雕龍絕矣。

translations.literal: Lan asked about the Cui clan of Anping; Wei said, "Since Ziyu, the art of the carved dragon has perished."
translations.idiomatic: Lan asked about the Cui clan of Anping; Wei said, "Since Ziyu, literary brilliance has died out."

sentences.zh: 」崔暹聞之怒。

translations.literal: " When Cui Xian heard this he was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: " When Cui Xian heard this he was enraged.

sentences.zh: 緯詣門謝之，暹上馬不顧。

translations.literal: Wei went to his gate to apologize, but Xian mounted his horse and paid him no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Wei went to his gate to apologize, but Xian mounted his horse and ignored him.

sentences.zh: 緯語人曰：「雖失要人意，聘梁使不得舍我。

translations.literal: Wei told others: "Though I have lost an important man's favor, the chief envoy receiving Liang cannot do without me."
translations.idiomatic: Wei remarked to others that although he had fallen from a patron's grace, no chief envoy to Liang could afford to leave him behind.

sentences.zh: 」武定五年，兼散騎常侍，使梁。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year of Wuding he served concurrently as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and was sent as envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year of Wuding he served concurrently as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and was sent as envoy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 緯常逸游放達，自號「隱君」，蕭然有絕塵之意。

translations.literal: Wei often wandered freely unrestrained, styled himself "Recluse Lord," had an air of transcending the dust of the world.
translations.idiomatic: Wei lived freely and without restraint, called himself the Recluse Lord, and carried himself as one who had left the world behind.

sentences.zh: 使還，除太子家令，卒。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he was appointed Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 齊初，贈北徐州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was posthumously appointed Governor of Northern Xu province, with the posthumous epithet Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Northern Qi he was posthumously made Governor of Northern Xu province, with the posthumous epithet Wen.

sentences.zh: 璨字世顯，靈弟趙郡太守均之子也。

translations.literal: Can, styled Shixian, was son of Jun, Administrator of Zhao commandery, younger brother of Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Can, styled Shixian, was the son of Jun, administrator of Zhao commandery and younger brother of Ling.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺五寸，容貌魁偉。

translations.literal: Body eight feet five inches, appearance towering and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet five inches tall, with a towering and imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 受學于梁祚，位中書郎，雅為高允所知。

translations.literal: Received learning from Liang Zuo, rose to Secretariat Gentleman, was well known to Gao Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liang Zuo, became a secretariat gentleman, and won the esteem of Gao Yun.

sentences.zh: 天安初，宋徐州刺史薛安都舉彭城降，詔鎮南大將軍博陵公尉元、鎮東將軍城陽公孔伯恭等迎之，獻文復以璨參二府軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an, Xue Andu, Governor of Xu province in Song, offered Pengcheng in surrender; an edict ordered Grand General Who Guards the South, Duke of Boling Wei Yuan, Grand General Who Guards the East, Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong, and others to welcome him, and Emperor Xianwen again had Can serve on the staffs of both commands.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tian'an era, Xue Andu, Governor of Xu province in Liu Song, offered Pengcheng in surrender; the court ordered Grand General Who Guards the South, Duke of Boling Wei Yuan, Grand General Who Guards the East, Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong, and others to welcome him, and Emperor Xianwen again had Can serve on the staffs of both commands.

sentences.zh: 安都率文武出迎，元不加禮接，安都還城，遂不降。

translations.literal: Andu led civil and military officials out to welcome them, but Yuan did not receive him with courtesy; Andu returned to the city and thereupon did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Andu led civil and military officials out to welcome them, but Yuan did not receive him with courtesy; Andu returned to the city and thereupon refused to surrender.

sentences.zh: 宋將張永、沈攸之等先屯下磕，元令璨與中書郎高閭入彭城說安都，即與俱載赴軍。

translations.literal: Song generals Zhang Yong, Shen Youzhi, and others first encamped at Xiake; Yuan ordered Can and Secretariat Gentleman Gao Lu to enter Pengcheng and persuade Andu; Andu at once rode out with them to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Song generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi had encamped at Xiake. Yuan sent Can and the secretariat gentleman Gao Lu into Pengcheng to win over Andu, who immediately rode out with them to join the army.

sentences.zh: 元等入城，收管籥。

translations.literal: Yuan and the others entered the city and took control of the keys and seals.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and the others entered the city and took control of the keys and seals.

sentences.zh: 其夜，永攻南門，不克退還。

translations.literal: That night Yong attacked south gate, could not take it, withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yong assaulted the south gate, failed to breach it, and fell back.

sentences.zh: 璨勸元乘永，永失據，攻永米船，大破之，於是遂定淮北。

translations.literal: Can urged Yuan to strike while Yong was off balance; Yong lost his footing, and they attacked Yong's grain boats and routed them thoroughly, thereby securing the north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Can urged Yuan to strike while Yong was vulnerable; Yong lost his footing, they attacked Yong's grain boats and routed them thoroughly, and thereby secured the north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 加璨甯朔將軍，與張讜對為兗州刺史，安帖初附。

translations.literal: Can was promoted General Who Pacifies the North, paired with Zhang Tan as Governors of Yan province, settled the newly attached.
translations.idiomatic: Can was made General Who Pacifies the North and, together with Zhang Tan, governed Yan province, calming the newly submitted population.

sentences.zh: 以參定徐州功，賜爵始豐侯，卒，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: For his merit in securing Xu province he was granted the title Marquis of Shifeng; at his death he received the posthumous epithet Yi.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in securing Xu province he received the enfeoffment of Marquis of Shifeng; at his death he received the posthumous epithet Yi.

sentences.zh: 子元茂襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yuanmao inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanmao inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 元茂以寬雅著稱，位司徒司馬、彭城鎮副將，人吏安之。

translations.literal: Yuanmao was renowned for generous refined character; rose to Chief Clerk of Minister over the Masses, Deputy General of Pengcheng garrison; people and officials found peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmao was known for his generous and refined manner. As chief clerk of the Minister over the Masses and deputy general of the Pengcheng garrison, he kept officials and commoners alike at ease.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈顯武將軍、徐州刺史，諡曰順。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously appointed General of Manifest Martiality and Governor of Xu province, with the posthumous epithet Shun.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made General of Manifest Martiality and Governor of Xu province, with the posthumous epithet Shun.

sentences.zh: 子秀之，字鳳起，襲爵，位尚書都官郎。

translations.literal: Son Xiuzhi, styled Fengqi, inherited title, rose to Director in Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiuzhi, styled Fengqi, inherited the title and served as director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 秀之弟子雲，字鳳升；

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's younger brother Yun, styled Fengsheng;
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's younger brother Yun, styled Fengsheng;

sentences.zh: 子雲弟子羽，字鳳降；

translations.literal: Yun's younger brother Yu, styled Fengjiang;
translations.idiomatic: Yun's younger brother Yu, styled Fengjiang;

sentences.zh: 子羽弟子岳，字鳳歭。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Yue, styled Fengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Yue, styled Fengzhi.

sentences.zh: 秀之等並早孤，事母孝謹，兄弟容貌並魁偉，風度審正，而皆早卒。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi and the others all lost their fathers early, served their mother with filial care, were alike in towering appearance and dignified bearing, yet all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi and the others all lost their fathers early, served their mother with filial devotion, were alike in towering appearance and dignified bearing, yet all died young.

sentences.zh: 鳳升子道宗，位直閣將軍。

translations.literal: Fengsheng's son Daozong rose to General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong, son of Fengsheng, became general of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 道宗弟德林，司徒中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Daozong's younger brother Delin, Staff Officer for Central Troops in Ministry over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Delin, Daozong's younger brother, served as staff officer for central troops under the Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 元茂弟宣茂，太和初，拜中書博士，後兼定州大中正，受鄉人財貨，為御史所劾，除名。

translations.literal: Yuanmao's younger brother Xuanmao, at the beginning of Taihe, was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat; later, while serving concurrently as Chief Rectifier of Ding province, he accepted goods from fellow townsmen, was impeached by the censorate, and was removed from the register.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanmao's younger brother Xuanmao, at the beginning of the Taihe era, was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat; later, while serving concurrently as Chief Rectifier of Ding province, he accepted goods from fellow townsmen, was impeached by the censorate, and was struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 正始初，除太中大夫，遷光祿勳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengshi he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel and was transferred to Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengshi era he was appointed Grand Master of Palace Counsel and was promoted to Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 與遊肇往復，肇善之。

translations.literal: He exchanged letters with You Zhao, and Zhao thought well of him.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged letters with You Zhao, and Zhao thought well of him.

sentences.zh: 卒于幽州刺史，遺令薄葬，贈齊州刺史，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: He died in office as Governor of You province, left instructions for a simple burial, was posthumously appointed Governor of Qi province, and received the posthumous epithet Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Governor of You province, left instructions for a simple burial, was posthumously made Governor of Qi province, and received the posthumous epithet Hui.

sentences.zh: 子籍之，字脩遠，性謹正，粗涉書史。

translations.literal: Son Jizhi, styled Xiuyuan, nature conscientious upright, roughly acquainted with books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jizhi, styled Xiuyuan, was careful and upright by nature and had some knowledge of history and the classics.

sentences.zh: 位司徒諮議參軍、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Rose to Staff Officer for Consultation in Ministry over the Masses, Grand Master of Palace Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to consultation staff officer under the Minister over the Masses and grand master of palace enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 著《忠誥》一篇，文多不載。

translations.literal: Composed one piece "Loyal Admonition"; most of the text is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a work entitled Loyal Admonition, though most of it is no longer preserved.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈定州刺史。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously appointed Governor of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Governor of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 子徹，仕齊，位尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His son Che served Qi and rose to Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Che served Northern Qi and rose to Vice Director of the Left in the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 徹子純，隋開皇中為介州長史。
