translations.literal: Che's son Chun, in Sui Kaihuang era served as Chief Administrator of Jie province.
translations.idiomatic: Che's son Chun served under the Sui during the Kaihuang era as chief administrator of Jie province.

sentences.zh: 純子德饒，字世文。

translations.literal: Chun's son Derao, styled Shiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's son Derao, styled Shiwen.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏好學，有至性。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever, fond of learning, and possessed the utmost sincerity of nature.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was clever, fond of learning, and possessed the utmost sincerity of nature.

sentences.zh: 弱冠仕隋為校書郎，仍直內史省，參掌文翰。

translations.literal: At capping entered Sui service as Collator, assigned to Secretariat, took part in managing documents.
translations.idiomatic: After his capping he entered Sui service as collator, was posted to the Secretariat, and helped manage official papers.

sentences.zh: 轉監察御史，糾正不避權貴。

translations.literal: Transferred to Investigating Censor; in correcting abuses did not shrink from powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to investigating censor and, when exposing wrongdoing, did not flinch before the powerful.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，遷司隸從事。

translations.literal: Daye third year, promoted to Attendant of Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye he was promoted to attendant of the metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 每巡四方，理冤枉，褒孝悌。

translations.literal: Whenever he toured the four quarters he redressed wrongful convictions and praised filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: On his tours through the realm he overturned unjust verdicts and commended those who showed filial piety and brotherly duty.

sentences.zh: 雖位秩未通，德行為當時所重。

translations.literal: Though rank not yet high, conduct and virtue were heavily regarded in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Although his office was still modest, men of the time held his character in high regard.

sentences.zh: 凡與交結，皆海內髦彥。

translations.literal: All with whom he formed friendships were leading talents from across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone he befriended was a leading figure among the realm's finest minds.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，父母寢疾，輒終日不食，十旬不解衣。

translations.literal: Nature supremely filial; when parents lay ill he would go all day without eating and for ten ten-day periods not remove his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: He was profoundly filial. When his parents fell ill he would fast all day and for a hundred days never undress to sleep.

sentences.zh: 及丁憂，水漿不入口五日；

translations.literal: When he entered mourning he took neither water nor food for five days;
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he took neither food nor water for five days;

sentences.zh: 哀慟，歐血數升。

translations.literal: grieving in anguish, he vomited several sheng of blood.
translations.idiomatic: grieving in anguish, he vomited several sheng of blood.

sentences.zh: 及送葬，會仲冬積雪，行四十餘里，單縗徒跣，號踴幾絕。

translations.literal: When going to burial, it happened midwinter deep snow; walked more than forty li in plain hemp mourning clothes barefoot, wailing and leaping nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial, in midwinter snow, he walked more than forty li in plain hemp and barefoot, wailing and beating his breast until he nearly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 會葬者千餘人，莫不為之流涕。

translations.literal: Those attending burial more than a thousand; none failed to weep for him.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand mourners attended, and every one of them wept.

sentences.zh: 後甘露降於庭樹，有鳩巢其廬，納言楊達巡省河北，詣廬吊慰之，因改所居村名為孝敬村，裏為和順裏。

translations.literal: Later sweet dew descended on courtyard trees; a dove nested on his hut; Director of the Secretariat Yang Da on inspection tour of Hebei came to hut to offer condolences and comfort, and thereby changed the village where he dwelt to Xiaojing Village and the lane to Heshun Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Later sweet dew fell on the trees in his courtyard and doves nested on his cottage. Yang Da, Director of the Secretariat, was touring Hebei when he came to offer condolence; he renamed the village Filial Respect and the lane Harmonious Compliance.

sentences.zh: 後為金河縣長，未之官，屬群盜蜂起，賊帥格謙、孫宣雅等十餘頭聚眾於勃海，有敕許其歸首。

translations.literal: Later appointed Magistrate of Jinhe county; before taking office bandits swarmed everywhere; bandit chiefs Ge Qian, Sun Xuanya, and more than ten others gathered followers at Bohai; an edict granted them permission to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed magistrate of Jinhe but had not yet taken up the post when bandits rose everywhere. More than a dozen chiefs, including Ge Qian and Sun Xuanya, gathered forces in Bohai until an edict offered them amnesty if they surrendered.

sentences.zh: 謙等懼，不敢降，以德饒信行有聞，遣奏曰：「若德饒來者，即相率歸首。

translations.literal: Qian and the others feared and did not dare surrender; because Derao's trustworthiness and conduct were renowned, they sent a memorial saying: "If Derao comes, we shall all follow one another in surrendering."
translations.idiomatic: Qian and his fellows were afraid to yield. Knowing Derao's reputation for integrity, they sent a memorial: "If Derao comes, we will surrender together."

sentences.zh: 」帝遣德饒往勃海慰諸賊。

translations.literal: " The emperor sent Derao to Bohai to reassure the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent Derao to Bohai to reassure the bandits.

sentences.zh: 至冠氏，會他賊攻陷縣城，見害。

translations.literal: Reached Guanshi; other bandits happened to attack and take county seat; he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Guanshi, other bandits happened to storm the county seat, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 其弟德佋，性重然諾。

translations.literal: His younger brother Deyu was by nature strict in keeping his word.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Deyu was by nature strict in keeping his word.

sentences.zh: 大業末為離石郡司法書佐，太守楊子崇特禮之。

translations.literal: At end of Daye era served as Judicial Clerk of Lishi commandery; Administrator Yang Zichong treated him with special courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye era he served as judicial clerk of Lishi commandery, where Administrator Yang Zichong treated him with marked respect.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，子崇遇害，棄屍城下。

translations.literal: When righteous armies rose, Zichong was killed; corpse abandoned below city wall.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous armies rose, Zichong was killed and his body left below the city wall.

sentences.zh: 德佋赴哭盡哀，收瘞之。

translations.literal: Deyu went to mourn with full grief, gathered body and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu went to mourn him with full grief, recovered the body, and buried it.

sentences.zh: 至介休，詣義師請葬子崇。

translations.literal: Reached Jiexiu, sought righteous army to request proper burial for Zichong.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Jiexiu and asked the righteous army to grant Zichong a proper burial.

sentences.zh: 見許，因贈子崇官，令德佋為使者，往離石禮葬子崇。

translations.literal: Request granted; Zichong posthumously granted office; Deyu made envoy and sent to Lishi to perform rites and bury Zichong.
translations.idiomatic: His request was granted. Zichong was posthumously given an office, and Deyu was made envoy to Lishi to bury him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 徹弟公緒。

translations.literal: Che's younger brother Gongxu.
translations.idiomatic: Che's younger brother Gongxu.

sentences.zh: 公緒字穆叔，性聰敏，博通經傳。

translations.literal: Gongxu, styled Mushu, nature clever and keen, thoroughly versed in classics and commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxu, styled Mushu, was quick-witted by nature and deeply learned in the classics and their commentaries.

sentences.zh: 魏末為冀州司馬，屬疾去官，絕跡贊皇山。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he served as Chief Administrator of Ji province; when illness struck he left office and vanished into Mount Zanhuang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Northern Wei he served as Chief Administrator of Ji province; when illness struck he left office and vanished into Mount Zanhuang.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，以侍御史征，不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao in Qi he was summoned as Attendant Censor but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era in Northern Qi he was summoned as Attendant Censor but did not accept.

sentences.zh: 公緒沈冥樂道，又不閒時務，故誓心不仕。

translations.literal: Gongxu was reclusive, delighted in the Way, unskilled in affairs of the age; therefore vowed heart not to serve in office.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxu lived in seclusion, devoted to the Way and indifferent to public affairs, and vowed never to take office.

sentences.zh: 尤明天文，善圖緯之學，嘗謂子弟曰：「吾觀齊之分野，福德不多，國家祚終四七。

translations.literal: Especially bright in astronomy, skilled in chart-and-weft lore; once told sons and younger relatives: "I observe Qi's allotted territory—fortune and virtue not much; the state's reign will end at four times seven."
translations.idiomatic: He was especially versed in astronomy and the lore of prognostic charts. Once he told his sons and nephews: "I see little fortune left in Qi's allotted stars—the dynasty will not outlast twenty-eight years."

sentences.zh: 」及齊亡歲，距天保之元二十八年矣。

translations.literal: " In the year Qi perished, twenty-eight years had passed since the first year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: " In the year Northern Qi fell, twenty-eight years had passed since the first year of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 公緒雅好著書，撰《典言》十卷、《禮質疑》五卷、《喪服章句》一卷、《古今略記》二十卷、《玄子》五卷、《趙記》八卷、《趙語》十二卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: Gongxu by nature loved composing books; wrote "Dianyan" ten juan, "Li zhiyi" five juan, "Sangfu zhangju" one juan, "Gujin lueji" twenty juan, "Xuanzi" five juan, "Zhaoji" eight juan, "Zhaoyu" twelve juan—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxu loved to write. He produced ten scrolls of Canonical Sayings, five of Ritual Doubts, one of Mourning-Garment Commentary, twenty of Brief Records Past and Present, five of Master Xuan, eight of Records of Zhao, and twelve of Sayings of Zhao—all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 公緒既善陰陽之術，有秘記，傳之子孫而不好焉，臨終取以投火。

translations.literal: Since Gongxu was skilled in yin-yang arts and possessed a secret record, which he transmitted to sons and grandsons though they did not care for it, on deathbed he took it and cast into fire.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in yin-yang arts, he kept a secret manual and passed it to his descendants, though they had no taste for it; on his deathbed he threw it into the fire.

sentences.zh: 子少通，有學行。

translations.literal: His son Shaotong possessed learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaotong possessed learning and conduct.

sentences.zh: 公緒弟概，字季節，少好學。

translations.literal: Gongxu's younger brother Gai, styled Jijie, from youth loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Gai, styled Jijie, loved learning from childhood.

sentences.zh: 然性倨傲，每對諸兄弟，露髻披服，略無少長之禮。

translations.literal: Yet nature haughty; whenever facing brothers bared topknot and let clothes hang loose, utterly without elder-younger courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was proud by nature. Before his brothers he would bare his topknot and let his clothes hang loose, showing no regard for seniority.

sentences.zh: 為齊文襄大將軍府行參軍，進側集，題云「富春公主撰」。

translations.literal: Served as Acting Staff Officer in Gao Cheng's Grand General headquarters; for collection presented to heir inscribed title "Composed by Princess of Fuchun."
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting staff officer in Gao Cheng's grand general's headquarters and, for a collection presented to the heir, credited it to the Princess of Fuchun.

sentences.zh: 閑緩不任事，每被譏訶。

translations.literal: Leisurely and lax, unfit for duty; often ridiculed and reproached.
translations.idiomatic: Idle and careless, he was unfit for office and was often mocked for it.

sentences.zh: 除殿中侍御史，修國史。

translations.literal: Appointed Attendant Censor Within the Palace, worked on national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant censor within the palace and worked on the national history.

sentences.zh: 後為太子舍人，為副使聘於江南。

translations.literal: Later Attendant of Heir Apparent, went as deputy envoy on embassy to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as attendant to the heir apparent and went as deputy envoy on a mission to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 江南多以僧寺停客，出入常袒露。

translations.literal: In Jiangnan guests often lodged in Buddhist temples; he commonly went in and out with chest bare.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan travelers were often put up in Buddhist temples, and he commonly walked about with his chest bare.

sentences.zh: 還，坐事解。

translations.literal: On his return he was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was dismissed on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 後卒于并州功曹參軍。

translations.literal: Later he died in office as Staff Officer for Merit in Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died in office as Staff Officer for Merit in Bing province.

sentences.zh: 撰《戰國春秋》及《音譜》並行於世。

translations.literal: Composed "Spring and Autumn of the Warring States" and "Manual of Tones"—both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Spring and Autumn of the Warring States and Manual of Tones, both of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 又自簡詩賦二十四首，謂之《達生丈人集》。

translations.literal: Also selected twenty-four poems and rhapsodies of his own and called the collection "Collected Works of the Reached-Life Elder."
translations.idiomatic: He also chose twenty-four of his own poems and rhapsodies and published them as Collected Works of the Reached-Life Elder.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：「達生丈人者，生於戰國之世，爵裏姓名無聞焉爾，時人揆其行己，強為之號。

translations.literal: Its preface says: "Reached-Life Elder was born in age of Warring States; rank, home, and name unknown—people of the time inferred his conduct and forced a title upon him."
translations.idiomatic: Its preface reads: "The Reached-Life Elder lived in the Warring States era. His rank, home, and name are lost; contemporaries judged his conduct and bestowed the title upon him."

sentences.zh: 頗好屬文，成輒棄槁。

translations.literal: He was rather fond of composing literary pieces, but whenever he finished one he discarded the draft.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather fond of composing literary pieces, but whenever he finished one he discarded the draft.

sentences.zh: 常持論文云：古人有言，性情生於欲。

translations.literal: He often maintained in discussing literature: "Ancients had a saying—nature and feeling are born from desire."
translations.idiomatic: He often argued in literary discussion that, as the ancients said, temperament and emotion arise from desire.

sentences.zh: 又曰人之性靜，欲實汨之。

translations.literal: Also said human nature is tranquil, but desire truly muddies it.
translations.idiomatic: He also held that human nature is calm, but desire truly defiles it.

sentences.zh: 然則性也者，所受於天，神識是也，故為形骸之主；

translations.literal: Thus then nature is what is received from Heaven—it is spirit-consciousness, and therefore is master of the bodily form;
translations.idiomatic: Nature, then, is what one receives from Heaven—it is the spirit and consciousness, and therefore the master of the bodily frame.

sentences.zh: 情也者所受於性，嗜欲是也，故為形骸之役。

translations.literal: Feeling is what is received from nature—it is appetite and desire, and therefore is servant of the bodily form.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling is what one receives from nature—it is appetite and desire, and therefore the servant of the bodily frame.

sentences.zh: 由此言之，情性之辯，斷焉殊異。

translations.literal: From this speaking, the distinction between feeling and nature is decisively different.
translations.idiomatic: Spoken from this standpoint, the distinction between feeling and nature is decisively clear.

sentences.zh: 故其身泰，則均齊死生，塵垢名利，縱酒恣色，所以養情；

translations.literal: Therefore when the body is at ease, then treating life and death equally, brushing off fame and profit like dust, indulging in wine and freely enjoying beauty—these are means of nourishing feeling;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when the body is at ease, one treats life and death as equal, brushes off fame and profit like dust, and indulges freely in wine and sensual pleasure—this is how one nourishes feeling.

sentences.zh: 否，則屏除愛著，擯落枝體，收神反聽，所以養識。

translations.literal: If not, then casting aside attachment, stripping away the limbs, gathering the spirit and turning inward in listening—these are means of nourishing consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise one casts aside attachment, strips away concern for the limbs, gathers the spirit, and turns inward in listening—this is how one nourishes consciousness.

sentences.zh: 是以遇榮樂而無染，遭厄窮而不悶，或出人間，或棲物表，逍遙寄託，莫知所終。」

translations.literal: Thus encountering glory and joy without being stained, meeting hardship and poverty without vexation, sometimes going among humanity, sometimes dwelling beyond things, wandering freely and entrusting oneself—none knows where it ends."
translations.idiomatic: Thus one meets glory and joy without being stained, hardship and poverty without distress; sometimes moving among humanity, sometimes dwelling beyond the world of things, wandering freely and entrusting oneself—with no one knowing where it ends."

sentences.zh: 李順，字德正，钜鹿公靈之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Li Shun, styled Dezheng, was a younger male cousin of Duke of Julu Ling on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shun, styled Dezheng, was a younger cousin of Li Ling, Duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 父系，慕容垂散騎侍郎、東武城令。

translations.literal: His father Xi served Murong Chui as Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and Magistrate of Dongwucheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi had served Murong Chui as Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry and Magistrate of Dongwucheng.

sentences.zh: 道武定中原，以為平棘令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daowu pacified the Central Plains, he was appointed Magistrate of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu pacified the Central Plains, Xi was appointed Magistrate of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈趙郡太守、平棘男。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Administrator of Zhao commandery and the title Baron of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted the title Administrator of Zhao commandery and Baron of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 順博涉經史，有計策。

translations.literal: Shun was broadly versed in the classics and history and possessed stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was broadly versed in the classics and histories and possessed a strategist's mind.

sentences.zh: 神瑞中，拜中書博士，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: During the Shenrui era he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat, then transferred to Gentlemen Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenrui era he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat, then promoted to Gentlemen Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從征蠕蠕，以籌略，賜爵平棘子。

translations.literal: On campaign against the Rouran, for his strategic planning he was granted the title Viscount of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against the Rouran, for his strategic planning he was granted the title Viscount of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 太武將討赫連昌，謂崔浩曰：「朕前北征，李順獻策數事，實合經略大謀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu was about to attack Helian Chang, he said to Cui Hao: "On my previous northern campaign Li Shun offered several stratagems that truly accorded with broad strategic designs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu was about to attack Helian Chang, he said to Cui Hao, "On my previous northern campaign Li Shun offered several stratagems that truly accorded with broad strategic designs.

sentences.zh: 今欲使總前驅之事，何如？

translations.literal: Now I wish to put him in overall charge of the vanguard. What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now I wish to put him in overall charge of the vanguard. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「順智足周務，實如聖旨。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Shun's intellect suffices for thorough affairs—truly as Your Majesty says.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "Shun's intellect suffices for thorough affairs—truly as Your Majesty says.

sentences.zh: 但臣與之婚姻，深知其行，然性果於去就，不可專委。

translations.literal: But I am related to him by marriage and know his conduct well; yet by nature he is decisive about staying or leaving, and he cannot be wholly entrusted."
translations.idiomatic: "But I am related to him by marriage and know his conduct well; yet by nature he is decisive about staying or leaving, and he cannot be wholly entrusted."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The emperor then dropped the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 初，浩弟娶順妹，又以弟子娶順女，雖婚媾，而浩頗輕順，順又不伏，由是潛相猜忌，故浩毀之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hao's younger brother had married Shun's sister, and Hao's nephew had married Shun's daughter; though they were linked by marriage, Hao rather looked down on Shun and Shun would not submit—therefore they secretly harbored mutual suspicion, and so Hao slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Hao's younger brother had married Shun's sister, and Hao's nephew had married Shun's daughter; though they were linked by marriage, Hao looked down on Shun and Shun would not yield—therefore they secretly harbored mutual suspicion, and Hao slandered him.

sentences.zh: 至統萬，大破昌軍，順謀功居多。

translations.literal: At Tongwan greatly broke Chang's army; Shun's merit in planning was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: At Tongwan they routed Chang's army, and Shun's contribution to the plan was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 後征統萬，昌出逆戰，順破其左軍。

translations.literal: Later on the campaign against Tongwan, when Chang came out to meet them in battle, Shun routed his left wing.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on the campaign against Tongwan, when Chang came out to meet them in battle, Shun routed his left wing.

sentences.zh: 及克統萬，帝賜諸將珍寶雜物，順固辭，唯取書數千卷，帝善之。

translations.literal: When Tongwan was taken, the emperor bestowed precious objects and miscellaneous goods on the generals; Shun firmly declined all but took several thousand scrolls of books, which the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongwan was taken, the emperor bestowed precious objects and miscellaneous goods on the generals; Shun firmly declined everything but took several thousand scrolls of books, which the emperor commended.

sentences.zh: 遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attending Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 又從擊赫連定於平涼。

translations.literal: He also followed on the attack against Helian Ding at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed on the attack against Helian Ding at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 三秦平，進爵為侯，遷四部尚書，甚見寵待。

translations.literal: When the Three Qins were pacified, his enfeoffment was raised to marquis, he was transferred to Director of the Four Departments, and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Qins were pacified, his enfeoffment was raised to marquis, he was appointed Director of the Four Departments, and enjoyed great favor.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜以河西內附，帝欲簡行人，崔浩曰：「宜令清德重臣，奉詔褒慰，尚書順即其人也。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun submitted the Hexi region to the empire; the emperor wished to select an envoy. Cui Hao said: "A minister of pure virtue and weighty standing should be sent with an edict to praise and comfort him—Director Shun is the man.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun submitted the Hexi region to the empire; the emperor wished to select an envoy. Cui Hao said, "A minister of pure virtue and weighty standing should be sent with an edict to praise and comfort him—Director Shun is the man.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「順納言大臣，不宜方為此使，若蒙遜身執玉帛而朝於朕，復何以加之？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Shun is a minister who remonstrates at court; he is not fit to serve merely as such an envoy. If Mengxun came in person bearing jade and silks to pay court to me, what further honor could I give him?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Shun is a minister who remonstrates at court; he is not fit to serve merely as such an envoy. If Mengxun came in person bearing jade and silks to pay court to me, what further honor could I give him?

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「邢貞使吳，亦魏之太常，苟事是宜，無嫌於重。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Xing Zhen was sent to Wu though he too was Grand Director of Ceremonial for Wei—if the mission is appropriate, there is no objection on grounds of rank.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said, "Xing Zhen was sent to Wu though he too was Grand Director of Ceremonial for Wei—if the mission is appropriate, there is no objection on grounds of rank.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，以順為太常，策拜蒙遜為太傅，涼王。

translations.literal: Emperor followed this; made Shun Grand Director of Ceremonial, issued edict investing Mengxun as Grand Tutor, Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. He made Shun grand director of ceremonial and issued an edict investing Mengxun as grand tutor and prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜使持節、都督四州諸軍事、長安鎮都大將、甯西將軍、開府，進爵高平公。

translations.literal: On return from mission appointed Commissioner with Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in four provinces, Grand General of Chang'an garrison, General Who Pacifies the West, opened office; enfeoffment raised to Duke of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made commissioner with the staff, commander-in-chief of military affairs in four provinces, grand general of the Chang'an garrison, General Who Pacifies the West, with an opened headquarters, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徵為四部尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back as Director of the Four Departments and additionally made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as Director of the Four Departments and additionally appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 延和初，使涼。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yanhe era he was sent on mission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yanhe era he was sent on mission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜辭疾，箕坐隱幾，無起動狀。

translations.literal: Mengxun pleaded illness, sat with legs spread upon armrest, showed no sign of rising.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun pleaded illness and sat sprawled on an armrest, giving no sign that he would rise.

sentences.zh: 順正色大言曰：「不謂此叟無禮，乃至於是！

translations.literal: Shun said sternly in a loud voice: "I never thought this old fellow would be so rude as this!
translations.idiomatic: Shun said sternly in a loud voice, "I never thought this old fellow would be so rude as this!

sentences.zh: 」握節而出。

translations.literal: " He grasped his staff of office and marched out.
translations.idiomatic: " He grasped his staff of office and marched out.

sentences.zh: 蒙遜使中兵校郎楊定歸追順曰：「太常雲朝廷賜不拜之詔，是以敢自安耳；

translations.literal: Mengxun sent Central Army Commandant Yang Dinggui after Shun, who said: "The Grand Director said the court has granted an edict excusing him from bowing, and therefore he dared remain at ease;
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun sent Central Army Commandant Yang Dinggui after Shun, who said, "The Grand Director said the court has granted an edict excusing him from bowing, and therefore he dared remain at ease;

sentences.zh: 若曰爾拜爾跽，而不承命，乃小臣之罪矣。

translations.literal: but if Your Excellency says you will bow and kneel yet still do not accept the command, that will be the fault of a petty subject."
translations.idiomatic: "but if Your Excellency says you will bow and kneel yet still do not accept the command, that will be the fault of a petty subject."

sentences.zh: 」順曰：「齊桓公九合諸侯，一匡天下，周公賜胙，命曰伯舅無拜，而桓公降而拜受。

translations.literal: " Shun said: "Duke Huan of Qi nine times convened the feudal lords and set the realm to rights; the Duke of Zhou granted him sacrificial flesh with the command, 'As my uncle you need not bow'—yet Huan descended and bowed to receive it.
translations.idiomatic: " Shun said, "Duke Huan of Qi nine times convened the feudal lords and set the realm to rights; the Duke of Zhou granted him sacrificial flesh with the command, 'As my uncle you need not bow'—yet Huan descended and bowed to receive it.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷未有不拜之詔，而便偃蹇自取，此乃速禍之道。

translations.literal: The court has issued no edict excusing you from bowing, yet you insolently take this upon yourself—this is the way to hurry disaster upon yourself."
translations.idiomatic: "The court has issued no edict excusing you from bowing, yet you insolently take this upon yourself—this is the way to hurry disaster upon yourself."

sentences.zh: 」蒙遜拜伏盡禮。

translations.literal: " Mengxun bowed and prostrated himself with full courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: " Mengxun bowed and prostrated himself with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 順還，帝問與蒙遜往復辭，及其政教得失。

translations.literal: When Shun returned, the emperor asked about his exchanges with Mengxun and about the gains and losses of his government and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun returned, the emperor asked about his exchanges with Mengxun and about the strengths and weaknesses of his governance and instruction.

sentences.zh: 順曰：「蒙遜專威河右，三十許年，經涉艱難，粗識機變，雖不能貽厥孫謀，猶足以終其一世。

translations.literal: Shun said: "Mengxun has held sole authority west of the Yellow River for some thirty years; through hardship he has roughly learned to read situations—though he cannot leave a legacy for his descendants, he is still enough to finish out his life.
translations.idiomatic: Shun said, "Mengxun has held sole authority west of the Yellow River for some thirty years; through hardship he has roughly learned to read situations—though he cannot leave a legacy for his descendants, he is still enough to finish out his life.

sentences.zh: 但前歲表許十月送曇無懺，及臣往迎，便乖本意，不臣不信，於是而甚。

translations.literal: But last year in his memorial he promised to send Tanwuchen in the tenth month, and when I went to receive him he went against his original intent; he is greatly lacking in loyalty and trust.
translations.idiomatic: "But last year in his memorial he promised to send Tanwuchen in the tenth month, and when I went to receive him he went against his original intent; he is greatly lacking in loyalty and trust.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，不復周矣。

translations.literal: In my view he will not long remain steadfast."
translations.idiomatic: "In my view he will not long remain steadfast."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「若如卿言，則效在無遠，襲世之後，早晚當滅。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "If it is as you say, the effect is not far off; after he passes the realm on, destruction will come sooner or later.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "If it is as you say, the effect is not far off; after he passes the realm on, destruction will come sooner or later.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣略見其子，並非才俊。

translations.literal: " He replied: "I have briefly seen his sons, and none are men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I have briefly seen his sons, and none are men of talent.

sentences.zh: 如聞敦煌太守牧犍，器性粗立，若繼蒙遜，必此人也。

translations.literal: I hear that Muzhi, Administrator of Dunhuang, has some capacity and firmness of character; if he succeeds Mengxun, it will surely be this man.
translations.idiomatic: "I hear that Muzhi, Administrator of Dunhuang, has some capacity and firmness of character; if he succeeds Mengxun, it will surely be this man.

sentences.zh: 然比之于父，僉雲不逮，殆天所用資聖明也。

translations.literal: Yet compared with his father all say he falls short—perhaps this is Heaven's way of providing for Your Sage Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: "Yet compared with his father all say he falls short—perhaps this is Heaven's way of providing for Your Sage Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕方事於東，未暇營西，如卿所言，三五年間，不足為晚。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I am at present occupied with the east and have no leisure to manage the west; as you say, within three or five years it will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I am at present occupied with the east and have no leisure to manage the west; as you say, within three or five years it will not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」及蒙遜死問至，太武謂順曰：「卿言蒙遜死，驗矣；

translations.literal: When word of Mengxun's death arrived, Emperor Taiwu said to Shun: "What you said about Mengxun's death has been verified;
translations.idiomatic: When word of Mengxun's death arrived, Emperor Taiwu said to Shun, "What you said about Mengxun's death has been verified;

sentences.zh: 又言牧犍立，何其妙哉！

translations.literal: and that Muzhi would succeed him—how wonderfully perceptive!
translations.idiomatic: "and that Muzhi would succeed him—how wonderfully perceptive!

sentences.zh: 朕克涼州，亦當不遠。

translations.literal: My conquest of Liang province cannot be far off.
translations.idiomatic: "My conquest of Liang province cannot be far off.

sentences.zh: 」於是賜絹千匹、廄馬一乘，寵待彌厚，政無巨細，無所不參。

translations.literal: Thereupon bestowed thousand bolts silk and one stable horse; favored him ever more generously; on affairs great or small there was nothing in which he did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted a thousand bolts of silk and a stable horse, favored him ever more warmly, and consulted him on every matter, large or small.

sentences.zh: 崔浩惡之。

translations.literal: Cui Hao hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao hated him.

sentences.zh: 順凡使涼州十二回，太武稱其能。

translations.literal: Shun in all made twelve missions to Liang province; Emperor Taiwu praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Shun served on twelve missions to Liang province in all, and Emperor Taiwu praised his skill.

sentences.zh: 而蒙遜數與順遊宴，頗有悖言，恐順泄之，以金寶納順懷中，故蒙遜罪釁得不聞。

translations.literal: Yet Mengxun often feasted and traveled with Shun and spoke rather rebelliously; fearing Shun would reveal this, put gold and precious objects into Shun's bosom, so Mengxun's crimes and faults did not become known.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Mengxun often feasted with Shun and let slip treasonable words. Fearing exposure, he stuffed gold and jewels into Shun's robes, and so his offenses never reached the court.

sentences.zh: 又西域沙門曇無懺有方術，在涼州，詔追之。

translations.literal: Also Western Regions monk Tanwuchen possessed occult arts, was in Liang province; edict summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions monk Tanwuchen, who possessed occult arts, was in Liang province when an edict summoned him.

sentences.zh: 順受蒙遜金，聽殺之。

translations.literal: Shun took gold from Mengxun and allowed him to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shun took gold from Mengxun and allowed him to be killed.

sentences.zh: 浩並知之，密言於帝。

translations.literal: Hao knew all of this and spoke of it secretly to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Hao knew all of this and spoke of it secretly to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝未之信。

translations.literal: The emperor did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not believe it.

sentences.zh: 太延三年，順復使涼州，及還，帝問以將平河右計，順以人勞既久，不可頻動，帝從之。

translations.literal: Taiyan third year, Shun again sent on mission to Liang province; on return emperor asked about plans to pacify west of river; Shun said people exhausted long, ought not be stirred frequently; emperor followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiyan, Shun was again sent to Liang province. On his return the emperor asked how to pacify the lands west of the Yellow River. Shun argued that the people had been worn down too long to bear repeated campaigns, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 五年，議征涼州，順以涼州乏水草，不宜遠征。

translations.literal: Fifth year, when conquest of Liang province debated, Shun said Liang province lacked grass and water, not suitable for distant expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when an expedition against Liang province was debated, Shun said the region lacked grass and water and was unsuited to a distant campaign.

sentences.zh: 崔浩固以為宜征，帝從浩議。

translations.literal: Cui Hao firmly maintained expedition advisable; emperor followed Hao's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao insisted that an expedition was warranted, and the emperor sided with him.

sentences.zh: 及至姑臧，甚豐水草，帝與景穆書，頗嫌順。

translations.literal: When reached Guzang grass and water abundant; emperor wrote to Crown Prince Jingmu, somewhat resentful of Shun.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Guzang, grass and water proved abundant. The emperor wrote to Crown Prince Jingmu with evident resentment toward Shun.

sentences.zh: 後謂浩曰：「卿昔所言，今果驗矣。

translations.literal: Later he said to Hao: "What you said before has now indeed been verified.
translations.idiomatic: Later he said to Hao, "What you said before has now indeed been verified.

sentences.zh: 」克涼州後，聞受蒙遜金而聽其殺曇無懺，益嫌之。

translations.literal: After Liang province taken, when heard Shun had taken Mengxun's gold and allowed Tanwuchen to be killed, resented him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang province fell, learning that Shun had taken Mengxun's gold and permitted Tanwuchen's execution, the emperor grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 猶以寵舊，未加其罪，尚詔順差次群臣，賜以爵位。

translations.literal: Still because of old favor did not yet impose punishment; even ordered Shun to rank officials and grant them enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, out of old affection he withheld punishment and even had Shun rank the officials and assign them titles.

sentences.zh: 順頗受納，品第不平。

translations.literal: Shun accepted many bribes and ranked them unfairly.
translations.idiomatic: Shun accepted many bribes and ranked them unfairly.

sentences.zh: 涼州人徐桀發其事，浩又毀之。

translations.literal: Xu Jie of Liang province exposed the matter; Hao slandered him again.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie of Liang province brought the affair to light, and Hao slandered Shun once more.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，刑順於城西。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and executed Shun west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and executed Shun west of the city.

sentences.zh: 順死後數年，其從父弟孝伯為太武知重，居中用事。

translations.literal: Several years after Shun's death his younger male cousin Xiaobo came to be known and valued by Emperor Taiwu, held power within court.
translations.idiomatic: Several years after Shun's death, his cousin Xiaobo won Emperor Taiwu's trust and wielded influence at court.

sentences.zh: 及浩誅，帝怒甚，謂孝伯曰：「卿從兄往雖誤國，朕意亦未至此。

translations.literal: When Hao was executed the emperor was exceedingly angry and said to Xiaobo: "Although your elder cousin erred against the state in the past, my mind had not gone so far as this.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was executed the emperor was exceedingly angry and said to Xiaobo, "Although your elder cousin erred against the state in the past, my mind had not gone so far as this.

sentences.zh: 由浩，遂殺卿從兄。

translations.literal: It was because of Hao that I ended up killing your elder cousin."
translations.idiomatic: "It was because of Hao that I ended up killing your elder cousin."

sentences.zh: 」皇興初，順子敷等貴寵，獻文追贈順侍中、鎮西大將軍、太尉公、高平王，諡曰宣王。

translations.literal: At beginning of Huangxing, Shun's sons Fu and others enjoyed high favor; Emperor Xianwen posthumously granted Shun Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, Grand Commandant, Prince of Gaoping, posthumous title Prince Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Huangxing, Shun's sons Fu and others rose in favor. Emperor Xianwen posthumously made Shun palace attendant, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, grand commandant, and Prince of Gaoping, with the posthumous title Prince Xuan.

sentences.zh: 妻邢氏曰孝妃。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Xing was titled Consort Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Xing was titled Consort Xiao.

sentences.zh: 順四子。

translations.literal: Shun had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shun had four sons.

sentences.zh: 長子敷，字景文。

translations.literal: His eldest son Fu, styled Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Fu, styled Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 真君二年，選入中書教學，以忠謹給侍東宮，以為中散。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenjun he was selected for instruction in the Secretariat; for loyalty and prudence he was given attendance at the Eastern Palace and made Central Scattered Courtier.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenjun he was selected for instruction in the Secretariat; for loyalty and prudence he was given attendance at the Eastern Palace and appointed Central Scattered Courtier.

sentences.zh: 與䐶、盧遐、度世等並以聰敏內參機密。

translations.literal: Together with Li Zhi, Lu Xia, Dushi, and others inwardly entrusted with secret affairs on account of cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Li Zhi, Lu Xia, Dushi, and others, he was admitted to confidential counsel because of his keen mind.

sentences.zh: 敷性謙恭，加有文學，文成寵遇之。

translations.literal: Fu was modest and courteous by nature, and with his literary attainments he was favored by Emperor Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was modest and courteous by nature, and with his literary attainments he was favored by Emperor Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書下大夫，賜爵平棘子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Clerk Under the Secretariat and granted the title Viscount of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Clerk Under the Secretariat and granted the title Viscount of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 後兼錄南部，遷散騎常侍、南部尚書、中書監，領內外秘書，襲爵高平公。

translations.literal: Later he additionally took charge of the Southern Department, was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of the Southern Department, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and charged with internal and external secretarial affairs, and inherited the enfeoffment of Duke of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Later he additionally took charge of the Southern Department, was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of the Southern Department, and Supervisor of the Secretariat, charged with internal and external secretarial affairs, and inherited the enfeoffment of Duke of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 朝政大議，事無不關。

translations.literal: In great deliberations of court policy there was nothing that did not concern him.
translations.idiomatic: In great deliberations of court policy there was nothing that did not concern him.

sentences.zh: 及宋徐州刺史薛安都、司州刺史常珍奇等以彭城、懸瓠降，于時朝議謂未必可信，敷乃固執必然。

translations.literal: When Xue Andu, Governor of Xuzhou under Song, and Chang Zhenqi, Governor of Sizhou, surrendered Pengcheng and Xuancheng, at the time court opinion held that they might not be trusted; Fu alone firmly maintained that they certainly would.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Andu, Governor of Xuzhou under Song, and Chang Zhenqi, Governor of Sizhou, surrendered Pengcheng and Xuancheng, court opinion held that they might not be trusted; Fu alone firmly maintained that they certainly would.

sentences.zh: 乃遣師接援，淮海寧輯。

translations.literal: Troops were then dispatched to receive and support them, and the Huai and Hai regions were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were then dispatched to receive and support them, and the Huai and Hai regions were settled.

sentences.zh: 敷既見待二世，兄弟親戚在朝者十餘人。

translations.literal: Fu had been favored across two reigns, and more than ten brothers and kinsmen held office at court.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had been favored across two reigns, and more than ten brothers and kinsmen held office at court.

sentences.zh: 弟弈又有寵于文明太后。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi also enjoyed favor with Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yi also enjoyed favor with Empress Dowager Wenming.

sentences.zh: 䐶列其隱罪二十餘條，獻文大怒，皇興四年，誅敷兄弟，削順位號為庶人。

translations.literal: Li Zhi listed more than twenty hidden offenses, greatly angering Emperor Xianwen; in the fourth year of Huangxing he executed Fu and his brothers and reduced Shun's titles to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi listed more than twenty hidden offenses, greatly angering Emperor Xianwen; in the fourth year of Huangxing he executed Fu and his brothers and reduced Shun's titles to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 敷從弟顯德、妹夫廣平宋叔珍等皆坐關亂公私，同時伏法。

translations.literal: Fu's younger male cousin Xiande, his sister's husband Song Shuzhen of Guangping, and others were all convicted for having interfered with public and private affairs and were executed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's younger male cousin Xiande, his sister's husband Song Shuzhen of Guangping, and others were all convicted for having interfered with public and private affairs and were executed at the same time.

sentences.zh: 敷兄弟敦崇孝義，家門有禮，至於居喪法度，吉凶書記，皆合典則，為北州所稱美。

translations.literal: The Fu brothers honored filial piety and righteousness; their household observed ritual propriety, and in mourning rites, auspicious and inauspicious correspondence, everything accorded with canonical standards—they were praised throughout northern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu brothers honored filial piety and righteousness; their household observed ritual propriety, and in mourning rites, auspicious and inauspicious correspondence, everything accorded with canonical standards—they were praised throughout the northern provinces.

sentences.zh: 既致斯禍，時人嘆惜之。

translations.literal: After this catastrophe people of the time sighed and lamented for them.
translations.idiomatic: After this catastrophe people of the time sighed and lamented for them.

sentences.zh: 敷弟式，字景則，學業知名。

translations.literal: Fu's younger brother Shi, styled Jingze, was known for his scholarly attainments.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's younger brother Shi, styled Jingze, was known for his scholarly attainments.

sentences.zh: 位西兗州刺史、濮陽侯。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Inspector of Western Yan province and Marquis of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Inspector of Western Yan province and Marquis of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 式自以家據權要，心慮危禍，常敕津吏，台有使者，必先啟然後度之。

translations.literal: Shi, believing his family held power at court, feared disaster at heart and often instructed the ferry officers that when the court sent envoys they must report first before allowing them to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, believing his family held power at court, feared disaster at heart and often instructed the ferry officers that when the court sent envoys they must report first before allowing them to cross.

sentences.zh: 既而使人卒至，始雲南過，既濟，突入執式赴都，與兄俱死。

translations.literal: Yet envoys suddenly arrived; at first they said they were passing southward, but once they had crossed they burst in, seized Shi, and took him to the capital, where he died together with his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Yet envoys suddenly arrived; at first they said they were passing southward, but once they had crossed they burst in, seized Shi, and took him to the capital, where he died together with his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 子憲，字仲軌，清粹善風儀，好學有器度。

translations.literal: His son Xian, styled Zhonggui, was pure and refined with fine bearing, loved learning, and possessed capacity and measure.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian, styled Zhonggui, was pure and refined with fine bearing, loved learning, and possessed capacity and measure.

sentences.zh: 太和初，襲爵，又降為伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era he inherited the enfeoffment, then was lowered to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era he inherited the enfeoffment, then was lowered to marquis.

sentences.zh: 拜秘書中散，雅為孝文知賞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Central Scattered Courtier of the Secretariat and was greatly appreciated by Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Central Scattered Courtier of the Secretariat and was greatly appreciated by Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 後拜趙郡太守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Administrator of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 趙修與其州裏，修歸葬父母也，牧守以下畏之累跡，憲不為屈，時人高之。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiu was from his same district; when Xiu returned to bury his parents, magistrates and prefectures below him showed fear in their crowded tracks, but Xian did not yield—people of the time admired him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiu was from his same district; when Xiu returned to bury his parents, magistrates and prefectures below him showed fear in their crowded tracks, but Xian did not yield—people of the time admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 後以党附高肇，為御史所劾。

translations.literal: Later, because he had joined Gao Zhao's faction, he was impeached by the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was impeached by the censorate for having joined Gao Zhao's faction.

sentences.zh: 正光五年，行雍州刺史，尋除七兵尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenguang he served as acting Governor of Yong province; soon after he was appointed Minister of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhenguang he served as acting Governor of Yong province and was soon appointed Minister of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，除征東將軍、揚州刺史、淮南大都督。

translations.literal: During the Xiaochang era he was appointed General Who Campaigns East, Governor of Yang province, and Grand Commander of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he received appointment as General Who Campaigns East, Governor of Yang province, and Grand Commander of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 及梁平北大將軍元樹等來寇，憲力屈而降。

translations.literal: When Yuan Shu and others, generals of Liang's Northern Pacification army, came to raid, Xian's strength was exhausted and he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Shu and other generals of Liang's Northern Pacification army came to raid, Xian's strength was spent and he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 因求還國。

translations.literal: He then asked to return to his own state.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 既至，敕付廷尉。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, an imperial order handed him over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, an imperial order handed him over to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 憲女婿安樂王鑒據相州反，靈太后謂鑒心懷劫脅，遂詔賜憲死。

translations.literal: Xian's son-in-law, Prince of Anle Jian, seized Xiang province in rebellion; Empress Dowager Ling said Jian's heart had been coerced, and so an edict ordered Xian to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's son-in-law, Prince of Anle Jian, seized Xiang province in rebellion; Empress Dowager Ling held that Jian had acted under duress, and so an edict ordered Xian to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，贈儀同三司、尚書令、定州刺史，諡曰文靖。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was posthumously granted Three Divisions of Equal Rank, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ding province, with the posthumous epithet Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he was posthumously granted Three Divisions of Equal Rank, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Ding province, with the posthumous epithet Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 子希遠，字景沖，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Xiyuan, styled Jingchong, died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiyuan, styled Jingchong, died young.

sentences.zh: 希遠子祖悛，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: Xiyuan's son Zujuan inherited his grandfather's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyuan's son Zujuan inherited his grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 希遠弟希宗，字景玄。

translations.literal: Xiyuan's younger brother Xizong, styled Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyuan's younger brother Xizong, styled Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 性寬和，儀貌雅麗，有才學。

translations.literal: By nature he was gentle and harmonious, with an elegant and handsome bearing, and possessed learning and talent.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was gentle and amiable, handsome in bearing, and possessed both learning and talent.

sentences.zh: 位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Emblem.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Emblem.

sentences.zh: 齊神武擢為中外府長史。

translations.literal: Gao Huan of Northern Qi promoted him to chief administrator of the Central and Foreign Affairs Office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan promoted him to chief administrator of the Central and Foreign Affairs Office.

sentences.zh: 文宣帝納其第二女為皇后。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan took his second daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan took his second daughter as empress.

sentences.zh: 位上党太守，卒。

translations.literal: He served as Administrator of Shangdang and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Shangdang and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公、殷州刺史，諡曰文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Duke of Works and Governor of Yin province, with the posthumous epithet Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Duke of Works and Governor of Yin province, with the posthumous epithet Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 希宗長子祖升，儀容瑰麗，垂手過膝，文學足以自通。

translations.literal: Xizong's eldest son Zusheng was of splendid countenance, with hands hanging past his knees; his literary attainments sufficed for self-cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong's eldest son Zusheng was strikingly handsome, with hands that hung past his knees; his literary attainments were enough to see him through on his own.

sentences.zh: 位齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose to Governor of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 淫于從兵妻，見殺。

translations.literal: He violated the wife of a follower-soldier and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: He violated a follower-soldier's wife and was killed.

sentences.zh: 希宗弟希仁，字景山，有學識。

translations.literal: Xizong's younger brother Xiren, styled Jingshan, possessed learning and knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong's younger brother Xiren, styled Jingshan, possessed learning and erudition.

sentences.zh: 卒于侍中、太子詹事。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Palace Attendant and Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Palace Attendant and Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子公統，仕齊，位員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Gongtong served Qi and rose to Outer Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongtong served Northern Qi and rose to Outer Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 高歸彥之反，公統為之謀主。

translations.literal: When Gao Guiyan rebelled, Gongtong was the chief strategist for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Guiyan rebelled, Gongtong served as his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 歸彥敗，伏法。

translations.literal: When Guiyan was defeated, Gongtong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Guiyan was defeated, Gongtong was executed.

sentences.zh: 其母崔氏當沒官，其弟宣寶行賕，改籍注老。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Cui was to be confiscated as a government servant; his younger brother Xuanbao offered bribes to alter the registry and register her as elderly.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Cui was to be confiscated as a government servant; his younger brother Xuanbao offered bribes to alter the household registry and register her as elderly.

sentences.zh: 事發，武成帝棓殺之，肝腦塗地。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, Emperor Wucheng beat him to death with a club until his brains and viscera smeared the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, Emperor Wucheng beat him to death with a club until his brains and viscera smeared the ground.

sentences.zh: 希仁弟騫，字希義，博涉經史，文藻富贍。

translations.literal: Xiren's younger brother Qian, styled Xiyi, ranged broadly through classics and histories and was rich in literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Xiren's younger brother Qian, styled Xiyi, ranged widely through the classics and histories and wrote with rich literary ornament.

sentences.zh: 位散騎常侍、殷州大中正、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He rose to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Senior Rectifier of Yin province, and Director of the Left of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Senior Rectifier of Yin province, and Director of the Left of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 以本官兼散騎常侍使梁。

translations.literal: In his existing office he was additionally appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and sent as envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Retaining his existing office, he was additionally appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and sent as envoy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 後坐事免，論者以為非罪。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed on account of an offense; commentators held that he was not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed on account of an offense, though commentators held that he was not guilty.

sentences.zh: 騫嘗贈親友盧元明、魏收詩云：「監河愛升水，蘇子惜餘明。

translations.literal: Qian once presented a poem to his close friends Lu Yuanming and Wei Shou, saying: "One who guards the river loves rising water; Master Su cherishes the remaining light.
translations.idiomatic: Qian once sent his close friends Lu Yuanming and Wei Shou a poem, saying, "One who guards the river loves rising water; Master Su cherishes the lingering light.

sentences.zh: 益州達友趣，廷尉辯交情。

translations.literal: In Yizhou one attains friendly companions; at the Minister of Justice one disputes over friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In Yizhou one attains the company of friends; at the Minister of Justice one argues over friendship.

sentences.zh: 」蓋失職之志云。

translations.literal: " This expressed his feelings at losing office.
translations.idiomatic: " This expressed his feelings at losing office.

sentences.zh: 後除給事黃門侍郎，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and died.

sentences.zh: 其文筆別有集錄。

translations.literal: His writings were separately collected and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: His literary works were separately collected and recorded.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，贈儀同三司，諡曰文惠。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was posthumously granted Three Divisions of Equal Rank with the posthumous epithet Wenhui.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, he was posthumously granted Three Divisions of Equal Rank with the posthumous epithet Wenhui.

sentences.zh: 騫弟希禮，字景節，性敦厚，容止樞機，動遵禮度。

translations.literal: Qian's younger brother Xili, styled Jingjie, was by nature sincere and thick; his bearing and demeanor were measured and dignified, and in action he followed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's younger brother Xili, styled Jingjie, was by nature sincere and steadfast; his bearing was measured and dignified, and in all conduct he observed ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 起家著作佐郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: He began his career as Assistant to the Director of Composition and compiled the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Assistant to the Director of Composition and compiled the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 歷位太常少卿，兼廷尉少卿，行魏尹事，豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Vice Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently Vice Minister of Justice, acting Prefect of the Wei capital, and Governor of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Vice Minister of Ceremonies, concurrently Vice Minister of Justice, acting Prefect of the Wei capital, and Governor of Yu province.

sentences.zh: 仍居議曹，與邢邵等議定禮律。

translations.literal: He remained in the Deliberation Office and, together with Xing Shao and others, deliberated and fixed ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in the Deliberation Office and, together with Xing Shao and others, deliberated and fixed ritual and penal law.

sentences.zh: 卒于信州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while Governor of Xin province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Governor of Xin province.

sentences.zh: 子孝貞，字元操，好學善屬文。

translations.literal: His son Xiaozhen, styled Yuancao, loved learning and was skilled in composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaozhen, styled Yuancao, loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，釋褐司徒府參軍事。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, upon first appointment he became Aide in the Chancellor's office of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Northern Qi, upon first taking office he became Aide in the Chancellor's office of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 與弟孝基同見吏部郎中陸昂。

translations.literal: Together with his younger brother Xiaoji he went to see Lu Ang, Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his younger brother Xiaoji he went to see Lu Ang, Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 昂戲之曰：「弟名孝基，兄其替矣！

translations.literal: Ang joked, saying: "Your younger brother is named Xiaoji—the elder must be the substitute!
translations.idiomatic: Ang joked, saying, "Your younger brother is named Xiaoji—the elder must be the substitute!

sentences.zh: 」孝貞對曰：「禮雖不肖，請附子臧。

translations.literal: " Xiaozhen replied: "Though I am unworthy, Li asks to follow Zizang.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaozhen replied, "Though I am not Zengzi's equal, I yet ask to follow Zizang.

sentences.zh: 」昂握手曰：「士固不妄有名，吾賢必當遠至。

translations.literal: " Ang took his hand and said: "A scholar truly does not bear his name in vain; our worthy man will surely go far.
translations.idiomatic: " Ang took his hand and said, "A scholar truly does not bear his name in vain; our worthy man will surely go far.

sentences.zh: 」簡靜，不妄通接賓客。

translations.literal: " He was reserved and quiet and did not casually receive or call upon guests.
translations.idiomatic: " He was reserved and quiet and did not casually receive or call upon guests.

sentences.zh: 射策甲科，拜給事中。

translations.literal: In the archery examination he ranked in the top class and was appointed Attendant at the Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the archery examination he ranked in the top class and was appointed Attendant at the Court.

sentences.zh: 稍遷兼通直散騎常侍，副李翥使陳。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to concurrent Regular Attendant and Direct Transmission, and as deputy to Li Xu served as envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to concurrent Regular Attendant and Direct Transmission and, as deputy to Li Xu, served as envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 孝貞從姊則昭信皇后，從兄祖勳女為廢帝濟南王妃，祖欽女一為後主娥英，一為琅邪王儼妃，祖勳叔騫女為安德王延宗妃。

translations.literal: Xiaozhen's paternal cousin was Empress Zhaoxin; Zuxun his cousin's daughter was consort to the Deposed Emperor, Prince of Jinan; Zuxin's daughters—one became Empress Eying of the Later Lord, one consort to Prince of Langye Yan; Zuxun's uncle Qian's daughter was consort to Prince of Ande Yanzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhen's paternal cousin was Empress Zhaoxin; his cousin Zuxun's daughter was consort to the Deposed Emperor, Prince of Jinan; Zuxin's daughters—one became Empress Eying of the Later Lord, one consort to Prince of Langye Yan; Zuxun's uncle Qian's daughter was consort to Prince of Ande Yanzong.

sentences.zh: 諸房子女，多有才貌，又因昭信後，所以與帝室姻媾重疊。

translations.literal: The sons and daughters of the various branches were mostly gifted in talent and appearance; moreover, because of Empress Zhaoxin, their marriage ties with the imperial house overlapped repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: The sons and daughters of the various branches were mostly gifted in talent and appearance; moreover, because of Empress Zhaoxin, their marriage ties with the imperial house overlapped again and again.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並以文學自達，恥為外戚家。

translations.literal: The brothers all attained distinction through literature and were ashamed to be reckoned as a consort clan.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers all made their way through literary attainment and were ashamed to be counted as a consort clan.

sentences.zh: 于時黃門侍郎高乾和親要用事，求婚於孝貞，孝貞拒之。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Qianhe, Regular Attendant at the Yellow Gate and a close relative wielding power, sought marriage with Xiaozhen, but Xiaozhen refused.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gao Qianhe, Regular Attendant at the Yellow Gate and a close kinsman in power, sought marriage with Xiaozhen, but Xiaozhen refused.

sentences.zh: 由是有隙，陰譖之，出為太尉府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Hence there was enmity; he slandered Xiaozhen in secret and Xiaozhen was sent out as Aide for External Military Affairs in the Grand Commandant's office.
translations.idiomatic: Hence there was enmity; Qianhe slandered Xiaozhen in secret, and Xiaozhen was sent out as Aide for External Military Affairs in the Grand Commandant's office.

sentences.zh: 後曆中書舍人。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served in succession as Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，遷蒙州刺史，吏人安之。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to Governor of Meng province, where officials and people found security under him.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to Governor of Meng province, where officials and people found peace under his rule.

sentences.zh: 自此不復留意文筆。

translations.literal: From then on he no longer paid attention to literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he no longer gave his mind to literary composition.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，慨然歎曰：「五十之年，倏焉已過，鬢垂素髮，筋力已衰，宦意文情，一時盡矣，悲夫！

translations.literal: When people asked the reason, he sighed deeply and said: "Fifty years—gone in an instant! My temples hang with white hair, my sinews and strength are spent; ambition for office and passion for letters—all vanished at once. Alas!
translations.idiomatic: When people asked why, he sighed deeply and said, "Fifty years—gone in an instant! My temples are white, my strength is spent; ambition for office and passion for letters—all gone at once. Alas!

sentences.zh: 」然每暇日，輒引賓客，弦歌對酒，終日為歡。

translations.literal: " Yet on every day of leisure he would gather guests, sing to strings and drink wine, making merry all day long.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet on every day of leisure he would gather guests, sing to strings and drink wine, making merry all day long.

sentences.zh: 後徵拜內史侍郎，與內史令李德林參典文翰。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and together with Director of the Secretariat Li Delin shared charge of literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, sharing charge of literary composition with Director of the Secretariat Li Delin.

sentences.zh: 元操無干劇之用，頗稱不理。

translations.literal: Yuancao lacked capacity for demanding affairs and was said to be negligent in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Yuancao lacked capacity for demanding affairs and was said to be negligent in administration.

sentences.zh: 上譴怒之，敕御史劾其事。

translations.literal: The sovereign rebuked and was angry with him, and ordered the censorate to impeach his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign rebuked him in anger and ordered the censorate to impeach his conduct.

sentences.zh: 由是出為金州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: For this he was sent out as Governor of Jin province and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was sent out as Governor of Jin province and died in office.

sentences.zh: 所著文集三十卷行於世，子元玉。

translations.literal: His collected writings in thirty juan circulated in the world; his son was Yuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings in thirty juan circulated in the world; his son was Yuanyu.

sentences.zh: 元操弟孝基，亦有才學，風詞甚美。

translations.literal: Yuancao's younger brother Xiaoji also had talent and learning, with beautiful literary style.
translations.idiomatic: Yuancao's younger brother Xiaoji also had talent and learning, with a beautiful literary style.

sentences.zh: 以衛尉丞待詔文林館，位儀曹郎中。

translations.literal: As Deputy Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he awaited appointment at the Forest of Literature Hall and rose to Gentleman in the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: As Deputy Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he awaited appointment at the Forest of Literature Hall and rose to Gentleman in the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 孝基弟孝俊，太子洗馬。

translations.literal: Xiaoji's younger brother Xiaojun, Groom of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji's younger brother Xiaojun served as Groom of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 孝俊弟孝威，字季重，涉學有器幹，兄弟之中，最為敦篤。

translations.literal: Xiaojun's younger brother Xiaowei, styled Jizhong, ranged through learning with capacity and resolve; among the brothers he was the most sincere and steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojun's younger brother Xiaowei, styled Jizhong, ranged through learning with capacity and resolve; among the brothers he was the most sincere and steadfast.

sentences.zh: 位太尉外兵參軍，修起居注。

translations.literal: He rose to Aide for External Military Affairs in the Grand Commandant's office and compiled the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Aide for External Military Affairs in the Grand Commandant's office and compiled the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，禮部侍郎、大理少卿。

translations.literal: Serving Sui, he was Vice Minister of Ceremonies and Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Sui, he was Vice Minister of Ceremonies and Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 式弟弈，字景世，美容貌，有才藝。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Yi, styled Jingshi, had a handsome appearance and artistic talent.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Yi, styled Jingshi, had a handsome appearance and artistic talent.

sentences.zh: 位都官尚書、安平侯，與兄敷同死。

translations.literal: He rose to Minister of Justice and Marquis of Anping, and died together with his elder brother Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Justice and Marquis of Anping, and died together with his elder brother Fu.

sentences.zh: 太和初，文明太后追念弈兄弟，及誅䐶，存問憲等一二家，歲時賜以布帛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe, Empress Dowager Wenming recalled Yi's brothers; and when Li Zhi was executed she inquired after one or two households such as Xian's, granting cloth and silk at the seasonal festivals.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe, Empress Dowager Wenming recalled Yi's brothers; and when Li Zhi was executed she inquired after one or two households such as Xian's, granting cloth and silk at the seasonal festivals.

sentences.zh: 弈弟冏，字道度，少為中散，逃避得免。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Jiong, styled Daodu, while young served as Central Scattered Courtier and escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Jiong, styled Daodu, while young served as Central Scattered Courtier and escaped by flight.

sentences.zh: 後歷位度支尚書。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served in succession as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 太和二十一年，孝文幸長安，冏以咸陽山河險固，秦、漢舊都，勸帝去洛陽都之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taihe, Emperor Xiaowen visited Chang'an; Jiong urged the emperor to leave Luoyang and make it his capital, citing Xianyang's mountains and rivers as perilously secure and its status as the old capital of Qin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Taihe, Emperor Xiaowen visited Chang'an; Jiong urged the emperor to abandon Luoyang and establish the capital there, citing Xianyang's mountains and rivers as perilously secure and its status as the old capital of Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 後孝文引見冏，笑謂曰：「昔婁敬一說，漢祖即日西駕。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowen summoned Jiong and said with a smile: "In former times, when Lou Jing spoke but once, the Han Founder that very day drove westward.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xiaowen summoned Jiong and said with a smile, "In former times, when Lou Jing spoke but once, the Han Founder that very day drove westward.

sentences.zh: 尚書今以西京說朕，使朕不廢東轅。

translations.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing urged me with the western capital, keeping me from abandoning my eastern journey.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Masters of Writing urged me with the western capital, keeping me from abandoning my eastern journey.

sentences.zh: 當是獻可理殊，所以今古相反耳。

translations.literal: This must be that 'presenting what is acceptable' rests on different principles—hence ancient and modern run counter to each other.
translations.idiomatic: This must be that 'presenting what is acceptable' rests on different principles—hence ancient and modern run counter to each other.

sentences.zh: 」冏曰：「昔漢祖起於布衣，欲藉險以自固，婁敬之言，符於本旨。

translations.literal: " Jiong said: "In former times the Han Founder rose from the cloth-wearing people and wished to rely on perilous terrain to secure himself; Lou Jing's words matched his original intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiong said, "In former times the Han Founder rose from common cloth and wished to rely on perilous terrain to secure himself; Lou Jing's words matched his original intent.

sentences.zh: 今陛下德洽四海，事同隆周，是以愚臣獻說，不能上動。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's virtue pervades all within the four seas and your affairs are like those of the flourishing Zhou—therefore this foolish subject's presentation could not move you above.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's virtue pervades all within the four seas and your affairs are like those of the flourishing Zhou—therefore this foolish subject's presentation could not move you above.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 冏性鯁烈，敢直言，常面折孝文，彈駁公卿，無所回避，百寮皆憚之。

translations.literal: Jiong's nature was blunt and fierce; he dared speak directly, often rebuking Emperor Xiaowen to his face and impeaching dukes and ministers without avoidance—all the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's nature was blunt and fierce; he dared speak directly, often rebuking Emperor Xiaowen to his face and impeaching dukes and ministers without evasion—all the hundred officials feared him.

sentences.zh: 孝文常加優禮，每車駕巡幸，恆兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen often treated him with special honor; whenever the imperial carriage toured, Jiong regularly served concurrently as Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen often treated him with special honor; whenever the imperial carriage toured, Jiong regularly served concurrently as Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 雖才學不及諸兄，然公強當世，堪濟過之。

translations.literal: Although his talent and learning did not match his elder brothers, in public strength for his age he surpassed them in capacity to save the times.
translations.idiomatic: Although his talent and learning did not match his elder brothers, in public strength for his age he surpassed them in capacity to meet the needs of the times.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子祐，字長禧，篤穆友于，見稱於世。

translations.literal: His son You, styled Changxi, was sincere, dignified, and fraternal, and was praised by the world.
translations.idiomatic: His son You, styled Changxi, was sincere, dignified, and fraternal, and was praised by the world.

sentences.zh: 歷位給事中，累遷博陵太守，所在亦以清幹著。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Attendant at the Court, was promoted repeatedly to Administrator of Boling, and wherever he served was also known for integrity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Attendant at the Court, was promoted repeatedly to Administrator of Boling, and wherever he served was also known for integrity and competence.

sentences.zh: 順弟修基，陳留太守，卒。

translations.literal: Shun's younger brother Xiuji, Administrator of Chenliu, died.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's younger brother Xiuji, Administrator of Chenliu, died.

sentences.zh: 子探幽，高平太守。

translations.literal: His son TanYou, Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: His son TanYou served as Administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 探幽兄子洪鸞，河間太守。

translations.literal: Tanyou's elder brother's son Hongluan, Administrator of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Tanyou's elder brother's son Hongluan served as Administrator of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 李孝伯，高平公順從父弟也。

translations.literal: Li Xiaobo was a younger male cousin of Duke of Gaoping Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaobo was a younger male cousin of Duke of Gaoping Shun.

sentences.zh: 父曾，少以鄭氏《禮》、《左氏春秋》教授為業。

translations.literal: His father Zeng in his youth made his profession teaching the Zheng school's Rites and the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zeng in his youth made his profession teaching the Zheng school's Rites and the Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 郡三辟功曹，並不就，曰：「功曹之職，雖曰鄉選高第，猶是郡吏耳；

translations.literal: The commandery thrice summoned him as Merit Officer, but he never accepted, saying: "The office of Merit Officer, though called the highest selection of the district, is still a commandery clerk;
translations.idiomatic: The commandery thrice summoned him as Merit Officer, but he never accepted, saying, "The office of Merit Officer, though called the highest selection of the district, is still a commandery clerk;

sentences.zh: 北面事人，亦何容易。

translations.literal: to face north and serve another—how easily done is that?
translations.idiomatic: to face north and serve another—how easily done is that?

sentences.zh: 」州辟主簿，到官月餘，乃歎曰：「梁敬叔雲'州郡之職，徒勞人耳'。

translations.literal: " The province summoned him as Chief Clerk; after little more than a month in office he sighed and said: "Liang Jingshu said, 'Provincial and commandery offices are nothing but toil for men.'
translations.idiomatic: " The province summoned him as Chief Clerk; after little more than a month in office he sighed and said, "Liang Jingshu said, 'Provincial and commandery offices are nothing but toil for men.'

sentences.zh: 道之不行，身之憂也。

translations.literal: When the Way does not prevail, it is one's own worry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Way does not prevail, it is one's own worry.

sentences.zh: 」遂還家講授。

translations.literal: " So he returned home and devoted himself to teaching.
translations.idiomatic: " So he returned home and devoted himself to teaching.

sentences.zh: 道武時，為趙郡太守，令行禁止。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Daowu he served as Administrator of Zhao commandery; his orders were enforced and prohibitions observed.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Daowu's reign he served as Administrator of Zhao commandery, where his orders were enforced and prohibitions observed.

sentences.zh: 并州丁零數為山東害，知曾能得百姓死力，憚不入境。

translations.literal: Dingling of Bing province often harmed Shandong; knowing Zeng could obtain the people's utmost loyalty, they feared and did not enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Dingling from Bing province often plundered Shandong; knowing Zeng could elicit the people's utmost loyalty, they feared to enter his territory.

sentences.zh: 賊於常山界得一死鹿，賊長謂趙郡地也，責之，還令送鹿故處。

translations.literal: Bandits on the border of Changshan commandery obtained a dead deer; the bandit chief said it was Zhao commandery territory, rebuked them, and ordered the deer sent back to its original place.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits obtained a dead deer on the border of Changshan commandery; the bandit chief said it was Zhao commandery territory, rebuked them, and ordered the deer returned to where it had been.

sentences.zh: 郡謠曰：「詐作趙郡鹿，猶勝常山粟。

translations.literal: A commandery rhyme said: "Feigning a deer from Zhao commandery is still better than grain from Changshan.
