translations.idiomatic: A commandery rhyme ran, "Feigning a deer from Zhao commandery is still better than grain from Changshan.

sentences.zh: 」其見憚如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the fear in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the fear in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈荊州刺史、柏仁子，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Governor of Jing province and Viscount of Boren, with the posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Governor of Jing province and Viscount of Boren, with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 孝伯少傳父業，博綜群言，美風儀，動有法度。

translations.literal: Xiaobo in youth inherited his father's profession, mastered diverse learning, had fine bearing, and in his movements observed proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo in youth inherited his father's profession, mastered diverse learning, had fine bearing, and in his movements observed proper measure.

sentences.zh: 從兄言之太武，徵為中散，謂曰「真卿家千里駒也」。

translations.literal: A male cousin of his father's generation spoke of him to Emperor Taiwu; he was summoned as Central Scattered Courtier, and the emperor said, "Truly a thousand-league colt of the Li household."
translations.idiomatic: A male cousin of his father's generation spoke of him to Emperor Taiwu; he was summoned as Central Scattered Courtier, and the emperor said, "Truly a thousand-league colt of the Li household."

sentences.zh: 遷秘書奏事中散，轉散騎侍郎、光祿大夫，賜爵魏昌子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Central Scattered Courtier in attendance at the Secretariat, then became Attendant Gentleman at the Palace Mounted Guard and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and was granted the title Viscount of Weichang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Central Scattered Courtier in attendance at the Secretariat, then became Attendant Gentleman at the Palace Mounted Guard and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and was granted the title Viscount of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 以軍國機密，甚見親寵，謀謨切秘，時人莫能知。

translations.literal: Because of military and state secrets he was greatly favored and trusted; his stratagems were closely guarded, and people of the time could not know them.
translations.idiomatic: Because of military and state secrets he was greatly favored and trusted; his stratagems were closely guarded, and people of the time could not know them.

sentences.zh: 遷北部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Northern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the Northern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 以頻從征伐規略之功，進爵壽光侯。

translations.literal: For repeated merit in following campaigns in strategy and planning, he was advanced to Marquis of Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated merit in following campaigns in strategy and planning, he was advanced to Marquis of Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 真君末，宋文帝聞車駕南伐，遣其弟太尉、江夏王義恭率眾赴彭城。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenjun era, Emperor Wen of Song heard that the imperial carriage was campaigning south and sent his younger brother the Grand Commandant, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, to lead troops to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenjun era, Emperor Wen of Song heard that the imperial carriage was campaigning south and sent his younger brother the Grand Commandant, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, to lead troops to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 太武至彭城，登亞父塚以望城內，遣送其俘蒯應至小市門，宣詔勞問。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu reached Pengcheng, climbed the mound of the Second Father to view the city within, and had his captive Kuai Ying sent to the Small Market Gate to proclaim an edict of consolation and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu reached Pengcheng, climbed the mound of the Second Father to view the city within, and had his captive Kuai Ying sent to the Small Market Gate to proclaim an edict of consolation and inquiry.

sentences.zh: 義恭等問應士馬數，曰：「中軍四十餘萬。

translations.literal: Yigong and the others asked Ying the number of men and horses; he said, "The central army numbers more than four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong and the others asked Ying the number of men and horses; he said, "The central army numbers more than four hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 」宋徐州刺史武陵王駿遣人獻酒二器、甘蔗百挺，並請駱駝。

translations.literal: " The Song Governor of Xu province, Prince of Wuling Jun, sent men with two vessels of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane, and also requested camels.
translations.idiomatic: " The Song Governor of Xu province, Prince of Wuling Jun, sent men with two vessels of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane, and also requested camels.

sentences.zh: 帝明旦復登亞父塚，遣孝伯至小市門，駿亦使其長史張暢對。

translations.literal: The next morning the emperor again climbed the mound of the Second Father and sent Xiaobo to the Small Market Gate; Jun likewise had his Chief Clerk Zhang Chang respond.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the emperor again climbed the mound of the Second Father and sent Xiaobo to the Small Market Gate; Jun likewise had his Chief Clerk Zhang Chang respond.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「主上有詔詔太尉、安北，可暫出門，欲與相見。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said, "The sovereign has an edict for the Grand Commandant and Pacifier of the North: you may come briefly outside the gate—he wishes to meet you.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "The sovereign has an edict for the Grand Commandant and Pacifier of the North: you may come briefly outside the gate—he wishes to meet you.

sentences.zh: 今遣賜駱駝及貂裘雜物。

translations.literal: He now sends camels, sable fur robes, and various goods as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He now sends camels, sable fur robes, and various goods as gifts.

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「有詔之言，何得稱之於此？

translations.literal: " Chang said, "Words of an edict—how can they be spoken here?
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "Words of an edict—how can they be spoken here?

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「卿家太尉、安北是人臣不？

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said, "Are your household's Grand Commandant and Pacifier of the North subjects or not?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo said, "Are your household's Grand Commandant and Pacifier of the North subjects or not?

sentences.zh: 縱為鄰國之君，何為不稱詔於鄰國之臣？

translations.literal: Even if they are rulers of a neighboring state, why not speak of an edict to subjects of a neighboring state?
translations.idiomatic: Even if they are rulers of a neighboring state, why not speak of an edict to subjects of a neighboring state?

sentences.zh: 又何至杜門絕橋？

translations.literal: And why go so far as to shut the gates and cut off the bridge?
translations.idiomatic: And why go so far as to shut the gates and cut off the bridge?

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「二王以魏帝營壘未立，此精甲十萬，恐輕相陵踐，故且閉城。

translations.literal: " Chang said, "The two princes, because the Wei emperor's camps are not yet established and they have a hundred thousand picked armored troops here, fear a rash crossing and violation, and therefore for the time being closed the city.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "The two princes, because the Wei emperor's camps are not yet established and they have a hundred thousand picked armored troops here, fear a rash crossing and violation, and therefore for the time being closed the city.

sentences.zh: 待彼休息兵士，然後共修戰場，克日交戲。

translations.literal: When their troops have rested, they will then jointly prepare the battlefield and fix a day for combat.
translations.idiomatic: When their troops have rested, they will then jointly prepare the battlefield and fix a day for combat.

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「令行禁止，主將常事，何用廢橋杜門？

translations.literal: " Xiaobo said, "Orders enforced and prohibitions observed—these are ordinary matters for a commanding general; why demolish bridges and shut gates?
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaobo said, "Orders enforced and prohibitions observed—these are ordinary matters for a commanding general; why demolish bridges and shut gates?

sentences.zh: 復何以十萬誇大？

translations.literal: And why boast of a hundred thousand?
translations.idiomatic: And why boast of a hundred thousand?

sentences.zh: 我亦有良馬百萬，復可以此相矜。

translations.literal: We too have a million fine horses—we could likewise boast of this.
translations.idiomatic: We too have a million fine horses—we could likewise boast of this.

sentences.zh: 」既開門，暢屏人卻仗，出受賜物。

translations.literal: " Once the gates were opened, Chang dismissed attendants and sheathed weapons and came out to receive the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: " Once the gates were opened, Chang dismissed attendants and sheathed weapons and came out to receive the gifts.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「詔以貂裘賜太尉，駱駝騾馬賜安北。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said, "By edict the sable fur robe is granted to the Grand Commandant, and camels, mules, and horses to the Pacifier of the North.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "By edict the sable fur robe is granted to the Grand Commandant, and camels, mules, and horses to the Pacifier of the North.

sentences.zh: 」義恭獻皮袴褶一具，駿奉酒二器、甘蔗百挺。

translations.literal: " Yigong presented one set of leather trousers and jacket; Jun offered two vessels of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane.
translations.idiomatic: " Yigong presented one set of leather trousers and jacket; Jun offered two vessels of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane.

sentences.zh: 帝又遣賜義恭、駿等氈各一領，鹽各九種，並胡豉。

translations.literal: The emperor also sent gifts of one felt rug each for Yigong, Jun, and the others, nine kinds of salt each, and fermented bean paste from the north.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent gifts of one felt rug each for Yigong, Jun, and the others, nine kinds of salt each, and fermented bean paste from the north.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「有後詔：凡此諸鹽，各有所宜。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said, "There is a follow-up edict: each of these salts has its proper use.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "There is a follow-up edict: each of these salts has its proper use.

sentences.zh: 白鹽食鹽，主上自所食；

translations.literal: White salt and table salt are what the sovereign himself eats;
translations.idiomatic: White salt and table salt are what the sovereign himself eats;

sentences.zh: 黑鹽療腹脹氣滿，末之六銖，以酒而服；

translations.literal: black salt treats abdominal distension and gas fullness—grind six zhu of it and take it in wine;
translations.idiomatic: black salt treats abdominal distension and gas fullness—grind six zhu of it and take it in wine;

sentences.zh: 胡鹽療目痛；

translations.literal: Hu salt treats eye pain;
translations.idiomatic: Hu salt treats eye pain;

sentences.zh: 戎鹽療諸瘡；

translations.literal: Rong salt treats various sores;
translations.idiomatic: Rong salt treats various sores;

sentences.zh: 赤鹽、駁鹽、臭鹽、馬齒鹽四種，並非食鹽。

translations.literal: the four kinds red salt, variegated salt, foul salt, and horse-tooth salt are none of them table salt.
translations.idiomatic: the four kinds red salt, variegated salt, foul salt, and horse-tooth salt are none of them table salt.

sentences.zh: 太尉、安北，何不遣人來至朕間，見朕小大，知朕老少，觀朕為人？

translations.literal: Grand Commandant, Pacifier of the North—why not send someone to my quarters to see how large or small I am, know whether I am young or old, and observe what manner of man I am?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant, Pacifier of the North—why not send someone to my quarters to see how large or small I am, know whether I am young or old, and observe what manner of man I am?

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「魏帝為人，久為往來所具，故不復遣信。

translations.literal: " Chang said, "What manner of man the Wei emperor is has long been fully known through mutual visits, and therefore we do not send envoys again.
translations.idiomatic: " Chang said, "What manner of man the Wei emperor is has long been fully known through mutual visits, and therefore we do not send envoys again.

sentences.zh: 」義恭獻蠟燭十挺，駿獻錦一匹。

translations.literal: " Yigong presented ten stalks of wax candles; Jun presented one bolt of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: " Yigong presented ten stalks of wax candles; Jun presented one bolt of brocade.

sentences.zh: 孝伯風容閒雅，應答如流，暢及左右甚相嗟歎。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's bearing was easy and elegant; his replies flowed smoothly, and Chang and those around him greatly marveled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's bearing was easy and elegant; his replies flowed smoothly, and Chang and those around him greatly marveled.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，進爵宣城公。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and advanced his rank to Duke of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and advanced his rank to Duke of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 為使持節、散騎常侍、秦州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He served as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant at the Palace Mounted Guard, and Governor of Qin province, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant at the Palace Mounted Guard, and Governor of Qin province, then died.

sentences.zh: 贈征南大將軍、定州刺史，諡曰文昭公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand General Who Expands the South and Governor of Ding province, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand General Who Expands the South and Governor of Ding province, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhao.

sentences.zh: 孝伯體度恢雅，明達政事，朝野貴賤，咸推重之。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's physique and bearing were grand and refined; he was clear and penetrating in state affairs, and nobles and commoners throughout court and countryside all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's physique and bearing were grand and refined; he was clear and penetrating in state affairs, and nobles and commoners throughout court and countryside all esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 景穆曾啟太武，廣征俊秀，帝曰：「朕有一孝伯，足理天下，何用多為？

translations.literal: Jingmu once memorialized Emperor Taiwu to widely summon outstanding talent; the emperor said, "I have one Xiaobo—enough to order the realm; why gather many?
translations.idiomatic: Jingmu once memorialized Emperor Taiwu to widely summon outstanding talent; the emperor said, "I have one Xiaobo—enough to order the realm; why gather many?

sentences.zh: 假復求訪，此人輩亦何可得？

translations.literal: Even if we search further, how could men of this sort be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Even if we search further, how could men of this sort be obtained?

sentences.zh: 」其見貴如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 性方慎忠厚，每朝廷事有所不足，必手自書表，切言陳諫。

translations.literal: His nature was upright, cautious, and loyal-thorough; whenever something in court affairs fell short, he inevitably wrote a memorial himself and offered candid remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was upright, cautious, and loyal-thorough; whenever something in court affairs fell short, he inevitably wrote a memorial himself and offered candid remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 或不從者，至於再三，削滅槁草，家人不見。

translations.literal: If it was not followed, he might do so two or three times; he destroyed the draft straw and his family never saw it.
translations.idiomatic: If it was not followed, he might do so two or three times; he destroyed the draft straw and his family never saw it.

sentences.zh: 公廷論議，常引綱紀。

translations.literal: In public court discussion he constantly appealed to the governing principles.
translations.idiomatic: In public court discussion he constantly appealed to the governing principles.

sentences.zh: 或有言事者，孝伯恣其所陳，假有是非，終不抑折。

translations.literal: When someone spoke on affairs, Xiaobo let them state what they would; even if there were right and wrong, he never suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When someone spoke on affairs, Xiaobo let them state what they would; even if there were right and wrong, he never suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 及見帝，言其所長，初不隱人姓名，以為已善。

translations.literal: When he saw the emperor he spoke of others' strengths, never concealing people's names to claim credit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the emperor he spoke of others' strengths, never concealing people's names to claim credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 故衣冠之士，服其雅正。

translations.literal: Therefore men of the gentry admired his refined integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore men of the gentry admired his refined integrity.

sentences.zh: 自崔浩誅後，軍國謀謨，咸出孝伯。

translations.literal: After Cui Hao's execution, military and state stratagems all issued from Xiaobo.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Hao's execution, military and state stratagems all issued from Xiaobo.

sentences.zh: 太武寵眷，有亞於浩，亦以宰輔遇之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu's favor for him was second only to that for Hao, and he was treated as a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu's favor for him was second only to that for Hao, and he was treated as a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 獻替補闕，其跡不見，時人莫得而知。

translations.literal: His contributions and corrections leave no visible trace; people of the time could not know them.
translations.idiomatic: His contributions and corrections leave no visible trace; people of the time could not know them.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，遠近哀傷焉。

translations.literal: On the day he died, near and far mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, near and far mourned him.

sentences.zh: 孝伯美名，聞於遐邇。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's fine reputation was heard far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's fine reputation was heard far and near.

sentences.zh: 李彪使江南，齊武帝謂曰：「北有李孝伯，于卿遠近？

translations.literal: When Li Biao went on embassy to Jiangnan, Emperor Wu of Qi said to him, "In the north there is Li Xiaobo—how does he compare with you in rank?
translations.idiomatic: When Li Biao went on embassy to Jiangnan, Emperor Wu of Qi said to him, "In the north there is Li Xiaobo—how does he compare with you in rank?

sentences.zh: 」其為遠人所知若此。

translations.literal: " Such was his renown among distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was his renown among distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 其妻崔賾女，高明婦人，生一子元顯。

translations.literal: His wife was a daughter of Cui Yan, a capable woman; she bore one son, Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was a daughter of Cui Yan, a capable woman; she bore one son, Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 崔氏卒後納翟氏，不以為妻，憎忌元顯。

translations.literal: After the Cui clan wife died he took in Lady Zhai but did not make her his wife; she resented and envied Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: After the Cui clan wife died he took in Lady Zhai but did not make her his wife; she resented and envied Yuanxian.

sentences.zh: 後遇劫，元顯見害，世雲翟氏所為也。

translations.literal: Later during a robbery Yuanxian was killed; the world said it was the work of Lady Zhai.
translations.idiomatic: Later during a robbery Yuanxian was killed; the world said it was the work of Lady Zhai.

sentences.zh: 元顯志氣甚高，為時人所傷惜。

translations.literal: Yuanxian's spirit and ambition were very high, and people of the time mourned him with regret.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian's spirit and ambition were very high, and people of the time mourned him with regret.

sentences.zh: 翟氏二子，安人、安上，並有風度。

translations.literal: Lady Zhai's two sons, Anren and Anshang, both had fine bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhai's two sons, Anren and Anshang, both had fine bearing.

sentences.zh: 安人襲爵壽光侯，司徒司馬。

translations.literal: Anren inherited the title Marquis of Shouguang and served as Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Anren inherited the title Marquis of Shouguang and served as Chief Clerk to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son and the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son and the title was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 安上钜鹿太守，亦早卒。

translations.literal: Anshang was Administrator of Julu and also died young.
translations.idiomatic: Anshang was Administrator of Julu and also died young.

sentences.zh: 安人第豹子後追理先封，卒不得襲。

translations.literal: Anren's younger brother Baozi's descendants later pursued restoration of the earlier enfeoffment but in the end could not inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Anren's younger brother Baozi's descendants later pursued restoration of the earlier enfeoffment but in the end could not inherit.

sentences.zh: 孝伯兄祥，字元善。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's elder brother Xiang, styled Yuanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's elder brother Xiang, styled Yuanshan.

sentences.zh: 學傳家業，鄉党宗之。

translations.literal: He inherited the family's scholarly profession and his district honored him.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the family's scholarly profession and his district honored him.

sentences.zh: 位中書博士。

translations.literal: He held the post of Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時尚書韓元興率眾出青州，以祥為軍司。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of the Masters of Writing Han Yuanying led troops out from Qing province and made Xiang Army Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister of the Masters of Writing Han Yuanying led troops out from Qing province and made Xiang Army Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 略地至陳、汝，淮北之人詣軍降者七千餘戶，遷之兗、豫之南，置淮陽郡以撫之。

translations.literal: They seized territory as far as Chen and Ru; more than seven thousand households of people north of the Hu came to the army to surrender; they were moved south of Yan and Yu, and Huaiyang commandery was established to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: They seized territory as far as Chen and Ru; more than seven thousand households of people north of the Hu came to the army to surrender; they were moved south of Yan and Yu, and Huaiyang commandery was established to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 拜祥太守，流人歸者萬餘家，百姓安業。

translations.literal: Xiang was appointed Administrator; more than ten thousand refugee households returned, and the people settled in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was appointed Administrator; more than ten thousand refugee households returned, and the people settled in peace.

sentences.zh: 遷河間太守，有威恩之稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Hejian and was known for authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrator of Hejian and was known for authority and kindness.

sentences.zh: 徵拜中書侍郎，人有千餘上書，乞留數年，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; more than a thousand people submitted petitions asking that he be kept several years; the court did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; more than a thousand people submitted petitions asking that he be kept several years; the court did not consent.

sentences.zh: 卒官，追贈定州刺史、平棘子，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously granted Governor of Ding province and Viscount of Pingji, with the posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously granted Governor of Ding province and Viscount of Pingji, with the posthumous title Xian.

sentences.zh: 子安世，幼聰悟。

translations.literal: His son Anshi was intelligent and perceptive from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anshi was intelligent and perceptive from childhood.

sentences.zh: 興安二年，文成帝引見侍郎、博士子，簡其秀俊，欲以為中書學生。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xing'an, Emperor Wencheng summoned the sons of Attendants and Erudites, selected the outstanding among them, and wished to make them students of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xing'an, Emperor Wencheng summoned the sons of Attendants and Erudites, selected the outstanding among them, and wished to make them students of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安世年十一，帝見其尚小，引問之。

translations.literal: Anshi was eleven; the emperor saw he was still young and questioned him directly.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was eleven; the emperor saw he was still young and questioned him directly.

sentences.zh: 安世陳說父祖，甚有次第，即以為生。

translations.literal: Anshi set forth his father and forefathers with good order and was immediately made a student.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi set forth his father and forefathers with good order and was immediately made a student.

sentences.zh: 帝每幸國學，恆獨被引問。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor visited the National Academy, Anshi alone was regularly questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor visited the National Academy, Anshi alone was regularly questioned.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「汝但守此至大，不慮不富貴。

translations.literal: An edict said, "If you only preserve this to maturity, you need not worry about lacking wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "If you only preserve this to maturity, you need not worry about lacking wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 」天安初，拜中散，以謹慎，帝親愛之。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Tian'an he was appointed Central Scattered Courtier; because of his prudence the emperor personally favored him.
translations.idiomatic: " At the beginning of Tian'an he was appointed Central Scattered Courtier; because of his prudence the emperor personally favored him.

sentences.zh: 累遷主客令。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Director of Receiving Guests.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Director of Receiving Guests.

sentences.zh: 齊使劉纘朝貢，安世奉詔勞之。

translations.literal: When Qi sent Liu Zuan to pay court tribute, Anshi received edict to greet and console him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi sent Liu Zuan to pay court tribute, Anshi received edict to greet and console him.

sentences.zh: 安世美容貌，善舉止，纘等自相謂曰：「不有君子，其能國乎！

translations.literal: Anshi had fine looks and graceful bearing; Zuan and the others said among themselves, "Without such gentlemen, how could a state endure!
translations.idiomatic: Anshi had fine looks and graceful bearing; Zuan and the others said among themselves, "Without such gentlemen, how could a state endure!

sentences.zh: 」纘等呼安世為典客。

translations.literal: " Zuan and the others called Anshi Director of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan and the others called Anshi Director of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 安世曰：「何以亡秦之官，稱于上國？

translations.literal: Anshi said, "Why use an office title from the perished Qin to address one in a superior state?
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said, "Why use an office title from the perished Qin to address one in a superior state?

sentences.zh: 」纘曰：「世異之號，凡有幾也？

translations.literal: " Zuan said, "Titles differ from age to age—how many can there be altogether?
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan said, "Titles differ from age to age—how many can there be altogether?

sentences.zh: 」安世曰：「周謂掌客，秦改典客，漢名鴻臚，今曰主客。

translations.literal: " Anshi said, "Zhou called it Director of Receiving Guests; Qin changed it to Director of Ceremonies; Han named it Grand Master of Ceremonial; now it is Director of Receiving Guests.
translations.idiomatic: " Anshi said, "Zhou called it Director of Receiving Guests; Qin changed it to Director of Ceremonies; Han named it Grand Master of Ceremonial; now it is Director of Receiving Guests.

sentences.zh: 君等不欲影響文、武，而殷勤亡秦。

translations.literal: You gentlemen do not wish to echo Wen and Wu, yet warmly invoke the perished Qin.
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen do not wish to echo Wen and Wu, yet warmly invoke the perished Qin.

sentences.zh: 」纘又指方山曰：「此山去燕然遠近？

translations.literal: " Zuan again pointed to Mount Fang and said, "How far is this mountain from Mount Yanran?
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan again pointed to Mount Fang and said, "How far is this mountain from Mount Yanran?

sentences.zh: 」安世曰：「亦石頭之與番禺耳。」

translations.literal: " Anshi said, "About the same distance as from Shitou to Panyu."
translations.idiomatic: " Anshi said, "About the same distance as from Shitou to Panyu."

sentences.zh: 時每有江南使至，多出藏內珍物，令都下富室好容服者貨之，令使任情交易。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys came from Jiangnan, many rare goods from the inner treasury were brought out, and wealthy families in the capital who loved fine dress were allowed to sell to them, letting the envoys trade as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys came from Jiangnan, many rare goods from the inner treasury were brought out, and wealthy families in the capital who loved fine dress were allowed to sell to them, letting the envoys trade as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 使至金玉肆問價，纘曰：「北方金玉大賤，當是山川所出？

translations.literal: When the envoy came to a gold and jade shop to ask prices, Zuan said, "Gold and jade are so cheap in the north—they must come from the mountains and rivers?
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy came to a gold and jade shop to ask prices, Zuan said, "Gold and jade are so cheap in the north—they must come from the mountains and rivers?

sentences.zh: 」安世曰：「聖朝不貴金玉，所以同於瓦礫；

translations.literal: " Anshi said, "Our sage dynasty does not prize gold and jade, and therefore treats them the same as tiles and rubble;
translations.idiomatic: " Anshi said, "Our sage dynasty does not prize gold and jade, and therefore treats them the same as tiles and rubble;

sentences.zh: 又皇上德通神明，山不愛寶，故川無金，山無玉。

translations.literal: Moreover, our emperor's virtue reaches through to the spirits; the mountains do not hoard their treasures, and therefore the rivers have no gold and the mountains have no jade.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, our emperor's virtue communes with the spirits; the mountains withhold no treasure—thus the rivers hold no gold and the mountains hold no jade.

sentences.zh: 」纘初將大市，得安世言，慚而罷。

translations.literal: " At first Zuan was about to hold a great market, but when he heard Anshi's words he withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: " At first Zuan had planned a grand market, but when he heard Anshi's reply he withdrew in shame and abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 遷主客給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant in the Office of Receiving Guests.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant in the Office of Receiving Guests.

sentences.zh: 時人困饑流散，豪右多有占奪，安世乃上疏陳均量之制，孝文深納之。

translations.literal: At the time the people were afflicted by famine and scattered in flight; powerful families often seized and usurped land. Anshi submitted a memorial setting forth a system of equal measurement, and Emperor Xiaowen deeply adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The people were then suffering famine and dispersing in flight, while powerful families seized and appropriated land on every side. Anshi submitted a memorial proposing a system of equal land measurement, and Emperor Xiaowen embraced it wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 後均田之制，起於此矣。

translations.literal: Later the equal-field system arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: It was from this that the equal-field system would later take shape.

sentences.zh: 出為相州刺史，假趙郡公。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Xiang province, with provisional title Duke of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Xiang province and granted the provisional title Duke of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 敦農桑，斷淫祀。

translations.literal: He promoted agriculture and sericulture and abolished illicit shrines.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged farming and sericulture and suppressed unauthorized cults.

sentences.zh: 西門豹、史起有功於人者，為之修飾廟堂。

translations.literal: For Ximen Bao and Shi Qi, who had rendered service to the people, he had their temple halls refurbished.
translations.idiomatic: For Ximen Bao and Shi Qi, men who had served the people well, he restored and adorned their temple halls.

sentences.zh: 表薦廣平宋翻、陽平路恃慶，皆為朝廷善士。

translations.literal: In memorials he recommended Song Fan of Guangping and Lu Shiqing of Yangping, both worthy men of the court.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court recommending Song Fan of Guangping and Lu Shiqing of Yangping, both men of sterling character.

sentences.zh: 初，廣平人李波宗族強盛，殘掠不已，前刺史薛道舣親往討之，大為波敗，遂為逋逃之藪，公私成患。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Bo of Guangping had a powerful clan that ceaselessly plundered and ravaged. The previous governor Xue Daoyi went in person to attack him but suffered a great defeat at Bo's hands; the region became a refuge for fugitives, an affliction to public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man of Guangping named Li Bo had built a powerful clan that plundered without cease. The previous governor, Xue Daoyi, led a personal campaign against him but was routed; the area became a haven for fugitives and a plague on officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 百姓語曰：「李波小妹字雍容，褰裙逐馬如卷蓬。

translations.literal: The people had a saying: "Li Bo's young sister, styled Yongrong, lifts her skirt chasing horses like rolling grass.
translations.idiomatic: The people had a rhyme: "Li Bo's little sister, styled Yongrong, lifts her skirts chasing horses like wind-blown grass.

sentences.zh: 左射右射必疊雙，婦女尚如此，男子那可逢！

translations.literal: Shoot left, shoot right—she always hits pairs; if the women are like this, how can men be faced!
translations.idiomatic: Left bow, right bow—she never misses a pair! If the women are like this, what man dare cross them!

sentences.zh: 」安世設方略，誘波及諸子侄三十餘人，斬於鄴市，州內肅然。

translations.literal: " Anshi devised a stratagem, lured Bo and more than thirty of his sons and nephews, and executed them in the market at Ye; the province became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: " Anshi laid a plan, lured Bo and more than thirty of his sons and nephews into a trap, and had them beheaded in the market at Ye. The province was restored to order.

sentences.zh: 病卒於家。

translations.literal: He died of illness at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at home.

sentences.zh: 安世妻博陵崔氏，生一子枿。

translations.literal: Anshi's wife was Lady Cui of Boling; she bore one son, Nie.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi's wife was Lady Cui of Boling, who bore him one son, Nie.

sentences.zh: 崔氏以妒悍見出，又尚滄水公主，生二子，諡、鬱。

translations.literal: Lady Cui was divorced for jealousy and fierce temper; he then married the Princess of Cangshui, who bore two sons, Shi and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui was cast out for jealousy and a violent temper. Anshi then married the Princess of Cangshui, who bore two sons, Shi and Yu.

sentences.zh: 枿字琚羅，涉歷史傳，頗有文才，氣尚豪爽，公強當世。

translations.literal: Nie, styled Jurong, had read broadly in histories and chronicles; he had considerable literary talent, a spirit inclined to bold generosity, and was forthright and forceful in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Nie, styled Jurong, had steeped himself in histories and chronicles and possessed real literary gifts. His temperament was bold and open, and he was known throughout his age for his uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 太師、高陽王雍表薦枿為友。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor, Prince Gao of Gaoyang, recommended Nie in memorial as Companion.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, Prince Gao of Gaoyang, memorialized the throne recommending Nie as Companion.

sentences.zh: 時人多絕戶為沙門，枿上言：「三千之罪，莫大於不孝，不孝之大，無過於絕祀。

translations.literal: At the time many people cut off their households to become monks; Nie submitted a memorial: "Of the three thousand offenses, none is greater than lack of filial piety; of the enormities of unfilial conduct, none surpasses ending one's line of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Many at the time were abandoning their households to become monks. Nie submitted a memorial: "Of the three thousand offenses, none is greater than unfilial piety; of all forms of unfilial conduct, none surpasses cutting off the ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 安得輕縱背禮之情，而肆其向法之意；

translations.literal: How can one lightly indulge feelings that turn against ritual, and give free rein to inclinations that look toward the Dharma;
translations.idiomatic: How can one lightly indulge impulses that violate ritual, and give free rein to inclinations that turn toward the Dharma;

sentences.zh: 缺當世之禮，而求將來之益；

translations.literal: neglect the ritual of the present age while seeking benefit in times to come;
translations.idiomatic: neglect the duties of the present age while chasing benefits in lives to come;

sentences.zh: 棄堂堂之政，而從鬼教乎？

translations.literal: abandon the august governance of the state and follow the ghostly teaching?
translations.idiomatic: abandon the august governance of the realm and submit to a doctrine of ghosts?

sentences.zh: 」沙門都統僧暹等忿枿鬼教之言，以枿為謗毀佛法，泣訴靈太后。

translations.literal: " The Chief Superintendent of monks, Sengxian, and others resented Nie's words calling it ghostly teaching; they accused Nie of slandering and destroying the Buddhist law and tearfully appealed to Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: " The Chief Superintendent of monks, Sengxian, and others, incensed by Nie's reference to a "ghostly teaching," accused him of slandering and destroying the Buddhist law and tearfully appealed to Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 責之，枿自理曰：「鬼神之名皆是通靈達稱。

translations.literal: Rebuked, Nie defended himself: "The names of ghosts and spirits are all terms for communion with the numinous.
translations.idiomatic: When rebuked, Nie defended himself: "The names of ghosts and spirits are all terms denoting communion with the numinous realm.

sentences.zh: 佛非天非地，本出於人，名之為鬼，愚謂非謗。

translations.literal: The Buddha is neither Heaven nor Earth—originally he came forth from men; to call him a ghost, I think, is not slander.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha is neither Heaven nor Earth; he arose from among men. To call him a ghost, in my humble view, is not slander.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后雖以枿言為允，然不免暹等意，猶罰枿金一兩。

translations.literal: " Though Empress Dowager Ling regarded Nie's words as reasonable, she could not set aside Sengxian and the others' feelings, and still fined Nie one ounce of gold.
translations.idiomatic: " Though Empress Dowager Ling found Nie's argument reasonable, she could not entirely disregard Sengxian and his party, and still fined Nie one ounce of gold.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書郎，隨蕭寶夤西征，以枿為統軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; following Xiao Baoyin on the western expedition, Nie was made Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and, when Xiao Baoyin marched west, was appointed Nie commander-in-chief of the expedition.

sentences.zh: 枿德洽鄉閭，招募雄勇，其樂從者數百騎。

translations.literal: Nie's virtue was harmonious in village and lane; he recruited bold champions, and those who gladly followed him numbered several hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Nie's reputation for integrity ran deep in his home district. He recruited bold fighters, and several hundred horsemen gladly rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 枿傾家賑恤，率之西討。

translations.literal: Nie exhausted his family's resources in relief and went west at the head of them to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Nie poured out his family's wealth in relief and led them west on campaign.

sentences.zh: 寶夤見枿至，拊其肩曰：「子遠來，吾事辦矣。

translations.literal: When Baoyin saw Nie arrive he clapped his shoulder and said, "You have come from afar; my business is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin saw Nie arrive, he clapped him on the shoulder and said, "You have come from afar—my task is as good as done.

sentences.zh: 」故其下每有戰功，軍中號曰李公騎。

translations.literal: " Accordingly, whenever his command won merit in battle, the army called them Lord Li's Horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: " Henceforth, whenever his troops won distinction in battle, the army called them Lord Li's Horsemen.

sentences.zh: 寶夤啟枿為左丞，仍為別將，軍機戎政，皆與參決。

translations.literal: Baoyin memorialized for Nie as Left Assistant, and concurrently as Separate General; military affairs and martial administration were all decided with his participation.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin memorialized appointing Nie Left Assistant and Separate General; Nie took part in deciding all military strategy and martial administration.

sentences.zh: 寶夤又啟為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Baoyin again memorialized for him as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin further memorialized his appointment as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除岐州刺史，坐辭不赴任，免官。

translations.literal: On return to court he was appointed Governor of Qi province; he was stripped of office for declining the appointment and not taking up his post.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed governor of Qi province, but was dismissed for declining the post and refusing to take up his duties.

sentences.zh: 建義初，河陰遇害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he met disaster at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 初贈尚書右僕射、殷州刺史，後又贈散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Initially he was posthumously granted Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Yin province; later he was further granted Household Cadet of Regular Attendants, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor with the Three Ducal Ministers, and Governor of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He was first posthumously granted Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and governor of Yin province; later he received further posthumous honors as Household Cadet of Regular Attendants, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor with the Three Ducal Ministers, and governor of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 俶儻有大志，好飲酒，篤於親知。

translations.literal: Unconstrained and high-minded, fond of wine, devoted to kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He was free-spirited and ambitious, fond of wine, and deeply devoted to kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 每謂弟郁曰：「士大夫學問，稽博古今而罷，何用專經為老博士也？

translations.literal: He often told his younger brother Yu, "For a gentleman-scholar's learning, to examine and master antiquity and the present is sufficient; why must one specialize in a single classic and become an old erudite?
translations.idiomatic: He often told his younger brother Yu, "For a gentleman-scholar, it is enough to examine and master the breadth of antiquity and the present—why bury oneself in a single classic and become some doddering old pedant?

sentences.zh: 」與弟謐特相友愛。

translations.literal: " He was especially close and affectionate with his younger brother Mi.
translations.idiomatic: " He was especially close and affectionate with his younger brother Mi.

sentences.zh: 謐在鄉物故，枿慟哭絕氣，久而方蘇，不食數日，期年形骸毀悴，人倫哀歎之。

translations.literal: When Mi died at home, Nie wept until his breath failed; only after a long while did he revive. For days he ate nothing; within the year his body was wasted and haggard—men of character mourned and lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi died at home, Nie wept until he lost consciousness and only revived after a long while. He ate nothing for days, and within the year his body was wasted away. All who knew him mourned and lamented.

sentences.zh: 謐字永和，少好學，周覽百氏。

translations.literal: Mi, styled Yonghe, loved learning from youth and surveyed the works of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, styled Yonghe, loved learning from youth and ranged widely through the works of the hundred schools of thought.

sentences.zh: 初師事小學博士孔璠，數年後，璠還就謐請業。

translations.literal: At first he studied under the Erudite of Elementary Learning Kong Fan; several years later Fan in turn came to Mi to request instruction.
translations.idiomatic: At first he studied under Kong Fan, Erudite of Elementary Learning; several years later Fan himself came to Mi to request instruction.

sentences.zh: 同門生為之語曰：「青成藍，藍謝青，師何常，在明經。

translations.literal: Fellow students made a saying for them: "The indigo becomes the blue, the blue thanks the indigo; where does the teacher always reside? In the brightness of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow students composed a verse about them: "The pupil turns indigo, the indigo yields to the pupil—where does the teacher always dwell? In the clarity of the classics.

sentences.zh: 」謐以公子徵拜著作佐郎，辭以授弟郁，詔許之。

translations.literal: " Mi was summoned as a nobleman's son and appointed Assistant Gentleman of Works; he declined and ceded the post to his younger brother Yu, and the edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi was summoned as a nobleman's son and appointed Assistant Gentleman of Works, but he declined and ceded the post to his younger brother Yu; the edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 州再舉秀才，公府二辟，並不就。

translations.literal: The province twice recommended him as Outstanding Talent; the public offices twice summoned him—all without acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: The province twice recommended him as Outstanding Talent, and the public offices summoned him twice—he accepted none of these appointments.

sentences.zh: 唯以琴書為業，有絕世之心。

translations.literal: He devoted himself only to music and books and harbored a mind to withdraw from the world.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself solely to music and books and harbored a desire to withdraw from the world.

sentences.zh: 覽《考工記》、《大戴禮盛德篇》，以明堂之制不同，遂著《明堂制度論》曰：

translations.literal: Reading the "Artificers' Record" and the "Chapter on Great Virtue" in the Elder Dai's Rites, and finding the Mingtang system differed, he wrote the "Treatise on the Mingtang System," saying:
translations.idiomatic: Reading the "Artificers' Record" and the "Chapter on Great Virtue" in the Elder Dai's Rites, and finding their accounts of the Bright Hall differed, he composed the "Treatise on the Bright Hall System," which reads:

sentences.zh: 餘謂論事辯物，當取正於經典之真文；

translations.literal: I hold that in discussing affairs and distinguishing things, one should take one's standard from the true text of the classics;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that in debating affairs and distinguishing things, one must take one's standard from the authentic text of the classics;

sentences.zh: 援證定疑，必有驗于周、孔之遺訓，然後可以稱准的矣。

translations.literal: to marshal evidence and settle doubts, there must be confirmation in the surviving teachings of the Zhou and Confucius—only then can one call it a true criterion.
translations.idiomatic: to marshal evidence and settle doubts, there must be confirmation in the surviving teachings of the Zhou and Confucius—only then can one claim a true standard.

sentences.zh: 今禮文殘缺，聖言靡存，明堂之制，誰使正之？

translations.literal: Now the ritual texts are damaged and incomplete, the sage's words scarcely survive—who can set the Mingtang system aright?
translations.idiomatic: The ritual texts are now damaged and incomplete, the sage's words scarcely survive—who can set the Bright Hall system aright?

sentences.zh: 是以後人紛糾，競興異論，五九之說，各信其習。

translations.literal: Therefore later men have been tangled in dispute, each raising divergent theories; the theories of five rooms and nine rooms, each party trusting its own training.
translations.idiomatic: Hence later scholars have become entangled in dispute, each raising divergent theories—the five-room and nine-room schools, each trusting its own training.

sentences.zh: 是非無准，得失相半，故歷代紛紜，靡所取正。

translations.literal: Right and wrong had no standard, gain and loss divided evenly—hence age after age has been embroiled, with nothing to take as correct.
translations.idiomatic: With no standard for right and wrong and gain and loss evenly matched, age after age has been embroiled, with nothing to take as authoritative.

sentences.zh: 乃使裴頠云：「今群儒紛糾，互相掎摭，就令其象可得而圖。

translations.literal: This led Pei Yi to say, "Today the classicists are tangled in dispute, each pulling and denouncing the other; even supposing its form could be figured and drawn,
translations.idiomatic: This led Pei Yi to say, "Today the classicists are entangled in dispute, each pulling and denouncing the other; even supposing its form could be figured and drawn,

sentences.zh: 其所以居用之禮莫能通也，為設虛器耳。

translations.literal: the ritual of how to inhabit and use it none can harmonize—it would be merely setting up an empty vessel.
translations.idiomatic: none can agree on the ritual of how to inhabit and use it—it would be nothing but setting up an empty vessel.

sentences.zh: 況漢氏所作，四維之個，復不能令各處其辰。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the Han built—the corner chambers in the four dimensions—again could not make each occupy its season.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what the Han dynasty built—the corner chambers in the four directions—again could not make each occupy its proper season.

sentences.zh: 愚以為尊祖配天，其義明著，廟宇之制，理據未分，直可為殿屋以崇嚴父之祀。

translations.literal: I think honoring the ancestor and matching Heaven—the meaning is clear; as for the system of temples and halls, the rationale has not been separated out—one might simply build hall chambers to exalt the solemn sacrifice to the Father.
translations.idiomatic: I think the meaning of honoring the ancestor and matching Heaven is clear; as for the system of temple halls, the rationale has not been sorted out—one might simply build hall chambers to exalt the solemn sacrifice to the Father.

sentences.zh: 其餘雜碎，一皆除之。

translations.literal: As for the rest of the miscellaneous minutiae, all should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest of the miscellaneous details, all should be discarded.

sentences.zh: 」斯豈不以群儒舛互，並乖其實，據義求衷，莫適可從哉？

translations.literal: " Is this not because the classicists contradict one another, all departing from the reality—seeking the mean according to principle, with nothing that can be followed?
translations.idiomatic: " Is this not because the classicists contradict one another and all depart from the reality—so that when one seeks the mean according to principle, nothing can be followed?

sentences.zh: 但恨典文殘滅，求之靡據而已矣，乃復遂去室牖諸制。

translations.literal: I only regret that the canonical texts are destroyed and extinct, so that when one seeks them there is no basis—and then he again went so far as to remove the chambers, windows, and other institutions.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret that the canonical texts are destroyed and extinct, leaving no basis when one seeks them—and yet he went so far as to remove the chambers, windows, and other institutions as well.

sentences.zh: 施之於教，未知其所隆政，求之於情，未可喻其所以必須，惜哉言乎！

translations.literal: Applied to teaching, one cannot know what governance he was exalting; sought in feeling, one cannot explain why they must be needed—alas, what words!
translations.idiomatic: Applied to teaching, one cannot tell what governance he was exalting; sought in human feeling, one cannot explain why these must be required—alas, what words!

sentences.zh: 仲尼有言曰：「賜也，爾愛其羊，我愛其禮。

translations.literal: Confucius had a saying: "Ci, you love the sheep; I love the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius once said, "Ci, you care about the sheep; I care about the ritual.

sentences.zh: 」餘以為隆政必須其禮，豈彼一羊哉？

translations.literal: " I hold that to exalt governance one must have the ritual—how can it be merely that one sheep?
translations.idiomatic: " I hold that to exalt governance one must preserve the ritual—how can it come down to a single sheep?

sentences.zh: 推此而論，則聖人之于禮，殷勤而重之；

translations.literal: Extrapolating from this, the sage in matters of ritual was earnest and weighty;
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating from this, the sage in matters of ritual was earnest and weighty;

sentences.zh: 裴頠之於禮，任意而忽之，是則頠賢于仲尼矣！

translations.literal: Pei Yi in matters of ritual was arbitrary and neglectful—by this reckoning, Yi would be worthier than Zhongni!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yi in matters of ritual was arbitrary and neglectful—by this reckoning, Yi would be worthier than Confucius himself!

sentences.zh: 以斯觀之，裴氏子以不達失禮之旨也。

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, Master Pei's son failed to grasp the purport of ritual loss.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed in this light, the son of the Pei clan failed to grasp the true purport of ritual.

sentences.zh: 餘竊不自量，頗有鄙意，據理尋義，以求其真；

translations.literal: I do not presume on my own measure, but have some humble views; according to principle I seek meaning to arrive at the truth;
translations.idiomatic: I do not presume on my own capacity, but harbor some humble views; according to principle I seek meaning in pursuit of the truth;

sentences.zh: 貴合雅衷，不苟偏信。

translations.literal: I value what matches elegant conviction and do not rashly lean on partial belief.
translations.idiomatic: I value what accords with refined conviction and do not rashly cling to partial belief.

sentences.zh: 乃藉之以《禮傳》，考之以訓注；

translations.literal: I rely on the Ritual Tradition and examine it against commentaries and glosses;
translations.idiomatic: I rely on the Ritual Tradition and test it against commentaries and glosses;

sentences.zh: 博采先賢之言，廣搜通儒之說；

translations.literal: broadly gather the words of former worthies and widely search the theories of comprehensive scholars;
translations.idiomatic: I gather broadly the words of former worthies and search widely the theories of comprehensive scholars;

sentences.zh: 量其當否，參其同異，棄其所短，收其所長，推義察圖，以折厥衷，豈敢必善，聊亦合其言志矣。

translations.literal: measure their fitness, compare their agreements and differences, discard their shortcomings, gather their strengths, infer meaning and inspect the diagram to settle the right view—I dare not claim it must be good, but it may at least accord with the intent of my words.
translations.idiomatic: I weigh their fitness, compare agreements and differences, discard shortcomings and gather strengths, infer meaning and inspect the diagram to settle the right view—I dare not claim it must be correct, but it may at least accord with the intent of my argument.

sentences.zh: 凡論明堂之制者雖眾，然校其大略，則二途而已。

translations.literal: Those who discuss the Mingtang system are many; yet comparing the general outline, there are only two approaches.
translations.idiomatic: Those who discuss the Bright Hall system are many, yet comparing the general outline, there are only two schools of thought.

sentences.zh: 言五室者，則據《周禮考工》之記以為本，是康成之徒所執。

translations.literal: Those who speak of five chambers take the record in the "Artificers' Record" of the Zhou Rites as their foundation—this is what the followers of Kangcheng hold.
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak of five chambers take the record in the "Artificers' Record" of the Zhou Rites as their foundation—this is the position held by the followers of Zheng Kangcheng.

sentences.zh: 言九室者則案《大戴盛德》之篇以為源，是伯喈之倫所持。

translations.literal: Those who speak of nine chambers take the chapter "Great Virtue" in Elder Dai as their source—this is what the party of Bozhe upholds.
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak of nine chambers take the "Great Virtue" chapter in Elder Dai as their source—this is the position upheld by the party of Cai Yong.

sentences.zh: 此二書雖非聖言，然是先賢之中博見洽通者也。

translations.literal: These two books, though not sage words, are among the former worthies broad in vision and thorough in understanding.
translations.idiomatic: These two books, though not the words of sages, come from among the former worthies who were broad in vision and thorough in understanding.

sentences.zh: 但各記所聞，未能全正，可謂既盡美矣，未盡善也。

translations.literal: But each recorded what he heard and could not fully correct it—one may say they had reached beauty but not yet goodness.
translations.idiomatic: But each recorded what he heard and could not fully correct it—one may say they had reached beauty but not yet goodness.

sentences.zh: 而先儒不能考其當否，便各是所習，卒相非毀，豈達士之確論哉？

translations.literal: Yet the earlier Confucians could not examine whether they were correct; each at once affirmed what he had learned, and in the end mutually reviled one another—is this the sure discourse of an accomplished man?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the earlier Confucians could not examine whether these accounts were correct; each at once affirmed what he had learned and in the end mutually reviled one another—is this the reasoned discourse of a true scholar?

sentences.zh: 小戴氏傳禮事四十九篇，號曰《禮記》，雖未能全當，然多得其衷，方之前賢，亦無愧矣。

translations.literal: Younger Dai transmitted forty-nine chapters on ritual matters, called the "Record of Rites"; though not fully correct throughout, in many points he hit the mark—compared with earlier worthies, he has nothing to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: Younger Dai transmitted forty-nine chapters on ritual matters under the title "Record of Rites"; though not correct in every point, he hit the mark in many—compared with earlier worthies, he has nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 而《月令》、《玉藻》、《明堂》三篇，頗有明堂之義，餘故采掇二家，參之《月令》。

translations.literal: Among them the three chapters "Monthly Ordinance," "Jade Regalia," and "Bright Hall" contain considerable meaning regarding the Mingtang; therefore I have gathered from the two schools and compared them with the "Monthly Ordinance."
translations.idiomatic: Among them, the three chapters "Monthly Ordinance," "Jade Regalia," and "Bright Hall" contain considerable material on the Bright Hall; therefore I have drawn from both schools and compared them with the "Monthly Ordinance."

sentences.zh: 以為明堂五室，古今通則。

translations.literal: I take the Mingtang's five chambers as the universal rule from antiquity to the present.
translations.idiomatic: I take the Bright Hall's five chambers as the universal rule from antiquity to the present.

sentences.zh: 其室居中者，謂之太室；

translations.literal: The chamber in the center is called the Grand Chamber;
translations.idiomatic: The chamber at the center is called the Grand Chamber;

sentences.zh: 太室之東者，謂之青陽；

translations.literal: east of the Grand Chamber is called Qingyang;
translations.idiomatic: east of the Grand Chamber is called Qingyang;

sentences.zh: 當太室之南者，謂之明堂；

translations.literal: south of the Grand Chamber is called the Bright Hall;
translations.idiomatic: south of the Grand Chamber is called the Bright Hall;

sentences.zh: 太室之西者，謂之總章；

translations.literal: west of the Grand Chamber is called Zongzhang;
translations.idiomatic: west of the Grand Chamber is called Zongzhang;

sentences.zh: 當太室之北者，謂之玄堂。

translations.literal: north of the Grand Chamber is called the Dark Hall.
translations.idiomatic: north of the Grand Chamber is called the Dark Hall.

sentences.zh: 四面之室，各有夾房，謂之左右個，三十六戶七十二牖矣。

translations.literal: Each of the chambers on the four sides had flanking rooms called the left and right "individuals"—thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows in all.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the chambers on the four sides had flanking rooms called the left and right "cells"—thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows in all.

sentences.zh: 室個之形，今之殿前是其遺像耳。

translations.literal: The form of the chambers and individuals—the forecourt of today's palaces is their surviving image.
translations.idiomatic: The form of the chambers and cells—the forecourt of today's palaces is their surviving trace.

sentences.zh: 個者，即寢之房也。

translations.literal: "Individual" means the side room of a sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: A "cell" is the side room of a sleeping chamber.

sentences.zh: 但明堂與寢，施用既殊，故房個之名，亦隨事而遷耳。

translations.literal: But the Mingtang and the sleeping chamber differ in their application; hence the names of side rooms and individuals also shift according to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: But the Bright Hall and the sleeping chamber serve different functions; hence the names for side rooms and cells shift according to their use.

sentences.zh: 今粗書其像，以見鄙意，案圖察義，略可驗矣。

translations.literal: Now I roughly sketch its form to show my humble view; examined against the diagram and inspected for meaning, it can slightly be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Here I roughly sketch its form to show my humble view; examined against the diagram and inspected for meaning, it can be verified to a degree.

sentences.zh: 故檢之五室，則義明於《考工》；

translations.literal: Thus checked against the five chambers, the meaning is clear in the "Artificers' Record";
translations.idiomatic: Checked against the five chambers, the meaning is clear in the "Artificers' Record";

sentences.zh: 校之戶牖，則數協于《盛德》；

translations.literal: checked against doors and windows, the numbers accord with "Great Virtue";
translations.idiomatic: checked against doors and windows, the numbers accord with "Great Virtue";

sentences.zh: 考之施用，則事著於《月令》；

translations.literal: examined for application, the affairs are set forth in the "Monthly Ordinance";
translations.idiomatic: examined for practical use, the affairs are set forth in the "Monthly Ordinance";

sentences.zh: 求之閏也，合《周禮》與《玉藻》。

translations.literal: sought in intercalation, it agrees with the "Zhou Rites" and "Jade Regalia."
translations.idiomatic: sought in the matter of intercalation, it agrees with the "Zhou Rites" and "Jade Regalia."

sentences.zh: 既同夏、殷，又符周、秦，雖乖眾儒，儻或在斯矣。

translations.literal: It matches both Xia and Yin, and also conforms to Zhou and Qin—though it departs from the multitude of scholars, perhaps the truth lies here.
translations.idiomatic: It accords with both Xia and Yin and conforms to Zhou and Qin—though it departs from the multitude of scholars, perhaps the truth lies here.

sentences.zh: 《考工記》曰：「周人明堂，度以九尺之筵。

translations.literal: The "Artificers' Record" says: "The Zhou people's Bright Hall is measured by the nine-foot mat.
translations.idiomatic: The "Artificers' Record" says, "The Zhou people's Bright Hall is measured by the nine-foot mat.

sentences.zh: 東西九筵，南北七筵，堂崇一筵。

translations.literal: East and west, nine mats; south and north, seven mats; the hall's height, one mat.
translations.idiomatic: East and west, nine mats; south and north, seven mats; the hall's height, one mat.

sentences.zh: 五室，凡室二筵。

translations.literal: Five chambers—each chamber, two mats in all.
translations.idiomatic: Five chambers—each chamber spans two mats in all.

sentences.zh: 室中度以幾，堂上度以筵。

translations.literal: Within the chambers the measure is the bench; on the hall the measure is the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Within the chambers the measure is the bench; on the hall the measure is the mat.

sentences.zh: 」餘謂《記》得之於五室，而謬于堂之修廣。

translations.literal: " I hold that the Record is correct regarding the five chambers but mistaken regarding the hall's length and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: " I hold that the Record is correct regarding the five chambers but mistaken regarding the hall's length and breadth.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 當以理推之，令愜古今之情也。

translations.literal: One ought to deduce it by principle, so as to satisfy the sentiments of antiquity and the present.
translations.idiomatic: One ought to reason it out by principle, so that it satisfies what antiquity and the present alike require.

sentences.zh: 夫明堂者，蓋所以告月朔，布時令，宗文王，祀五帝者也。

translations.literal: Now the Bright Hall is that by which one announces the new moon, promulgates seasonal ordinances, takes King Wen as ancestor, and sacrifices to the Five Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall, in essence, is where the new moon is announced, seasonal ordinances are issued, King Wen is honored as forebear, and the Five Emperors are sacrificed to.

sentences.zh: 然營構之範，自當因宜創制耳。

translations.literal: Yet the scope of planning and construction should naturally be adapted to circumstances and newly devised—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the plan and construction should naturally be adapted to circumstances and newly devised—that is all there is to it.

sentences.zh: 故五室者，合于五帝各居一室之義。

translations.literal: Therefore the five chambers accord with the principle that each of the Five Emperors occupies one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the five chambers accord with the principle that each of the Five Emperors occupies a chamber of his own.

sentences.zh: 且四時之祀，皆據其方之正，又聽朔布令，咸得其月之辰，可謂施政及俱，二三但允。

translations.literal: Moreover, the sacrifices of the four seasons all take their proper directional orientation; hearing the new moon and issuing edicts all obtain the proper months and times—one may say that governance reaches completeness in both respects, and the second and third points are acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the sacrifices of the four seasons all follow their proper cardinal directions, and the audience for the new moon together with the promulgation of edicts each fall in their proper months and seasons—one may say that government is complete in both respects, and the second and third considerations hold.

sentences.zh: 求之古義，竊為當矣。

translations.literal: Sought against ancient meaning, I venture to say it is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against ancient meaning, I believe it is correct.

sentences.zh: 鄭康成漢末之通儒，後學所取正。

translations.literal: Zheng Kangcheng was a comprehensive scholar of the late Han, whom later students take as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Kangcheng was a master scholar of the late Han whom later students take as their standard.

sentences.zh: 釋五室之位，謂土居中，木火金水各居四維。

translations.literal: Explaining the positions of the five chambers, he says Earth occupies the center, while Wood, Fire, Metal, and Water each occupy the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: In explaining the positions of the five chambers, he holds that Earth occupies the center while Wood, Fire, Metal, and Water each occupy one of the four corners.

sentences.zh: 然四維之室既乖其正，施令聽朔各失厥衷，左右之個棄而不顧。

translations.literal: Yet since the chambers at the four corners already depart from what is correct, issuing edicts and hearing the new moon each miss their proper center, and the left and right niches are abandoned and ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Yet chambers placed at the four corners already depart from the cardinal directions; issuing edicts and hearing the new moon each miss their proper alignment, and the left and right niches are abandoned without regard.

sentences.zh: 乃反文之以美說，飾之以巧辭，言水木用事交于東北，木火用事交于東南，火土用事交于西南，金水用事交於西北。

translations.literal: He then turned the text into an elegant theory and adorned it with clever words, saying that when Water and Wood hold sway they meet in the northeast; when Wood and Fire hold sway, in the southeast; when Fire and Earth hold sway, in the southwest; and when Metal and Water hold sway, in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: He then twisted the text into an elegant theory and dressed it in clever language, saying that when Water and Wood hold sway they meet in the northeast; when Wood and Fire hold sway, in the southeast; when Fire and Earth hold sway, in the southwest; and when Metal and Water hold sway, in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 既依五行，當從其用事之交，出何經典？

translations.literal: Since it relies on the Five Phases, it ought to follow the intersections of their periods of dominance—what classic does this come from?
translations.idiomatic: If one is to rely on the Five Phases, one ought to follow the intersections at which they hold sway—what classic authorizes this?

sentences.zh: 可謂工於異端，言非而博，疑誤後學，非所望於先儒也。

translations.literal: One may say he is skilled at heterodox paths: his words are wrong yet copious, sowing doubt and misleading later students—this is not what one expects of the former Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: One may say he is adept at heterodox paths: his words are wrong yet copious, sowing doubt and misleading later students—this is not what one expects of the great scholars of old.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·玉藻》曰：「天子聽朔于南門之外，閏月則闔門左扉，立於其中。

translations.literal: The "Record of Rites: Jade Regalia" says: "The Son of Heaven hears the new moon outside the southern gate; in an intercalary month he closes the left leaf of the gate and stands within it.
translations.idiomatic: The "Record of Rites: Jade Regalia" says: "The Son of Heaven hears the report of the new moon outside the southern gate; in an intercalary month he closes the left leaf of the gate and stands within it.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注曰：「天子之廟及路寢皆如明堂制。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan annotates: "The Son of Heaven's ancestral temple and main palace chamber both follow the Bright Hall model.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Xuan annotates: "The Son of Heaven's ancestral temple and main palace chamber both follow the Bright Hall model.

sentences.zh: 明堂在國之陽，每月就其時之堂而聽朔焉。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall stands on the sunny side of the capital; each month he goes to the hall of that season to hear the new moon there.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall stands on the sunny side of the capital; each month the Son of Heaven goes to the hall of that season to hear the report of the new moon.

sentences.zh: 卒事反宿路寢，亦如之。

translations.literal: When the rite is finished he returns to lodge in the main palace chamber, and the same applies there.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite is finished he returns to lodge in the main palace chamber, and the same applies there.

sentences.zh: 閏月非常月，聽其朔于明堂門下，還處路寢門，終月也。

translations.literal: An intercalary month is not an ordinary month; he hears its new moon beneath the Bright Hall gate, then stays at the gate of the main palace chamber for the whole month.
translations.idiomatic: An intercalary month is not an ordinary month; he hears its new moon beneath the Bright Hall gate, then remains at the gate of the main palace chamber for the entire month.

sentences.zh: 」而《考工記》「周人明堂」，玄注曰：「或舉王寢，或舉明堂，互言之以明其制同也。

translations.literal: " Yet in the "Artificers' Record" passage on "the Zhou people's Bright Hall," Xuan annotates: "Sometimes the royal chamber is cited, sometimes the Bright Hall—each is mentioned in turn to show that their forms are the same.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet in the "Artificers' Record" passage on "the Zhou people's Bright Hall," Xuan annotates: "Sometimes the royal chamber is cited, sometimes the Bright Hall—each is mentioned in turn to show that their forms are the same.

sentences.zh: 」其同制之言，皆出鄭注。

translations.literal: " All statements that the forms are the same come from Zheng's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: " All statements that the forms are identical come from Zheng's commentary.

sentences.zh: 然則明堂與寢，不得異矣。

translations.literal: If so, then the Bright Hall and the palace chamber cannot differ.
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, the Bright Hall and the palace chamber cannot differ.

sentences.zh: 而 《尚書·顧命篇》曰：「迎子釗南門之外，延入翼室。

translations.literal: Yet the "Documents: Charge to Zhong" says: "He met Prince Zhao outside the southern gate and led him into the Wing Chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the "Documents: Charge to Zhong" says: "He met Prince Zhao outside the southern gate and led him into the Wing Chamber.

sentences.zh: 」此之翼室，即路寢矣。

translations.literal: " This Wing Chamber is the main palace chamber.
translations.idiomatic: " This Wing Chamber is the main palace chamber.

sentences.zh: 其下曰：「大貝賁鼓在西房，垂之竹矢在東房。

translations.literal: Below it says: "Large shell drums with tiger-pattern hides are in the western chamber; suspended bamboo arrows are in the eastern chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Below it says: "Large shell drums with tiger-pattern hides are in the western chamber; suspended bamboo arrows are in the eastern chamber.

sentences.zh: 」此則路寢有左右房，見於經史者也。

translations.literal: " This shows that the main palace chamber has left and right side chambers, as seen in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: " This shows that the main palace chamber had left and right side chambers, as attested in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·喪服·大記》曰：「君夫人卒于路寢。

translations.literal: The "Record of Rites: Mourning Garments: Greater Record" says: "The lord's consort died in the main palace chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The "Record of Rites: Mourning Garments: Greater Record" says: "The lord's consort died in the main palace chamber.

sentences.zh: 小斂，婦人髽，帶麻于房中。

translations.literal: At the lesser dressing, the women wore their hair in buns and tied hemp sashes in the side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: At the lesser dressing, the women wore their hair in buns and tied hemp sashes in the side chamber.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注曰：「此蓋諸侯禮。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan annotates: "This is probably the rite for feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Xuan annotates: "This is probably the rite for feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 帶麻于房中，則西南。

translations.literal: Tying hemp in the side chamber means the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Tying hemp in the side chamber refers to the southwest chamber.

sentences.zh: 天子諸侯。

translations.literal: For the Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike.
translations.idiomatic: This applies to both the Son of Heaven and feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 」左右房見於注者也。

translations.literal: " The left and right side chambers appear in the commentary.
translations.idiomatic: " The left and right side chambers appear in the commentary as well.

sentences.zh: 論路寢則明其左右，言明堂則闕其左右個，同制之說還相矛楯，通儒之注，何其然乎？

translations.literal: When discussing the main palace chamber he makes clear its left and right sides, yet when speaking of the Bright Hall he omits its left and right niches—the theory that the forms are the same thus contradicts itself. How can the commentary of so comprehensive a scholar be like this?
translations.idiomatic: When discussing the main palace chamber he makes clear its left and right sides, yet when speaking of the Bright Hall he omits its left and right niches—the claim that the forms are identical thus contradicts itself. How can the commentary of so eminent a scholar be like this?

sentences.zh: 使九室之徒奮筆而爭鋒者，豈不由處室之不當哉？

translations.literal: That the proponents of nine chambers take up their brushes and contend so fiercely—is it not because the placement of the chambers is wrong?
translations.idiomatic: That the proponents of the nine-chamber theory take up their brushes and contend so fiercely—is it not because the placement of the chambers is wrong?

sentences.zh: 《記》云：東西九筵，南北七筵。

translations.literal: The Record says: nine mats east to west, seven mats north to south.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: nine mats east to west, seven mats north to south.

sentences.zh: 五室，凡室二筵。

translations.literal: Five chambers; each chamber in all is two mats.
translations.idiomatic: Five chambers; each chamber measures two mats in all.

sentences.zh: 置五室於斯堂，雖使班、倕構思，王爾營度，則不能令三室不居其南北也。

translations.literal: Place five chambers in this hall—even if Ban and Chui applied their design, and Wang Er planned the layout—they could not keep three chambers from occupying the north-south axis.
translations.idiomatic: Place five chambers in this hall—even if Ban and Chui applied their design, and Wang Er planned the layout—they could not keep three chambers from occupying the north-south axis.

sentences.zh: 然則三室之間，便居六筵之地，而室壁之外，裁有四尺五寸之堂焉。

translations.literal: Then the space between the three chambers would occupy six mats, and beyond the chamber walls there would be only four feet five inches of hall.
translations.idiomatic: Then the space between the three chambers would occupy six mats, and beyond the chamber walls there would remain only four feet five inches of hall.

sentences.zh: 豈有天子布政施令之所，宗祀文王以配上帝之堂，周公負扆以朝諸侯之處，而室戶之外，僅餘四尺而已哉？

translations.literal: How could the place where the Son of Heaven promulgates government and issues edicts, the hall where King Wen is honored in sacrifice to match the Supreme Lord, and the spot where the Duke of Zhou leaned against the screen to hold court for the feudal lords leave only four feet beyond the chamber doors?
translations.idiomatic: How could the place where the Son of Heaven promulgates government and issues edicts, the hall where King Wen is honored in sacrifice to match the Supreme Lord, and the spot where the Duke of Zhou leaned against the screen to receive the feudal lords leave only four feet beyond the chamber doors?

sentences.zh: 假在儉約，為陋過矣。

translations.literal: Even supposing frugality, this would be excessively mean.
translations.idiomatic: Even on the assumption of frugality, this would be excessively cramped.

sentences.zh: 論其堂宇，則偏而非制；

translations.literal: Judged by its hall and chambers, it is lopsided and not according to regulation;
translations.idiomatic: Judged by its hall and chambers, it is lopsided and not according to regulation;

sentences.zh: 求之道理，則未愜人情，其不然一也。

translations.literal: sought by reason, it does not satisfy human expectation—this is the first reason it cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: sought by reason, it does not satisfy human expectation—this is the first reason it cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 余恐為鄭學者，苟求必勝，競生異端，以相訾抑，雲二筵者乃室之東西耳，南北則狹焉。

translations.literal: I fear that followers of Zheng's school, striving at all costs to prevail, will compete in producing heterodox views to attack and suppress one another, saying that the two mats refer only to the east-west of the chamber, while north and south would be narrow.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that followers of Zheng's school, striving at all costs to prevail, will compete in producing heterodox views to attack and suppress one another, saying that the two mats refer only to the east-west dimension of the chamber, while north and south would be narrow.

sentences.zh: 餘故備論之曰：若東西二筵，則室戶之外為丈三尺五寸矣。

translations.literal: I therefore set forth the full argument, saying: if east and west are two mats, then beyond the chamber doors there would be one zhang three chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore set forth the full argument: if east and west are two mats, then beyond the chamber doors there would be one zhang three chi five cun.

sentences.zh: 南北戶外復如此，則三室之中南北裁各丈二耳。

translations.literal: If north and south outside the doors are likewise, then within the three chambers north and south would each measure only one zhang two chi.
translations.idiomatic: If north and south outside the doors are treated the same way, then within the three chambers north and south would each measure only one zhang two chi.

sentences.zh: 《記》云：「四旁兩夾窗。

translations.literal: The Record says: "On all four sides, windows flank in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "On all four sides, windows flank in pairs.

sentences.zh: 」若為三尺之戶，二尺窗，窗戶之間，裁盈一尺。

translations.literal: " If the doors are three chi and the windows two chi, the space between window and door would barely exceed one chi.
translations.idiomatic: " If the doors are three chi and the windows two chi, the space between window and door would barely exceed one chi.

sentences.zh: 繩樞甕牖之室，篳門圭窬之堂，尚不然矣。

translations.literal: Even a room with a rope hinge and jar window, even a hall with a wicker gate and small opening, would not be like this.
translations.idiomatic: Even a room with a rope hinge and jar window, even a hall with a wicker gate and tiny opening, would not be so cramped.

sentences.zh: 假令復欲小廣之，則四面之外，闊狹不齊，東西既深，南北更淺，屋宇之制，不為通矣。

translations.literal: If one then wished to widen it slightly, the space beyond the four sides would be uneven in breadth and narrowness—east and west already deep, north and south even shallower—the rule of building would no longer hold.
translations.idiomatic: If one then wished to widen it slightly, the space beyond the four sides would be uneven—east and west already deep, north and south even shallower—and the rule of building would no longer hold.

sentences.zh: 驗之眾塗，略無算焉。

translations.literal: Tested against many approaches, scarcely any calculation works.
translations.idiomatic: Tested against many approaches, scarcely any calculation works.

sentences.zh: 且凡室二筵，丈八地耳，然則戶牖之間，不逾二尺也。

translations.literal: Moreover, two mats per chamber in all is only one zhang eight chi of space; thus the space between door and window would not exceed two chi.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, two mats per chamber in all is only one zhang eight chi of space; thus the space between door and window would not exceed two chi.

sentences.zh: 《禮記·明堂》：「天子負斧扆南向而立。

translations.literal: The "Record of Rites: Bright Hall" says: "The Son of Heaven, bearing the axe-screen, stands facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The "Record of Rites: Bright Hall" says: "The Son of Heaven, bearing the axe-screen, stands facing south.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注曰：「設斧於戶牖之間。
