translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan annotates: "The axe is set between the door and window.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Xuan annotates: "The axe is set between the door and window.

sentences.zh: 」而鄭氏《禮圖》說扆制曰：「從廣八尺，畫斧文於其上，今之屏風也。

translations.literal: " Yet in Master Zheng's "Ritual Diagrams," the description of the screen says: "Its width is eight chi; an axe pattern is painted on it—it is the present-day folding screen.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet in Master Zheng's "Ritual Diagrams," the description of the screen says: "Its width is eight chi; an axe pattern is painted on it—it is the present-day folding screen.

sentences.zh: 」以八尺扆置二尺之間，此之叵通，不待智者，較然可見矣。

translations.literal: " To place an eight-chi screen in a two-chi space—this cannot be reconciled; even without a wise man to judge, it is plainly visible.
translations.idiomatic: " To place an eight-chi screen in a two-chi space—this cannot be reconciled; even without a wise man to judge, it is plainly visible.

sentences.zh: 且若二筵之室為四尺之戶，則戶之兩頰裁各七尺耳，全以置之，猶自不容，矧復戶牖之間哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, if a two-mat chamber has a four-chi door, then each side of the door frame would measure only seven chi; even if the whole were devoted to it, it would still not fit—how much less the space between door and window?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if a two-mat chamber has a four-chi door, then each side of the door frame would measure only seven chi; even if the whole space were devoted to it, it would still not fit—how much less the space between door and window?

sentences.zh: 其不然二也。

translations.literal: This is the second reason it cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second reason it cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 又復以世代驗之，即虞、夏尚朴，殷、周稍文，製造之差，每加崇飾。

translations.literal: Again, tested by successive ages: Yu and Xia still valued simplicity; Yin and Zhou grew somewhat ornate; differences in construction grew ever more elevated and adorned.
translations.idiomatic: Again, tested against successive ages: Yu and Xia still valued simplicity; Yin and Zhou grew somewhat ornate; with each age, construction grew more elevated and adorned.

sentences.zh: 而夏後世室，堂修二七，周人之制，反更促狹，豈是夏禹卑宮之意，周監鬱鬱之美哉？

translations.literal: Yet the Later Xia ancestral hall had a hall length of two sevens, while the Zhou people's regulation is instead even more cramped and narrow—is this the intent of Yu of Xia's humble palaces, or Zhou's emulation of luxuriant grandeur?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Later Xia ancestral hall had a hall length of two sevens, while the Zhou regulation is instead even more cramped and narrow—is this the intent of Yu of Xia's humble palaces, or Zhou's emulation of luxuriant grandeur?

sentences.zh: 以斯察之，其不然三也。

translations.literal: Examined in this light, this is the third reason it cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: Examined in this light, this is the third reason it cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 又云「堂崇一筵」，便基高九尺，而壁戶之外裁四尺五寸，于營制之法自不相稱，其不然四也。

translations.literal: It also says "the hall's height is one mat," which makes the foundation nine chi high, while beyond the chamber walls there is only four chi five cun—this is inherently incompatible with the methods of planning and construction; this is the fourth reason it cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: It also says "the hall's height is one mat," which makes the foundation nine chi high, while beyond the chamber walls there is only four chi five cun—this is inherently incompatible with the methods of planning and construction; this is the fourth reason it cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 又云「室中度以幾，堂上度以筵」，而復云「凡室二筵」，而不以幾，還自相違，其不然五也。

translations.literal: It also says "within chambers the measure is the bench; on the hall the measure is the mat," yet again says "each chamber in all is two mats" without using the bench—this contradicts itself; this is the fifth reason it cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: It also says "within chambers the measure is the bench; on the hall the measure is the mat," yet again says "each chamber in all is two mats" without using the bench—this contradicts itself; this is the fifth reason it cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 以此驗之，《記》者之謬，抑可見矣。

translations.literal: Verified in this way, the errors of the Record can indeed be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Verified in this way, the errors of the Record can indeed be seen.

sentences.zh: 《盛德篇》云：明堂凡九室、三十六戶、七十二牖，上員下方，東西九仞，南北十筵，堂高三尺也。

translations.literal: The "Great Virtue" chapter says: the Bright Hall has nine chambers in all, thirty-six doors, seventy-two windows; round above and square below; nine ren east to west, ten mats north to south; the hall is three chi high.
translations.idiomatic: The "Great Virtue" chapter says: the Bright Hall has nine chambers in all, thirty-six doors, seventy-two windows; round above and square below; nine ren east to west, ten mats north to south; the hall is three chi high.

sentences.zh: 余謂《盛德篇》得之於戶牖，失之於九室。

translations.literal: I hold that the "Great Virtue" chapter is correct regarding doors and windows but mistaken regarding the nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that the "Great Virtue" chapter is correct regarding doors and windows but mistaken regarding the nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 五室之制，傍有夾房，面各有戶，戶有兩牖，此乃因事立則，非拘異術。

translations.literal: In the five-chamber system, there are flanking side chambers on either side; each face has its doors, and each door has two windows—this follows the principle of establishing rules according to affairs, not clinging to a separate artifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the five-chamber system, there are flanking side chambers on either side; each face has its doors, and each door has two windows—this follows the principle of establishing rules according to affairs, not clinging to a separate artifice.

sentences.zh: 戶牖之數，固自然矣。

translations.literal: The number of doors and windows is naturally so.
translations.idiomatic: The number of doors and windows follows naturally.

sentences.zh: 九室者，論之五帝，事既不合，施之時令，又失其辰，左右之個，重置一隅，兩辰同處，參差出入，斯乃義無所據，未足稱也。

translations.literal: As for nine chambers: judged against the Five Emperors, the affair does not fit; applied to seasonal ordinances, the times are again wrong; the left and right niches are piled into one corner; two seasons occupy the same place; they come and go unevenly—this has no basis in principle and is not worth acclaim.
translations.idiomatic: As for nine chambers: judged against the Five Emperors, the arrangement does not fit; applied to seasonal ordinances, the times are again wrong; the left and right niches are piled into one corner; two seasons occupy the same place; they come and go unevenly—this has no basis in principle and is not worth acclaim.

sentences.zh: 且又堂之修廣，裁六十三尺耳，假使四尺五寸為外之基，其中五十四尺便是五室之地，計其一室之中，僅可一丈，置其戶牖，則于何容之哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, the hall's length and breadth measure only sixty-three chi; supposing four chi five cun as the outer foundation, the inner fifty-four chi would be the ground for five chambers—calculated, within one chamber there would be barely one zhang; where could doors and windows be placed?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the hall's length and breadth measure only sixty-three chi; supposing four chi five cun as the outer foundation, the inner fifty-four chi would be the ground for five chambers—calculated, within one chamber there would be barely one zhang; where could doors and windows be placed?

sentences.zh: 若必小而為之，以容其數，則令帝王側身出入，斯為怪矣！

translations.literal: If one must make them small to accommodate the numbers, then the emperor and king would have to enter and leave sideways—this would be absurd!
translations.idiomatic: If one must make them small to accommodate the numbers, then the emperor and king would have to enter and leave sideways—this would be absurd!

sentences.zh: 此匪直不合典制，抑亦可哂之甚也。

translations.literal: This not only fails to accord with canonical regulation; it is also exceedingly laughable.
translations.idiomatic: This not only fails to accord with canonical regulation; it is also exceedingly laughable.

sentences.zh: 餘謂其九室之言，誠亦有由。

translations.literal: I hold that their talk of nine chambers indeed has some cause.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that their talk of nine chambers indeed has some cause.

sentences.zh: 然竊以為戴氏聞三十六戶七十二牖，弗見其制，靡知所置，便謂一室有四戶之窗，計其戶牖之數，即以為九室耳，或未之思也。

translations.literal: Yet I privately think that Master Dai heard of thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows, did not see their arrangement, and knew not where to place them; he therefore assumed that one chamber had four doors and windows, calculated the number of doors and windows, and took that to mean nine chambers—perhaps he had not thought it through.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I privately think that Master Dai heard of thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows, did not see their arrangement, and knew not where to place them; he therefore assumed that one chamber had four doors and windows, calculated the number of doors and windows, and took that to mean nine chambers—perhaps he had not thought it through.

sentences.zh: 蔡伯喈，漢末之時學士，而見重於當時，即識其修廣之不當，而必未思其九室之為謬。

translations.literal: Cai Yong was a scholar of late Han times, esteemed in his day; he recognized that the length and breadth were wrong, yet surely had not considered that the nine chambers were mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong was a scholar of late Han times, esteemed in his day; he recognized that the length and breadth were wrong, yet surely had not considered that the nine chambers were mistaken.

sentences.zh: 更修而廣之，假其法象。

translations.literal: He revised and enlarged it, borrowing its symbolic forms.
translations.idiomatic: He revised and enlarged it, borrowing its symbolic forms.

sentences.zh: 可謂因偽飾辭，順非而澤，諒可歎矣。

translations.literal: One may say he drew on falsehood to adorn his words, followed what was wrong and glossed it over—this is indeed lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: One may say he drew on falsehood to adorn his words, followed what was wrong and glossed it over—this is indeed lamentable.

sentences.zh: 餘今省彼眾家，委心從善，庶探其衷，不為苟異。

translations.literal: I now review the many schools, commit my heart to what is good, and hope to probe their inner meaning without being arbitrarily different.
translations.idiomatic: I now review the many schools, commit my heart to what is good, and hope to probe their inner meaning without being arbitrarily different.

sentences.zh: 但是古非今，俗間之常情；

translations.literal: Yet to reject the present in favor of antiquity is the common sentiment of the vulgar;
translations.idiomatic: Yet to reject the present in favor of antiquity is the common sentiment of the vulgar;

sentences.zh: 愛遠惡近，世中之恆事。

translations.literal: to love what is distant and hate what is near is the constant affair of the world.
translations.idiomatic: to love what is distant and hate what is near is the constant affair of the world.

sentences.zh: 而千載之下，獨論古制，驚俗之談，固延多誚。

translations.literal: Yet a thousand years later, to discuss ancient institutions alone is talk that shocks the vulgar and will naturally invite much ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a thousand years later, to discuss ancient institutions alone is talk that shocks the vulgar and will naturally invite much ridicule.

sentences.zh: 脫有深賞君子者，覽而揣之，儻或存焉。

translations.literal: If there is a gentleman of deep appreciation who reads and ponders this, perhaps something of it may remain.
translations.idiomatic: If there is a gentleman of deep appreciation who reads and ponders this, perhaps something of it may remain.

sentences.zh: 謐不飲酒，好音律，愛樂山水。

translations.literal: Mi did not drink wine; he loved music and delighted in mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: Mi did not drink wine; he loved music and delighted in mountains and waters.

sentences.zh: 高尚之情，長而彌固，一遇其賞，悠爾忘歸，乃作《神士賦》。

translations.literal: His lofty sentiment grew ever firmer with age; once he encountered what he admired, he would forget to return in leisurely absorption, and he composed the "Rhapsody on the Spirit Gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: His lofty sentiment grew ever firmer with age; once he encountered what he admired, he would forget to return in leisurely absorption, and he composed the "Rhapsody on the Spirit Gentleman."

sentences.zh: 延昌四年卒，年三十二，遐邇悼惜之。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Yanchang, aged thirty-two; near and far mourned and lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Yanchang, aged thirty-two; near and far mourned and lamented him.

sentences.zh: 其年，四門小學博士孔璠等學官四十五人上書曰：

translations.literal: That year, Kong Fan, Erudite of the Four Gates Elementary School, and forty-five other academic officials submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: That year, Kong Fan, Erudite of the Four Gates Elementary School, and forty-five other academic officials submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 竊見故處士趙郡李謐，十歲喪父，哀號罷鄰人之相；

translations.literal: We have observed the late recluse Li Mi of Zhao Commandery: at ten he lost his father, and his wailing exhausted the neighbors' mutual aid;
translations.idiomatic: We have observed the late recluse Li Mi of Zhao Commandery: at ten he lost his father, and his wailing so exhausted the neighbors that they could no longer comfort one another;

sentences.zh: 幼事兄枿，恭順盡友于之誠。

translations.literal: in youth he served his elder brother Zhi with reverent obedience, fulfilling the sincerity of brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: in youth he served his elder brother Zhi with reverent obedience, fulfilling the sincerity of brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 十三通《孝經》、《論語》、《毛詩》、《尚書》，歷數之術，尤盡其長。

translations.literal: At thirteen he mastered the "Classic of Filial Piety," the "Analects," the "Mao Version of the Odes," and the "Documents"; in the arts of calendrical calculation he especially brought his talents to full use.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he mastered the "Classic of Filial Piety," the "Analects," the "Mao Version of the Odes," and the "Documents"; in the arts of calendrical calculation he especially brought his talents to full use.

sentences.zh: 州閭鄉党，有神童之號。

translations.literal: In the district, neighborhood, and village he bore the title of prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the district, neighborhood, and village he bore the title of prodigy.

sentences.zh: 年十八，詣學受業時博士即孔璠也。

translations.literal: At eighteen he went to the academy to receive instruction; the erudite at that time was Kong Fan himself.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he went to the academy to receive instruction; the erudite at that time was Kong Fan himself.

sentences.zh: 覽始要終，論端究緒，授者無不欣其言矣。

translations.literal: He surveyed beginnings and grasped ends, examined openings and pursued conclusions—those who received his instruction were all delighted by his words.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed beginnings and grasped ends, examined openings and pursued conclusions—those who received his instruction were all delighted by his words.

sentences.zh: 於是鳩集諸經，廣校同異，比《三傳》事例，名《春秋叢林》十有二卷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered the various classics, broadly collated their agreements and differences, and compared the cases of the Three Commentaries, titling the work "Thicket of the Spring and Autumn" in twelve scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he gathered the various classics, broadly collated their agreements and differences, and compared the cases of the Three Commentaries, titling the work "Thicket of the Spring and Autumn" in twelve scrolls.

sentences.zh: 為璠等判析隱伏，垂盈百條。

translations.literal: For Fan and the others he adjudicated and analyzed hidden and obscure points, producing nearly a hundred entries.
translations.idiomatic: For Fan and the others he adjudicated and analyzed hidden and obscure points, producing nearly a hundred entries.

sentences.zh: 滯無常滯，纖豪必舉；

translations.literal: No obstruction may remain permanently blocked; even the slightest detail must be raised;
translations.idiomatic: No obstruction may remain permanently blocked; even the slightest detail must be addressed;

sentences.zh: 通不長通，有枉斯屈。

translations.literal: no passage may long remain open; where there is wrong, it is corrected.
translations.idiomatic: no passage may long remain open; where there is wrong, it is corrected.

sentences.zh: 不苟言以違經，弗飾辭而背理，辭氣磊落，觀者忘疲。

translations.literal: He did not speak carelessly against the classics, nor adorn his words against reason; his tone was forthright and open, and those who watched forgot their fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: He did not speak carelessly against the classics, nor adorn his words against reason; his tone was forthright and open, and those who listened forgot their fatigue.

sentences.zh: 每曰：「丈夫擁書萬卷，何假南面百城。

translations.literal: He often said: "A true man who possesses ten thousand scrolls of books—what need has he of facing south over a hundred cities?
translations.idiomatic: He often said: "A true man who possesses ten thousand scrolls of books—what need has he of facing south over a hundred cities?

sentences.zh: 」遂絕跡下帷，杜門卻掃，棄產營書，手自刪削，卷無重復者四千有餘矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he withdrew from public life, lowered his curtain to study, shut his door and refused visitors, abandoned his property to acquire books, and personally edited and trimmed them—more than four thousand scrolls without duplication.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he withdrew from public life, lowered his curtain to study, shut his door and refused visitors, abandoned his property to acquire books, and personally edited and trimmed them—more than four thousand scrolls without duplication.

sentences.zh: 猶括次專家，搜比黨議，隆科達曙，盛暑通宵。

translations.literal: He still organized the works of specialist scholars, searched and compared factional discussions, working from dusk till dawn during examination season and through hot summers all night long.
translations.idiomatic: He still organized the works of specialist scholars, searched and compared factional discussions, working from dusk till dawn during examination season and through hot summers all night long.

sentences.zh: 雖仲舒不窺園，君伯之閉戶，高氏之遺漂，張生之忘食，方之斯人，未足為喻。

translations.literal: Although Dong Zhongshu never glanced over his garden fence, Jun Bo closed his doors, Master Gao abandoned his grain to the flood, and Scholar Zhang forgot to eat—compared with this man, they are not enough to serve as comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Although Dong Zhongshu never glanced over his garden fence, Jun Bo closed his doors, Master Gao abandoned his grain to the flood, and Scholar Zhang forgot to eat—compared with this man, they scarcely serve as adequate comparison.

sentences.zh: 謐嘗詣故太常卿劉芳，推問音義，語及中代興廢之由。

translations.literal: Mi once visited the former Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang to inquire into the meaning of sounds and terms, and their conversation turned to the causes of rise and fall in the middle ages.
translations.idiomatic: Mi once visited the former Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang to inquire into the meaning of sounds and terms, and their conversation turned to the causes of rise and fall in the middle ages.

sentences.zh: 芳乃歎曰：「君若遇高祖，侍中、太常非僕有也。

translations.literal: Fang sighed and said, "If you had met Emperor Gaozu, the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Ceremonies would not have been mine to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sighed and said, "Had you met Emperor Gaozu, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Ceremonies would not have been mine to hold.

sentences.zh: 」前河南尹、黃門侍郎甄琛，內贊近機，朝野傾目，于時親識有求官者，答云：「趙郡李謐，耽學守道，不悶于時，常欲致言，但未有次耳。

translations.literal: " Former Administrator of Henan and Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhen Chen, who held sway at the inner court, drew the gaze of officialdom and folk alike. When acquaintances then sought office through him, he would answer: "Li Mi of Zhao commandery—devoted to learning and steadfast in the Way, untroubled by the times—often wished to speak up, but simply never had the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen Chen, former Administrator of Henan and Yellow Gate Gentleman, wielded influence at court and drew every eye. When acquaintances sought office through him, he answered: "Li Mi of Zhao commandery—devoted to learning, steadfast in the Way, untroubled by the times—often wished to speak up but never had the occasion.

sentences.zh: 諸君何為輕自媒衒？

translations.literal: Why do you gentlemen so lightly sell yourselves in self-promotion?
translations.idiomatic: Why do you gentlemen so lightly peddle yourselves?

sentences.zh: 」謂其子曰：「昔鄭玄、盧植不遠數千里詣扶風馬融，今汝明師甚邇，何不就業也？

translations.literal: " He told his son: "In antiquity Zheng Xuan and Lu Zhi traveled thousands of li to study under Ma Rong of Fufeng. Your master of clarity is very near—why do you not go learn from him?
translations.idiomatic: " He told his son: "Long ago Zheng Xuan and Lu Zhi traveled thousands of li to study under Ma Rong of Fufeng. Your luminous teacher is right at hand—why not go learn from him?

sentences.zh: 」又謂朝士曰：「甄琛行不愧時，但未薦李謐，以此負朝廷耳。

translations.literal: " He also told court gentlemen: "Zhen Chen's conduct does not shame the age—but in failing to recommend Li Mi, he has failed the court.
translations.idiomatic: " He also told court gentlemen: "Zhen Chen's conduct does not shame the age—but by failing to recommend Li Mi, he has failed the court.

sentences.zh: 」又結宇依岩，憑崖鑿室，方欲訓彼青衿，宣揚墳典，冀西河之教重興，北海之風不墜。

translations.literal: " He had also built dwellings against the cliffs, hewing chambers into the rock face, intending to instruct the young scholars there and spread the classics, hoping that the teaching of Xihé might be revived and the spirit of Beihai never fall.
translations.idiomatic: " He had built dwellings against the cliffs and hewn chambers into the rock, intending to instruct young scholars and spread the classics, hoping to revive the teaching of Xihé and keep the spirit of Beihai from falling.

sentences.zh: 而祐善空聞，暴疾而卒。

translations.literal: Yet his hoped-for goodness was heard of in vain—he died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the good he promised was heard of in vain: he died suddenly of illness.

sentences.zh: 邦國銜殄悴之哀，儒生結摧梁之慕，況璠等或服議下風，或親承音旨，師儒之義，其可默乎？

translations.literal: The realm bore the grief of untimely loss; scholars cherished mourning like a fallen beam—and as for Fan and the others, some had submitted to his learning from afar, some had personally received his instruction. Could the duty between teacher and student remain silent?
translations.idiomatic: The realm mourned an untimely loss; scholars grieved as for a fallen beam. Fan and the others—some had learned at his feet from afar, some had personally received his instruction. Could the bond between teacher and student stay silent?

sentences.zh: 事奏，詔曰：「謐屢辭徵辟，志守沖素，儒隱之操，深可嘉美。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict said: "Mi repeatedly declined summons and appointment, holding to unadorned integrity—the conduct of a scholarly recluse, deeply worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, an edict said: "Mi repeatedly declined summons, holding to unadorned integrity—the conduct of a scholarly recluse, deeply worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 可遠傍惠、康，近准玄晏。

translations.literal: Let him be compared from afar to Huì and Kāng, and from near to Xuán Yàn.
translations.idiomatic: Compare him from afar to Huì and Kāng, and from near to Xuán Yàn.

sentences.zh: 諡曰：貞靜處士，並表其門閭，以旌高節。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Recluse of Pure Endurance. Let his gate and lane be marked to honor his lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Recluse of Pure Endurance. Mark his gate and lane to honor his lofty integrity.

sentences.zh: 」於是表其門曰文德，裏曰孝義云。

translations.literal: " Thus his gate was inscribed Wéndé (Cultured Virtue), his lane Xiàoyì (Filial Righteousness).
translations.idiomatic: " His gate was then inscribed Wéndé (Cultured Virtue) and his lane Xiàoyì (Filial Righteousness).

sentences.zh: 郁字永穆，好學沈靖，博通經史。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Yongmu, loved learning and was calm and quiet, broadly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, courtesy name Yongmu, loved learning, was calm and quiet, and was broadly versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 為廣平王懷友，深見禮遇。

translations.literal: He was friend to Prince Huai of Guangping and was deeply honored.
translations.idiomatic: He was a friend to Prince Huai of Guangping and was deeply honored.

sentences.zh: 時學士徐遵明教授山東，生徒甚盛。

translations.literal: At the time the scholar Xu Zunming taught in Shandong, with a great throng of disciples.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xu Zunming taught in Shandong, and his disciples were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 懷征遵明在館，令鬱問其《五經》義例十餘條，遵明所答數條而已。

translations.literal: Huai summoned Zunming to his residence and had Yu question him on more than ten points of principle from the Five Classics—Zunming answered only a few.
translations.idiomatic: Huai summoned Zunming to his residence and had Yu question him on more than ten points of principle from the Five Classics; Zunming answered only a few.

sentences.zh: 稍遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 自國學之建，諸博士率不講說，其朝夕教授，唯郁而已。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the National Academy, the erudites generally did not lecture; day and night instruction fell to Yu alone.
translations.idiomatic: Since the National Academy was founded, the erudites generally did not lecture; only Yu taught day and night.

sentences.zh: 謙虛寬雅，甚有儒者之風。

translations.literal: Humble, broad-minded, and elegant, he possessed the true bearing of a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Humble, broad-minded, and elegant, he had the bearing of a true scholar.

sentences.zh: 再遷通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to regular attendant of direct communication and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 建義中，以兄枿卒，遂撫育孤侄，歸於鄉里。

translations.literal: During Jianyi, when his elder brother Nie died, he raised the orphaned nephew and withdrew to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianyi, when his elder brother Nie died, he raised the orphaned nephew and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，除散騎常侍、衛大將軍、左光祿大夫，兼都官尚書，尋領給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongxi he was made Regular Attendant, Grand General of the Guard, Left Grand Master for the Illustrious, and concurrent Minister of Punishments; soon he also held the post of Supervising Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongxi he was made regular attendant, grand general of the guard, left grand master for the illustrious, and concurrent minister of punishments; soon he also served as supervising gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 三年，于顯陽殿講《禮記》，詔鬱執經。

translations.literal: In the third year, at the Hall of Manifest Yang they lectured on the Record of Rites; Yu was ordered to hold the text.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, at the Hall of Manifest Yang they lectured on the Record of Rites, and Yu was ordered to hold the text.

sentences.zh: 鬱解說不窮，群難鋒起，無廢談笑。

translations.literal: Yu explained without exhaustion; challenges rose like spearpoints from the crowd, yet he did not cease his easy discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Yu explained without end; challenges rose like spearpoints from the crowd, yet he never lost his easy tone.

sentences.zh: 孝武及諸王凡預聽者，莫不嗟善。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu and all the princes who were present sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu and every prince present sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒，贈散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、儀同三司、都督、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness and was posthumously made Regular Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Equal in Honor with the Three Dukes, Area Commander, and Inspector of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died of illness and was posthumously made regular attendant, general of agile cavalry, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, equal in honor with the three dukes, area commander, and inspector of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 謐子士謙，字子約，一名容郎，髫齔喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Li Mi's son Shiqian, courtesy name Ziyue, also called Ronglang, lost his father in childhood and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi's son Shiqian, courtesy name Ziyue, also called Ronglang, lost his father as a child and was known for filial devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 母曾歐吐，疑中毒，因跪嘗之。

translations.literal: When his mother once vomited, suspecting poison, he knelt and tasted it himself.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother once vomited and poison was suspected, he knelt and tasted it himself.

sentences.zh: 伯父枿深所嗟尚，每稱：「此兒吾家顏子也。

translations.literal: His uncle Nie deeply admired him and often said, "This boy is our family's Yan Hui.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Nie deeply admired him and often said, "This boy is our family's Yan Hui.

sentences.zh: 」年十二，魏廣平王贊辟開府參軍事。

translations.literal: " At age twelve Prince Zan of Guangping of Wei summoned him as a staff officer on the opening of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " At twelve, Prince Zan of Guangping of Wei summoned him as a staff officer when his headquarters opened.

sentences.zh: 後丁母憂，居喪骨立。

translations.literal: Later, when mourning his mother, he wasted away to bone during the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later, mourning his mother, he wasted away to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 有姊適宋氏，不勝哀而死。

translations.literal: He had an elder sister married to the Song clan who died unable to bear the grief.
translations.idiomatic: An elder sister married into the Song clan died, unable to bear the grief.

sentences.zh: 士謙服闋，舍宅為伽藍。

translations.literal: When Shiqian's mourning ended, he gave his house to become a monastery.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqian's mourning ended, he gave his house to be a monastery.

sentences.zh: 脫身而出，詣學請業，研精不倦，遂博覽群籍，善天文術數。

translations.literal: Freeing himself, he went to the academy to seek instruction, delving deep without weariness, until he broadly read all books and was skilled in astronomy and numerology.
translations.idiomatic: Freeing himself, he went to the academy to study, delving deep without weariness until he had read widely and mastered astronomy and numerology.

sentences.zh: 齊吏部尚書辛術召署員外郎，趙郡王睿舉德行，皆稱疾不就。

translations.literal: The Qi Minister of Personnel Xin Shu summoned him as an extra master of writing; Prince Rui of Zhao recommended his virtue—both times he pleaded illness and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Minister of Personnel Xin Shu summoned him as an extra master of writing; Prince Rui of Zhao recommended his virtue—each time he pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 和士開亦重其名，將諷朝廷，擢為國子祭酒，因辭得免。

translations.literal: He Shikai also valued his name and was about to prompt the court to elevate him to Director of the National University; he declined and was spared the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He Shikai also valued his name and was about to prompt the court to make him director of the National University; he declined and was spared.

sentences.zh: 刺史高元海以禮再致之，稱為菩薩。

translations.literal: Inspector Gao Yuanhai courteously summoned him again and called him a bodhisattva.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Gao Yuanhai courteously summoned him again and called him a bodhisattva.

sentences.zh: 隋有天下，畢志不仕。

translations.literal: When the Sui gained the realm, he steadfastly refused office to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui gained the realm, he steadfastly refused office until the end.

sentences.zh: 自以少孤，未嘗飲酒食肉，口無殺害之言。

translations.literal: Having been orphaned young, he never drank wine or ate meat, and never spoke of killing.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he never drank wine or ate meat and never spoke of killing.

sentences.zh: 親賓至，輒陳樽俎，對之危坐，終日不倦。

translations.literal: When kin and guests came, he would still set out dishes, sit upright before them, and keep company all day without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: When kin and guests came, he still set out dishes, sat upright before them, and kept company all day without weariness.

sentences.zh: 李氏宗党豪盛，每春秋二社，必高會極宴，無不沈醉喧亂。

translations.literal: The Li clan and its branches were wealthy and numerous; at each spring and autumn she-sacrifice they held grand feasts to the full, and none failed to grow drunk and noisy.
translations.idiomatic: The Li clan and its branches were wealthy and numerous; at each spring and autumn she-sacrifice they held grand feasts, and all ended drunk and noisy.

sentences.zh: 嘗集士謙所，盛饌盈前，而先為設黍。

translations.literal: Once they gathered at Shiqian's home; rich fare heaped the table, but he first served millet.
translations.idiomatic: Once they gathered at Shiqian's home with rich fare heaped before them, but he first served millet.

sentences.zh: 謂群從曰：「孔子稱黍為五穀之長，荀卿亦云食先黍稷，古人所尚，寧可違乎！

translations.literal: He told the clan members, "Confucius called millet the chief of the five grains; Xun Qing likewise said eating begins with millet and panic millet—what the ancients honored, how could we violate it!
translations.idiomatic: He told the clan, "Confucius called millet the chief of the five grains; Xun Qing said eating begins with millet and panic millet—what the ancients honored, how could we violate it!

sentences.zh: 」少長肅然，無敢弛惰，退而相謂曰：「既見君子，方覺吾徒之不德也。

translations.literal: " Young and old grew solemn; none dared slacken. Withdrawing they said to one another, "Having met a true gentleman, we now see how unworthy our company has been.
translations.idiomatic: " Young and old grew solemn; none dared slacken. Withdrawing they said, "Having met a gentleman, we see how unworthy we have been.

sentences.zh: 」士謙聞而自責曰：「何乃為人疏，頓至於此！」

translations.literal: " Shiqian heard and blamed himself: "How could I have been so distant from others as to bring things to this pass!"
translations.idiomatic: " Shiqian heard and blamed himself: "How could I have been so distant from people as to bring things to this!"

sentences.zh: 家富於財，躬處節儉，每以振施為務。

translations.literal: Though rich in wealth, he personally lived frugally and made relief and giving his constant task.
translations.idiomatic: Though rich in wealth, he lived frugally himself and made relief and giving his constant task.

sentences.zh: 州裏有喪事。

translations.literal: In the district there was a funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the district there was a funeral.

sentences.zh: 不均，至相鬩訟。

translations.literal: The contributions were unequal, until brothers quarreled and sued one another.
translations.idiomatic: Contributions were unequal, until brothers quarreled and sued one another.

sentences.zh: 士謙聞而出財補其少者，令與多者相埒。

translations.literal: Shiqian heard of it, gave out funds to supplement those who gave less, and made them equal to those who gave more.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian heard of it, gave funds to supplement those who gave less, and made them equal to those who gave more.

sentences.zh: 兄弟愧懼，更相推讓，卒為善士。

translations.literal: The brothers felt shame and fear, yielded to one another anew, and in the end became good men.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers felt shame and fear, yielded to one another, and in the end became good men.

sentences.zh: 有牛犯其田者，士謙牽置涼處，飼之過於本主。

translations.literal: When an ox strayed into his fields, Shiqian led it to a shady spot and fed it better than its owner would have.
translations.idiomatic: When an ox strayed into his fields, Shiqian led it to shade and fed it better than its owner would have.

sentences.zh: 望見盜刈禾黍者，默而避之。

translations.literal: When he saw thieves reaping his grain, he silently withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw thieves reaping his grain, he silently withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其家僮嘗執盜粟者，士謙慰喻之曰：「窮困所致，義無相責。

translations.literal: When a household servant once seized a grain thief, Shiqian comforted him and said, "Poverty drove this—by right there is nothing to blame.
translations.idiomatic: When a household servant once seized a grain thief, Shiqian comforted him: "Poverty drove this—by right there is nothing to blame.

sentences.zh: 」遽令放之。

translations.literal: " He at once had the man released.
translations.idiomatic: " He at once had the man released.

sentences.zh: 其奴嘗與鄉人董震因醉角力，震扼其喉，斃於手下。

translations.literal: A slave of his once wrestled in drunkenness with a villager named Dong Zhen; Zhen seized his throat and killed him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: A slave of his once wrestled drunk with a villager named Dong Zhen; Zhen seized his throat and killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 震懼請罪，士謙謂曰：「卿本無殺心，何為相謝？

translations.literal: Zhen, afraid, begged forgiveness. Shiqian said, "You never meant to kill—why apologize?
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, afraid, begged forgiveness. Shiqian said, "You never meant to kill—why apologize?

sentences.zh: 然可速去，無為吏拘。

translations.literal: But go quickly, lest the officers seize you.
translations.idiomatic: But go quickly, lest the officers seize you.

sentences.zh: 」性寬厚皆此類也。

translations.literal: " His generous nature was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " His generous nature was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 後出粟萬石以貸鄉人，屬年穀不登，債家無以償，皆來致謝。

translations.literal: Later he lent ten thousand bushels of grain to neighbors; when the year's harvest failed, debtors could not repay and all came to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Later he lent ten thousand bushels of grain to neighbors; when the harvest failed, debtors could not repay and all came to apologize.

sentences.zh: 士謙曰：「吾家餘粟，本圖賑贍，豈求利哉！

translations.literal: Shiqian said, "The surplus grain in our house was meant for relief—how could we seek profit!
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian said, "Our surplus grain was meant for relief—how could we seek profit!

sentences.zh: 」於是悉召債家，為設酒食，對之燔契，曰：「債了矣，幸勿為念也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he summoned all debtors, set out wine and food, and burned the contracts before them, saying, "The debt is done—pray do not dwell on it.
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned all debtors, set out wine and food, and burned the contracts before them, saying, "The debt is done—do not dwell on it.

sentences.zh: 」各令罷去。

translations.literal: " He had each go home.
translations.idiomatic: " He had each go home.

sentences.zh: 明年大熟，債家爭來償，士謙拒之，一無所受。

translations.literal: The next year the harvest was abundant; debtors vied to repay him—Shiqian refused and accepted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the harvest was abundant; debtors vied to repay him, but Shiqian refused and accepted nothing.

sentences.zh: 他年饑，多有死者，士謙罄家資為之糜粥，賴以全活者萬計；

translations.literal: In another famine year many died; Shiqian spent all his household wealth on gruel and porridge, and those who lived because of it numbered in the tens of thousands;
translations.idiomatic: In another famine year many died; Shiqian spent all his household wealth on gruel and porridge, and tens of thousands lived because of it;

sentences.zh: 收埋骸骨，所見無遺；

translations.literal: he gathered and buried the bones he saw, leaving none behind;
translations.idiomatic: he gathered and buried every bone he saw, leaving none behind;

sentences.zh: 至春，又出田糧種子，分給貧乏。

translations.literal: come spring, he again put out seed grain and distributed it to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: come spring, he again put out seed grain and distributed it to the poor.

sentences.zh: 趙郡農人德之，撫其子孫曰：「此李參軍遺惠也。

translations.literal: The farmers of Zhao commandery blessed him, stroking their sons and grandsons and saying, "This is the lasting kindness of Administrator Li.
translations.idiomatic: The farmers of Zhao commandery blessed him, telling their sons and grandsons, "This is the lasting kindness of Administrator Li.

sentences.zh: 」仁心感物，群犬生子，交共相乳。

translations.literal: " His humane heart moved creatures; dogs in the neighborhood whelped and nursed one another's young in turn.
translations.idiomatic: " His humane heart moved creatures: neighborhood dogs whelped and nursed one another's young in turn.

sentences.zh: 凶年散谷至萬餘石，合諸藥以救疾癘，如此積三十年。

translations.literal: In famine years he distributed more than ten thousand bushels of grain and combined herbs to treat plague—thus for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he distributed more than ten thousand bushels of grain and combined herbs to treat plague—thus for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 或謂士謙：「子多陰德。

translations.literal: Someone said to Shiqian, "Sir, you have accumulated much hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Shiqian, "Sir, you have accumulated much hidden virtue.

sentences.zh: 」士謙曰：「夫言陰德，其猶耳鳴，己獨知之，人無知者。

translations.literal: " Shiqian said, "To speak of hidden virtue is like ringing in the ears—only oneself knows it; others do not.
translations.idiomatic: " Shiqian said, "Hidden virtue is like ringing in the ears—only oneself knows it; others do not.

sentences.zh: 今吾所作，吾子皆知，何陰德之有？」

translations.literal: What I do now, my children all know—where is the hidden virtue in that?"
translations.idiomatic: What I do now, my children all know—where is the hidden virtue in that?"

sentences.zh: 士謙善談玄理，嘗有客坐，不信佛家應報義。

translations.literal: Shiqian was skilled at discussing Dark Learning. Once a guest seated with him did not believe in Buddhist karma and retribution.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian was skilled at discussing Dark Learning. Once a guest with him did not believe in Buddhist karma and retribution.

sentences.zh: 士謙喻之曰：「積善余慶，積惡餘殃，豈非休咎邪？

translations.literal: Shiqian enlightened him: "Accumulated good brings lasting blessing; accumulated evil lasting calamity—is this not fortune and misfortune?
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian enlightened him: "Accumulated good brings lasting blessing; accumulated evil brings lasting calamity—is this not fortune and misfortune?

sentences.zh: 佛經雲'轉輪五道，無復窮已'，此則賈誼所言'千變萬化，未始有極，忽然為人'之謂也。

translations.literal: The Buddhist scripture says 'turning through the five paths without end'—this is what Jia Yi meant by 'myriad changes without limit, suddenly becoming human.'
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist scripture says "turning through the five paths without end"—this is what Jia Yi meant by "myriad changes without limit, suddenly becoming human."

sentences.zh: 佛道未來，而賢者已知其然矣。

translations.literal: Before Buddhism came, the worthy already knew this was so.
translations.idiomatic: Before Buddhism came, the worthy already knew it was so.

sentences.zh: 至若鮌為黃熊，杜宇為鶗鴂，褒君為龍，牛哀為猛獸，君子為鵠，小人為猿，彭生為豕，如意為犬，黃母為黿，宣武為鱉，鄧艾為牛，徐伯為魚，鈴下為烏，書生為蛇，羊祜前身李氏之子，此非佛家變受異形之謂邪？

translations.literal: Consider Gun who became a yellow bear, Du Yu who became a shrike, Lord Bao who became a dragon, Niu Ai who became a fierce beast, the noble who became a swan, the petty man who became an ape, Peng Sheng who became a pig, Ruyi who became a dog, Huang Mu who became a softshell turtle, Xuan Wu who became a turtle, Deng Ai who became an ox, Xu Bo who became a fish, a bell-man who became a crow, a scholar who became a snake, Yang Hu in a former life the son of the Li clan—is this not what the Buddhists mean by receiving strange forms in transmutation?
translations.idiomatic: Consider Gun who became a yellow bear, Du Yu a shrike, Lord Bao a dragon, Niu Ai a fierce beast, the noble a swan, the petty man an ape, Peng Sheng a pig, Ruyi a dog, Huang Mu a softshell turtle, Xuan Wu a turtle, Deng Ai an ox, Xu Bo a fish, a bell-man a crow, a scholar a snake, Yang Hu in a former life the son of the Li clan—is this not what the Buddhists mean by transmuting into strange forms?

sentences.zh: 」客曰：「邢子才雲'豈有松柏後身，化為樗櫟 '，僕以為然。

translations.literal: " The guest said, "Xing Zicao said, 'Can a pine or cypress in a later life turn into a stinking elm?'—I think him right.
translations.idiomatic: " The guest said, "Xing Zicao said, 'Can a pine or cypress in a later life turn into a stinking elm?'—I think him right.

sentences.zh: 」士謙曰：「此不類之談也，變化皆由心作，木豈有心乎？

translations.literal: " Shiqian said, "That is nonsense of the wrong kind—transformation is all made by the mind; can wood have a mind?
translations.idiomatic: " Shiqian said, "That is nonsense—transformation is all made by the mind; can wood have a mind?

sentences.zh: 」客又問三教優劣，士謙曰：「佛，日也；

translations.literal: " The guest asked again which of the three teachings was superior. Shiqian said, "Buddhism is the sun;
translations.idiomatic: " The guest asked again which of the three teachings was superior. Shiqian said, "Buddhism is the sun;

sentences.zh: 道，月也；

translations.literal: Daoism is the moon;
translations.idiomatic: Daoism is the moon;

sentences.zh: 儒，五星也。

translations.literal: Confucianism is the five stars.
translations.idiomatic: Confucianism is the five stars.

sentences.zh: 」客亦不能難而止。

translations.literal: " The guest could not refute him and fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: " The guest could not refute him and fell silent.

sentences.zh: 士謙平生時時為詠懷詩，輒毀其本，不示人。

translations.literal: Shiqian from time to time composed meditative poems, but always destroyed the drafts and never showed them to others.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian from time to time composed meditative poems but always destroyed the drafts and never showed them.

sentences.zh: 又嘗論刑罰，遺文不具。

translations.literal: He also once discussed punishments; the surviving text is incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: He also once discussed punishments; the surviving text is incomplete.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「帝王制法，沿革不同，自可損益，無為頓改。

translations.literal: The gist runs: "When emperors and kings make law, the changes through the ages differ; one may add or subtract, but need not overturn all at once.
translations.idiomatic: The gist runs: "When emperors and kings make law, changes through the ages differ; one may add or subtract, but need not overturn all at once.

sentences.zh: 今之贓重者死，是酷而不懲也。

translations.literal: Today the penalty for heavy corruption is death—this is cruel yet fails to deter.
translations.idiomatic: Today the penalty for heavy corruption is death—this is cruel yet fails to deter.

sentences.zh: 語曰：'人不畏死，不可以死恐之。

translations.literal: The saying goes, 'When men do not fear death, you cannot frighten them with death.'
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes, "When men do not fear death, you cannot frighten them with death."

sentences.zh: '愚謂此罪，宜從肉刑，刖其一趾；

translations.literal: I hold that for this crime one should apply corporal punishment—cut off one toe;
translations.idiomatic: I hold that for this crime one should apply corporal punishment—cut off one toe;

sentences.zh: 再犯者，斷其左腕。

translations.literal: for a second offense, sever the left wrist.
translations.idiomatic: for a second offense, sever the left wrist.

sentences.zh: 流刑刖去右手三指；

translations.literal: For exile, cut off three fingers of the right hand;
translations.idiomatic: For exile, cut off three fingers of the right hand;

sentences.zh: 又犯者，下其腕。

translations.literal: if they offend again, remove the wrist.
translations.idiomatic: if they offend again, remove the wrist.

sentences.zh: 小盜宜黥。

translations.literal: Petty theft should be tattooed.
translations.idiomatic: Petty theft should be tattooed.

sentences.zh: 又犯，刖落其所用三指；

translations.literal: If they offend again, cut off the three fingers they use;
translations.idiomatic: If they offend again, cut off the three fingers they use;

sentences.zh: 又不悛，則下其腕。

translations.literal: if still unrepentant, remove the wrist.
translations.idiomatic: if still unrepentant, remove the wrist.

sentences.zh: 無不止也。

translations.literal: None would fail to stop.
translations.idiomatic: None would fail to stop.

sentences.zh: 無賴之人，竄之邊裔，職為亂階，適所以召戎矣，非求安之道也。

translations.literal: Ruffians driven to the borderlands become a ladder to disorder—it is precisely how one summons barbarians, not the path to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Ruffians driven to the borderlands become a ladder to disorder—it is precisely how one summons barbarians, not the path to peace.

sentences.zh: 博弈淫遊，盜之萌也，禁而不止，黥之則可。

translations.literal: Gambling and dissolute wandering are the seed of theft; if prohibition fails, tattooing will do.
translations.idiomatic: Gambling and dissolute wandering are the seed of theft; if prohibition fails, tattooing will do.

sentences.zh: 」有識者頗以為得政體。

translations.literal: " Men of discernment largely thought this grasped the substance of governance.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of discernment largely thought this grasped the substance of governance.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇八年，終於家。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaihuang of Sui, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaihuang of Sui, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 趙州士女聞之，莫不流淚曰：「我曹不死而令李參軍死乎！

translations.literal: When the gentlemen and women of Zhao prefecture heard the news, none did not shed tears and say: "We do not die yet let Administrator Li die!"
translations.idiomatic: When the gentlemen and women of Zhao prefecture heard the news, none could hold back tears. "How is it," they cried, "that we still live while Administrator Li is dead!"

sentences.zh: 」會葬者萬餘人。

translations.literal: " More than ten thousand attended the burial.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand attended his burial.

sentences.zh: 李景伯等以士謙道著丘園，條其行狀，詣尚書省請先生之諡，事寢不行，遂相與樹碑於墓。

translations.literal: Li Jingbo and others, because Shiqian's Way was renowned in hills and gardens, itemized his conduct and deeds, went to the Ministry of Personnel to request a posthumous title for the Master; the matter lapsed and was not carried out, whereupon together they erected a stele at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingbo and others, seeing that Shiqian's virtue was renowned though he dwelt in seclusion, drew up an account of his conduct and submitted it to the Ministry of Personnel requesting a posthumous title—but the petition lapsed without result. They then jointly erected a stele at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 其妻范陽盧氏，亦有婦德。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Lu of Fanyang, also had wifely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Lu of Fanyang, was likewise a model of wifely virtue.

sentences.zh: 及夫終，所有賻贈，一無所受。

translations.literal: When her husband died, all funeral gifts she wholly did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died, she refused every funeral gift offered her.

sentences.zh: 謂州裏父老曰：「參軍平生好施，今雖殞歿，安可奪其志哉！

translations.literal: She told the elders of the prefecture and district: "Administrator Li all his life loved giving; though he has now perished, how can we wrest away his purpose!"
translations.idiomatic: She told the elders of the district: "Administrator Li loved giving all his life. Though he is gone, how can we betray his wishes?"

sentences.zh: 」乃散粟五百石以賑窮乏，免奴婢六十人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she distributed five hundred bushels of grain to relieve the poor and needy, and freed sixty slaves and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: She then distributed five hundred bushels of grain to relieve the destitute and freed sixty slaves and maidservants.

sentences.zh: 案趙郡李氏，出自趙將武安君牧。

translations.literal: Investigating: the Li clan of Zhao commandery descended from Zhao's general Lord Wu'an, Mu.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao commandery Li traced their descent to Zhao's general, Lord Wu'an, Li Mu.

sentences.zh: 當楚、漢之際，廣武君左車則其先也。

translations.literal: At the juncture of Chu and Han, Guangwu Lord Zuoche was their ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: At the clash between Chu and Han, their forebear was Guangwu Lord Zuoche.

sentences.zh: 左車十四世孫恢，字仲興，漢桓、靈間，高尚不仕，號有道大夫。

translations.literal: Zuoche's fourteenth-generation descendant Hui, courtesy name Zhongxing, between Emperors Huan and Ling of Han, loftily virtuous and not serving, styled himself the Worthy Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Zuoche's fourteenth-generation descendant Hui, styled Zhongxing, lived between the reigns of Emperors Huan and Ling of Han—loftily virtuous, refusing office, and known as the Worthy Grandee.

sentences.zh: 恢生定，字文義，仕魏，位漁陽太守。

translations.literal: Hui begat Ding, courtesy name Weny, served Wei, post Yuyang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Hui begat Ding, styled Weny, who served Wei as Administrator of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 有子四人，並仕晉。

translations.literal: He had four sons, all serving Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons, all of whom served Jin.

sentences.zh: 平字伯括，為樂平太守；

translations.literal: Ping, courtesy name Boguo, was Administrator of Leping;
translations.idiomatic: Ping, styled Boguo, served as Administrator of Leping;

sentences.zh: 機字仲括，位國子博士；

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Zhongguo, post National University Erudite;
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Zhongguo, held the post of Erudite at the National University;

sentences.zh: 隱字叔括，保字季括，位並尚書郎。

translations.literal: Yin, courtesy name Shuguo; Bao, courtesy name Jiguo — posts both Gentlemen of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, styled Shuguo, and Bao, styled Jiguo, both served as Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 兄弟皆以儒素著名，時謂之四括。

translations.literal: The brothers all were famed for Confucian plainness, the age calling them the Four Guo.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were all famed for plain Confucian learning and were known in their time as the Four Guo.

sentences.zh: 機子楷，字雄方，位書侍御史，家于平棘南。

translations.literal: Ji's son Kai, courtesy name Xiongfang, post Writing Attendant Censor, established household south of Pingji.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's son Kai, styled Xiongfang, served as Writing Attendant Censor and made his home south of Pingji.

sentences.zh: 有男子五人，輯、晃、棨、勁、睿。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Ji, Huang, Qi, Jin, and Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Ji, Huang, Qi, Jin, and Rui.

sentences.zh: 輯字護宗，晃字仲黃，棨字季黃，勁字少黃，睿字幼黃，並以友悌著美，為當世所宗，時所謂四黃者也。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Huzong; Huang, courtesy name Zhonghuang; Qi, courtesy name Jihuang; Jin, courtesy name Shaohuang; Rui, courtesy name Youhuang — all famed for fraternal harmony, honored by the age, what the time called the Four Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji styled Huzong; Huang, Zhonghuang; Qi, Jihuang; Jin, Shaohuang; Rui, Youhuang—all renowned for brotherly harmony and honored by their contemporaries as the Four Huang.

sentences.zh: 輯位高密郡守，二子，慎、敦。

translations.literal: Ji held post as Administrator of Gaomi commandery; two sons, Shen and Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Ji served as Administrator of Gaomi; his two sons were Shen and Dun.

sentences.zh: 晃位鎮南府長史，一子，義。

translations.literal: Huang held post as Senior Clerk of the Pacify-the-South Commandery, one son, Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang served as Senior Clerk of the Pacify-the-South Commandery; his son was Yi.

sentences.zh: 勁位書侍御史，四子，盛、敏、隆、喜。

translations.literal: Jin held post Writing Attendant Censor, four sons: Sheng, Min, Long, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin served as Writing Attendant Censor and had four sons: Sheng, Min, Long, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 睿位高平太守，二子，勖、充。

translations.literal: Rui held post Gaoping Administrator, two sons, Xu and Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Rui served as Administrator of Gaoping; his two sons were Xu and Chong.

sentences.zh: 其後，慎、敦居柏仁，子孫甚微。

translations.literal: Afterwards Shen and Dun dwelt at Boren; descendants very few.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Shen and Dun settled at Boren, but their line barely survived.

sentences.zh: 義南徙故壘，世謂之南祖。

translations.literal: Yi moved south to the old fort; generations called this the Southern Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi moved south to the old fort—a branch later known as the Southern Ancestor line.

sentences.zh: 勖兄弟居巷東，盛兄弟居巷西，世人指其所居，因以為目，蓋自此也。

translations.literal: Xu's brothers dwelt east of the lane, Sheng's brothers west of the lane; people pointed to where they lived and thereby made designations—likely from this.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's branch lived east of the lane and Sheng's west; people took their dwellings as names for each line—and so the custom began.

sentences.zh: 義字敬仲，位司空長史。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Jingzhong, post Senior Clerk of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Jingzhong, served as Senior Clerk to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 生東宮舍人吉，字彥同。

translations.literal: He begat Eastern Palace Attendant Ji, courtesy name Yantong.
translations.idiomatic: He begat Ji, styled Yantong, an Attendant of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 吉生尚書郎聰，字小時。

translations.literal: Ji begat Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Cong, courtesy name Xiaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Ji begat Cong, styled Xiaoshi, a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 聰生真，字。

translations.literal: Cong begat Zhen, courtesy name [—].
translations.idiomatic: Cong begat Zhen, whose courtesy name is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 義深事列於後。

translations.literal: Yishen's affairs are recorded below.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yishen's biography follows below.

sentences.zh: 勖字景賢，位頓丘太守。

translations.literal: Xu, courtesy name Jingxian, post Dunqiu Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, styled Jingxian, served as Administrator of Dunqiu.

sentences.zh: 勖生趙郡太守頤，字彥祖。

translations.literal: Xu begat Zhao commandery Administrator Yi, courtesy name Yanzu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu begat Yi, styled Yanzu, Administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 頤生勰、系、曾，各有令子，事並列於前。

translations.literal: Yi begat Xie, Xi, and Zeng; each had fine sons, affairs all recorded above.
translations.idiomatic: Yi begat Xie, Xi, and Zeng—each line produced able men, their accounts given earlier in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 盛位中書郎。

translations.literal: Sheng held post Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng served as Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三子，纘、襲、閣。

translations.literal: Three sons: Zuan, Xi, and Ge.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Zuan, Xi, and Ge.

sentences.zh: 纘字緯業，位太尉祭酒。

translations.literal: Zuan, courtesy name Weiye, post Steward of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan, styled Weiye, served as Steward of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 生四子，誕、休、重、苞。

translations.literal: He begat four sons: Dan, Xiu, Zhong, and Bao.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Dan, Xiu, Zhong, and Bao.

sentences.zh: 誕字紹元，假趙郡太守。

translations.literal: Dan, courtesy name Shaoyuan, acting Zhao commandery Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, styled Shaoyuan, served as acting Administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 生四子，建、追、磪、龜。

translations.literal: He begat four sons: Jian, Zhui, Cui, and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Jian, Zhui, Cui, and Gui.

sentences.zh: 龜字神龜，位州主簿。

translations.literal: Gui, courtesy name Shengui, post Commandery Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Gui, styled Shengui, served as Chief Clerk of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 生二子，鳳林、秀林。

translations.literal: He begat two sons: Fonglin and Xiulin.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Fonglin and Xiulin.

sentences.zh: 李裔，字徽伯。

translations.literal: Li Yi, courtesy name Huibo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, styled Huibo.

sentences.zh: 父秀林，小名榼，性溫直。

translations.literal: Father Xiulin, childhood name Ke, nature warm and upright.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiulin, nicknamed Ke, was warm and upright in character.

sentences.zh: 太和中，中書博士，為頓丘相，豪右畏之。

translations.literal: In Taihe, Doctor of the Secretariat; served as Chancellor of Dunqiu; powerful families feared him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served as a Doctor of the Secretariat and Chancellor of Dunqiu, and the local magnates feared him.

sentences.zh: 景明初，試守博陵郡，抑強扶弱，政以嚴威為名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, trial Administrator of Boling commandery; restraining the strong and supporting the weak, governance famed for stern authority.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Jingming era he served as acting Administrator of Boling, restraining the powerful and aiding the weak—his rule became famed for stern authority.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Because of mother's mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒司馬、定州大中正、太中大夫。

translations.literal: Later became Steward of the Minister of Works, Senior Arbiter of Ding province, Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Steward of the Minister of Works, Senior Arbiter of Ding province, and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Died; posthumously enfeoffed Governor of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Governor of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 裔出後伯父鳳林。

translations.literal: Yi was given in succession to father's elder brother Fonglin.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was adopted as heir to his father's elder brother Fonglin.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中為定州鎮軍長史，帶博陵太守。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang served as Senior Clerk of the Pacifying Army of Ding province, concurrently Boling Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era he served as Senior Clerk of Ding's Pacifying Army and concurrently as Administrator of Boling.

sentences.zh: 于時逆賊杜洛周侵亂州界，裔潛引洛周，州遂陷沒。

translations.literal: At that time rebel Du Luozhou invaded and ravaged the commandery borders; Yi secretly invited Luozhou in, and the province then fell and was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Du Luozhou ravaged the borders of the province, Yi secretly admitted him—and the province fell.

sentences.zh: 洛周特無綱紀，至於市令、驛帥咸以為王，呼曰市王、驛王，乃封裔定州王。

translations.literal: Luozhou especially lacked discipline; even market magistrates and post-station chiefs all were made kings, called Market King and Post-station King; then enfeoffed Yi as King of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou ran a lawless camp: even market magistrates and post-station chiefs were made "kings"—Market King, Post-station King—and he enfeoffed Yi as King of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 洛周尋為葛榮所滅，裔仍事榮。

translations.literal: Luozhou soon was destroyed by Ge Rong; Yi still served Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Luozhou was soon destroyed by Ge Rong, and Yi then served Rong.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮禽葛榮，遂縶裔及高昂、薛修義、李無為等於晉陽。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong, then bound Yi together with Gao Ang, Xue Xiuyi, Li Wuwei, and others at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong captured Ge Rong, he imprisoned Yi together with Gao Ang, Xue Xiuyi, Li Wuwei, and others at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 從榮至洛，榮死乃免。

translations.literal: Following Rong to Luoyang, when Rong died then was released.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Rong to Luoyang and was released only after Rong's death.

sentences.zh: 天平初，以齊神武大丞相諮議參軍，參定策功，封固安縣伯，為候衛大將軍、陝州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, as Advisory Aide-de-Camp to Great Chancellor Shenwu of Qi; shared merit in settling the strategy; enfeoffed Baron of Gu'an county; made General of Garrison Guard and Governor of Shan province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he served as Advisory Aide to the great chancellor Shenwu of Qi, helped settle strategy, and was enfeoffed Baron of Gu'an county and appointed General of Garrison Guard and Governor of Shan province.

sentences.zh: 及周文帝攻克州城，見害。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou captured the provincial city, was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou took the provincial capital, Yi was killed.

sentences.zh: 東魏贈尚書令、司徒、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei posthumously granted Minister Mentor, Minister of Works, Governor of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei posthumously appointed him Minister Mentor, Minister of Works, and Governor of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 子子旦襲。

translations.literal: Son Zidan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zidan inherited his rank.

sentences.zh: 子旦弟子雄。

translations.literal: Zidan's younger brother Zixiong.
translations.idiomatic: Zidan's younger brother was Zixiong.

sentences.zh: 及晉王廣出鎮并州，以子雄為河北行台兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Prince Jin Guang went out to garrison Bing province, made Zixiong Minister of the Armies of the Hebei Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jin Guang went out to garrison Bing province, he appointed Zixiong Minister of the Armies of the Hebei Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上謂曰：「吾兒既少，卿兼文武之才，今者推誠相委，吾無北顧憂矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor told him: "My son is still young; you combine civil and military talent. Now I entrust you in good faith—I have no worry looking north."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told him: "My son is still young, and you possess both civil and military gifts. I now entrust you fully—I need no longer look north with worry."

sentences.zh: 」子雄頓首流涕，誓以效命。

translations.literal: " Zixiong kowtowed, tears flowing, vowing to give his life in service.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong kowtowed, weeping, and swore to serve with his life.

sentences.zh: 子雄當官正直，侃然有不可犯色，王甚敬憚，吏人稱焉。

translations.literal: Zixiong in office was upright, sternly bearing an unapproachable mien; the Prince greatly respected and feared him; officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong was upright in office, bearing a stern, unapproachable dignity; the prince deeply respected and feared him, and officials and commoners alike praised him.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，卒官。

translations.literal: After a year and more, died in office.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 子公挺嗣。

translations.literal: Son Gongting succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongting inherited his position.

sentences.zh: 裔從祖詵字令世，誕弟休之子也。

translations.literal: Yi's collateral ancestor Shen, courtesy name Lingshi, was son of Dan's younger brother Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's collateral kinsman Shen, styled Lingshi, was the son of Dan's younger brother Xiu.

sentences.zh: 休字紹則，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Xiu, courtesy name Shaozhe, Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, styled Shaozhe, served as Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 詵與族兄靈、族弟熙等俱被征，事在高允《征士頌》。

translations.literal: Shen together with clan elder brother Ling, clan younger brother Xi, and others all were summoned; the matter is in Gao Yun's "Eulogy for Recluses Summoned."
translations.idiomatic: Shen was summoned together with his clan elder Ling and younger kinsman Xi, among others—the episode appears in Gao Yun's Eulogy for Recluses Summoned.

sentences.zh: 詵位中書侍郎、京兆太守。

translations.literal: Shen held posts Attendant of the Secretariat, Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shen served as Attendant of the Secretariat and Administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 詵從祖弟善見，位趙郡太守。

translations.literal: Shen's collateral younger kinsman Shanjian, post Zhao commandery Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's collateral kinsman Shanjian served as Administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 善見子顯進，位州主簿、濮陽太守。

translations.literal: Shanjian's son Xianjin, posts Commandery Chief Clerk, Administrator of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shanjian's son Xianjin served as Chief Clerk of the prefecture and Administrator of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 顯進子暎，字暉道，位相州中從事、步兵校尉，贈殷州刺史。

translations.literal: Xianjin's son Ying, courtesy name Huidao, posts Staff Officer of the Central Office of Xiang province, Colonel of Footsoldiers; posthumously granted Governor of Yin province.
translations.idiomatic: Xianjin's son Ying, styled Huidao, served as Staff Officer of Xiang province and Colonel of Footsoldiers, and was posthumously appointed Governor of Yin province.

sentences.zh: 暎子普濟，學涉有名，性和韻，位濟北太守，時人語曰「入粗入細李普濟」。

translations.literal: Ying's son Puji, learning broad and famed, nature harmonious and balanced, post Administrator of Jibei; people of the time said: "Entering coarse, entering fine—Li Puji."
translations.idiomatic: Ying's son Puji was broadly learned and widely known, gentle and even-tempered by nature, and served as Administrator of Jibei. People said of him: "From the rough to the fine—there is Li Puji."

sentences.zh: 武定中，位北海太守。

translations.literal: In Wuding, post Administrator of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuding era he served as Administrator of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 暎弟育，字仲遠，位相州防城別將，以拒葛榮之勳，賜爵趙郡公。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Zhongyuan, post Separate Commander for City Defense of Xiang province; for merit in resisting Ge Rong, granted nobility Duke of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Yu, styled Zhongyuan, served as Separate Commander for City Defense of Xiang province; for merit in resisting Ge Rong he was granted the title Duke of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 後除金紫光祿大夫，卒，贈都官尚書，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Later removed and made Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp; died; posthumously granted Minister of Justice, posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and Purple Clasp; when he died he was posthumously made Minister of Justice and given the posthumous name Zhen, "Upright."

sentences.zh: 子愔襲，與從父兄普濟並應秀才舉，時人謂其所居為秀才村。

translations.literal: Son Yin succeeded; together with collateral elder brother Puji both responded to the xiucai examination; people of the time called where they dwelt Xiucai Village.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin inherited his rank; he and his elder cousin Puji both passed the xiucai examination, and people called their neighborhood Xiucai Village—the Village of Successful Scholars.

sentences.zh: 愔位太子舍人。

translations.literal: Yin held post Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 愔族叔肅，字彥邕，位員外常侍。

translations.literal: Yin's clan uncle Su, courtesy name Yanyong, post Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's clan uncle Su, styled Yanyong, served as Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 初諂附侍中元暉。

translations.literal: At first flattered and clung to Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Hui.
translations.idiomatic: At first he fawned on and attached himself to Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Hui.

sentences.zh: 後以左道事侍中穆紹。

translations.literal: Later by heterodox ways served Attendant-in-Ordinary Mu Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Attendant-in-Ordinary Mu Shao through heterodox arts.

sentences.zh: 常裸身被髮，畫復銜刀，於隱屏處為紹求福。

translations.literal: Often naked with disheveled hair, painted talismans holding knives in the mouth, in hidden screened places seeking blessings for Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Naked and with hair loose, painted talismans held in his teeth and a knife between his lips, he would perform rites in secret alcoves to seek blessings for Shao.

sentences.zh: 故紹愛之，薦為黃門郎。

translations.literal: Therefore Shao favored him, recommended him as Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Shao favored him for this and recommended him as Yellow Gate Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 性酒狂，從靈太后幸江陽王繼第，侍飲頗醉，言辭不遜，抗辱太傅、清河王懌。

translations.literal: Nature wine-mad; followed Empress Dowager Ling to visit the residence of Prince Jiangyang Ji, attending the drinking quite drunk, words not deferential, boldly insulting Grand Tutor Prince Qinghe Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was a drunkard by nature. When he accompanied Empress Dowager Ling on a visit to Prince Jiangyang Ji's residence, he drank heavily at table, spoke disrespectfully, and openly insulted Grand Tutor Prince Qinghe Yi.

sentences.zh: 為有司彈劾，太后恕之。

translations.literal: Was impeached by the relevant offices; Empress Dowager pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities impeached him, but the empress dowager pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 卒于夏州刺史。

translations.literal: Died as Governor of Xia province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Governor of Xia province.

sentences.zh: 肅從弟皦，字景林，有學識，位廷尉少卿，贈齊州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Su's collateral younger kinsman Jiao, courtesy name Jinglin, had learning and knowledge, post Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; posthumously granted Governor of Qi province; posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Su's kinsman Jiao, styled Jinglin, was learned and capable and served as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; posthumously appointed Governor of Qi province, he was given the posthumous name Xuan, "Manifest."

sentences.zh: 子慎，武定中，位東平太守。

translations.literal: Son Shen, in Wuding, post Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen served as Administrator of Dongping during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 皦從弟仲旋。

translations.literal: Jiao's collateral younger kinsman Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's kinsman Zhongxuan.

sentences.zh: 司徒左長史、恆農太守。

translations.literal: Senior Clerk of the Left of the Minister of Works, Administrator of Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Clerk on the Left of the Minister of Works and Administrator of Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 先是宮、牛二姓阻險為害，仲旋示以威惠，即並歸伏。

translations.literal: Previously the Gong and Niu two surnames blocked perilous places doing harm; Zhongxuan showed them authority and kindness, and at once all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Gong and Niu clans had lorded over a defensible stronghold and troubled the region; Zhongxuan met them with sternness and kindness, and they submitted at once.

sentences.zh: 累遷左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 天平初，遷都於鄴，以仲ＦＭ為營構將，進號衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianping, the capital was transferred to Ye; Zhongxuan was made Construction General; advanced title Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping, when the capital moved to Ye, Zhongxuan was made Construction General and promoted to Guard General.

sentences.zh: 出為兗州刺史，還除將作大匠，所曆並著聲績。

translations.literal: Went out as Governor of Yan province; returned and was made Master of Construction Works; all posts he passed through showed noted repute and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Yan province, then returned to court as Master of Construction Works; in every post he won noted repute.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Died; posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Three Insignia on a Par, Governor of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously appointed General of Agile Cavalry, with the Three Insignia on a Par, and Governor of Qing province.

sentences.zh: 子希良，侍御史。

translations.literal: Son Xiliang, Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiliang served as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 煥字仲文，小字醜瑰，中書侍郎盛弟隆之後也。

translations.literal: Huan, courtesy name Zhongwen, childhood name Chougui, descended from Attendant of the Secretariat Sheng's younger brother Long.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, styled Zhongwen, nicknamed Chougui, was descended from Sheng's younger brother Long—the Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 隆字太彝，位阜城令。

translations.literal: Long, courtesy name Taiyi, post Magistrate of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Long, styled Taiyi, served as Magistrate of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 隆生幕縣令謀。

translations.literal: Long had Mou, magistrate of Mu county.
translations.idiomatic: Long had a son Mou, who served as magistrate of Mu county.

sentences.zh: 謀生始平太守景，名犯太祖元皇帝諱。

translations.literal: Mou had Jing, Administrator of Shiping, whose given name violated the taboo of Grand Ancestor Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mou had a son Jing, Administrator of Shiping, whose given name violated the taboo name of Grand Ancestor Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 景生東郡太守伯應。

translations.literal: Jing had Boying, Administrator of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing had a son Boying, Administrator of Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 伯應生煥。

translations.literal: Boying had Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Boying had a son Huan.

sentences.zh: 煥有幹用，與酈道元俱為李彪所知。

translations.literal: Huan had capacity for practical affairs; together with Li Daoyuan he was recognized by Li Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had proven ability in practical affairs, and he and Li Daoyuan alike won the notice of Li Biao.

sentences.zh: 恆州刺史穆泰據代都謀反，煥以書侍御史與任城王澄推究之。

translations.literal: Mu Tai, Inspector of Heng province, seized the Dai capital and plotted rebellion; Huan, as Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary for Writing, together with Prince Cheng of Rencheng investigated it.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Tai, Inspector of Heng Province, seized the Dai capital and plotted rebellion, Huan served as palace attendant-in-ordinary for writing and, together with Prince Cheng of Rencheng, conducted the investigation.

sentences.zh: 煥先驅至州，宣旨曉喻，乃執泰等。

translations.literal: Huan went ahead as vanguard to the province, proclaimed the imperial decree and explained it, then arrested Tai and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Huan rode ahead to the province, proclaimed the imperial decree and explained its meaning, and then arrested Tai and his co-conspirators.

sentences.zh: 景明初，齊豫州刺史裴叔業以壽春歸附，煥以司空從事中郎為軍司馬，與楊大眼、奚康生等迎接，仍行揚州事，賜爵容城伯。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingming, Pei Shuye of Southern Qi, Inspector of Yu province, surrendered Shouchun; Huan served as Army Marshal with the title Attendant-in-Ordinary under the Minister of Works, and together with Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and others went to receive him; he was then put in charge of Yang province affairs and granted the title Marquis of Rongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingming era, Pei Shuye of Southern Qi, Inspector of Yu Province, surrendered Shouchun. Huan served as army marshal with the title Attendant-in-Ordinary under the Minister of Works and, together with Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and others, went out to receive him. He was then put in charge of Yang Province affairs and granted the title Marquis of Rongcheng.

sentences.zh: 及荊蠻擾動，敕煥兼通直散騎常侍慰勞之，降者萬餘家。

translations.literal: When the Jing barbarians stirred in unrest, an edict ordered Huan concurrently as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry to comfort them; more than ten thousand households submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When unrest spread among the Jing barbarians, the court ordered Huan, concurrently serving as regular attendant of direct communication and cavalry, to go and reassure them; more than ten thousand households surrendered.

sentences.zh: 除梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Liang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Inspector of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 時武興氐楊集起舉兵作逆，敕假煥平西將軍，督別將大破集起軍。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Jieqi of the Wuxing Di raised troops in rebellion; an edict provisionally appointed Huan General Who Pacifies the West and ordered him to supervise separate generals in greatly defeating Jieqi's army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Jieqi of the Wuxing Di raised troops in rebellion. By edict Huan was provisionally made General Who Pacifies the West and directed subordinate generals in a major defeat of Jieqi's forces.

sentences.zh: 又破秦州賊呂苟兒，及斬氐王楊定。

translations.literal: He also defeated the brigand Lü Gou'er of Qin province and beheaded the Di king Yang Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the Qin Province bandit Lü Gou'er and beheaded the Di king Yang Ding.

sentences.zh: 還朝，遇患卒，贈幽州刺史，諡曰昭。
