translations.literal: Returning to court, he fell ill and died; posthumously granted Inspector of You province, posthumous title Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he fell ill and died. He was posthumously made Inspector of You Province with the posthumous title Zhao (Illustrious).

sentences.zh: 子密，字希邕，少有節操。

translations.literal: His son Mi, styled Xiyong, from youth had integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mi, styled Xiyong, had been upright in character since youth.

sentences.zh: 母患積年，名醫療之不愈，乃精習經方，洞閑針藥，母疾得除。

translations.literal: His mother suffered illness for years; famous physicians treated her without cure; he then thoroughly studied canonical prescriptions, became thoroughly skilled in acupuncture and medicine, and his mother's illness was removed.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been ill for years, and even famous physicians could not cure her. He then mastered canonical prescriptions and became thoroughly skilled in acupuncture and medicine, and his mother's illness was finally cured.

sentences.zh: 由是以醫術知名。

translations.literal: From this he became renowned for medical skill.
translations.idiomatic: From this he became renowned for his medical skill.

sentences.zh: 屬爾硃兆弑逆，與勃海高昂為報復計。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao committed regicide, together with Gao Ang of Bohai he plotted revenge.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao committed regicide, he joined Gao Ang of Bohai in plotting revenge.

sentences.zh: 後從神武，封容城縣侯，位襄州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Huan, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Rongcheng county, and held the post of Inspector of Xiang province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Huan, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Rongcheng County, and served as Inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 李義深，趙郡高邑人也。

translations.literal: Li Yishen was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yishen was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖真，字令才，位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen, styled Lingcai, held the post of Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen, styled Lingcai, served as Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父紹，字嗣宗，殷州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Shao, styled Sigong, was Vice Governor of Yin province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao, styled Sigong, was Vice Governor of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 義深有當世才用，而心胸險峭，時人語曰：「劍戟森森李義深。

translations.literal: Yishen had talent useful in his age, but his heart was treacherous and precipitous; people of the time said: "Swords and halberds densely arrayed—Li Yishen."
translations.idiomatic: Yishen had talent fit for his age, but his heart was treacherous and sharp-edged. People of the time said, "Swords and halberds densely arrayed—Li Yishen."

sentences.zh: 」初以殷州別駕歸齊神武，再遷鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: At first, as Vice Governor of Yin province he submitted to Gao Huan of Northern Qi and was twice promoted to Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as Vice Governor of Yin Province, he submitted to Gao Huan of Northern Qi and was twice promoted to Vice Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 見爾硃兆兵盛，叛歸之。

translations.literal: Seeing Erzhu Zhao's armies strong, he defected and returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Erzhu Zhao's armies at their height, he defected and went over to him.

sentences.zh: 兆平，神武恕其罪。

translations.literal: When Zhao was defeated, Gao Huan pardoned his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was defeated, Gao Huan pardoned his offense.

sentences.zh: 遷齊州刺史，好利，多所受納。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Qi province; fond of profit, he accepted many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Qi Province. Greedy for gain, he accepted many bribes.

sentences.zh: 轉行梁州刺史，為陽夏太守段業告其在州聚斂，被禁止。

translations.literal: Transferred to act as Inspector of Liang province; Duan Ye, Administrator of Yangxia, reported that he amassed wealth in the province; he was detained.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Inspector of Liang Province. Duan Ye, Administrator of Yangxia, reported that he had amassed wealth in the province, and he was placed under detention.

sentences.zh: 卒於禁所。

translations.literal: He died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: He died in detention.

sentences.zh: 子騊駼，有才辯，位兼通直散騎常侍，聘陳。

translations.literal: His son Taotao was talented in eloquence, held the concurrent post of Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry, and went on embassy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taotao was gifted in eloquence, served concurrently as regular attendant of direct communication and cavalry, and went on embassy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳人稱之。

translations.literal: The people of Chen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chen praised him.

sentences.zh: 後為壽陽道行台左丞，與王琳同陷陳。

translations.literal: Later he served as Left Assistant of the Branch Headquarters on the Shouyang route and, together with Wang Lin, was trapped in Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Left Assistant of the Branch Headquarters on the Shouyang route and, together with Wang Lin, was captured in Chen.

sentences.zh: 周末逃歸。

translations.literal: At the end of Northern Zhou he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Northern Zhou he escaped and returned home.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中為永安郡太守、絳州長史，卒。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang of Sui he served as Administrator of Yong'an commandery and Chief Commandant of Jiang prefecture, then died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui he served as Administrator of Yong'an Commandery and Chief Commandant of Jiang Prefecture, and then died.

sentences.zh: 子政藻，明敏有才幹。

translations.literal: His son Zhengzao was clear-minded, perceptive, and capable.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengzao was bright, perceptive, and capable.

sentences.zh: 騊駼沒陳，政藻時為開府行參軍，判集書省事，便謝病解職，居處若在喪禮，人士稱之。

translations.literal: When Taotao was lost in Chen, Zhengzao was at the time Staff Officer in the Opening Establishment, handling affairs of the Office of Collected Writings; he immediately pleaded illness and resigned his office, conducting himself as if in mourning rites; gentlemen praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taotao was lost in Chen, Zhengzao was then a staff officer in the opening establishment, handling affairs of the Office of Collected Writings. He immediately pleaded illness and resigned, conducting himself as if in mourning. Gentlemen praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，曆尚書工部員外郎，卒於宜州長史。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang he successively served as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works of the Masters of Writing and died while Chief Commandant of Yi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang he served successively as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works under the Masters of Writing and died while serving as Chief Commandant of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 騊駼弟文師，曆中書舍人，齊郡太守。

translations.literal: Taotao's younger brother Wenshi successively served as Drafting Secretary of the Palace Secretariat and Administrator of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Taotao's younger brother Wenshi successively served as drafting secretary of the Palace Secretariat and Administrator of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 義深弟同軌，體貌魁岸，腰帶十圍，學綜諸經，兼該釋氏，又好醫術。

translations.literal: Yishen's younger brother Tonggui had a towering physique, a belt ten arm-spans around, mastery of all the classics, thorough knowledge of Buddhism, and also loved medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Yishen's younger brother Tonggui had a towering physique and a waist ten arm-spans around. He had mastered all the classics, was thoroughly versed in Buddhism, and also loved medicine.

sentences.zh: 年二十，舉秀才，再遷著作郎，典儀注，修國子博士。

translations.literal: At age twenty he was nominated as Flowering Talent, twice promoted to Gentleman Compiler, oversaw ritual regulations, and was appointed Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was nominated as Flowering Talent, was twice promoted to gentleman compiler, oversaw ritual regulations, and was appointed erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 興和中，兼通直散騎常侍，使梁。

translations.literal: During Xinghe he concurrently served as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry and went on embassy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: During Xinghe he concurrently served as regular attendant of direct communication and cavalry and went on embassy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁武深耽釋學，遂集名僧於其愛敬、同泰二寺，講《涅般大品經》，引同軌豫席，兼遣其朝士議共觀聽，同軌論難久之，道俗咸以為善。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang deeply devoted himself to Buddhist learning; he gathered renowned monks at his Aijin and Tongtai monasteries to lecture on the Mahaparinirvana Sutra, invited Tonggui to a reserved seat, and also sent his court gentlemen to observe and listen together; Tonggui debated for a long time; clergy and laity alike judged it excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang was deeply devoted to Buddhist learning. He gathered renowned monks at his Aijin and Tongtai monasteries to lecture on the Mahaparinirvana Sutra, invited Tonggui to a reserved seat, and also sent court gentlemen to listen. Tonggui debated at length, and clergy and laity alike judged it excellent.

sentences.zh: 盧景裕卒，齊神武引同軌在館教諸公子，甚嘉禮之。

translations.literal: When Lu Jingyu died, Gao Huan summoned Tonggui to the residence to teach the various princes' sons and greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Jingyu died, Gao Huan summoned Tonggui to the residence to instruct the sons of the princes and treated him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 每旦入授，日暮始歸，緇素請業者，同軌夜為解說，四時恆爾，不以為倦。

translations.literal: Each morning he entered to instruct, only returning at dusk; those who requested instruction, lay and clerical alike, Tonggui explained for them by night; through all four seasons it was always thus, and he did not consider it wearisome.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he entered to teach and only returned at dusk. For those who sought instruction, lay and clerical alike, Tonggui explained by night. Through all four seasons it was always thus, and he never considered it wearisome.

sentences.zh: 卒，時人傷惜之，神武亦嗟悼之。

translations.literal: He died; people of the time grieved and regretted it, and Gao Huan also sighed in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, people of the time grieved for him, and Gao Huan also sighed in mourning.

sentences.zh: 贈瀛州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Inspector of Ying province, posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Inspector of Ying Province with the posthumous title Kang (Peaceful).

sentences.zh: 同軌弟幼舉，安德太守，以貪污棄市。

translations.literal: Tonggui's younger brother Youju, Administrator of An'de, was executed in the market for embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui's younger brother Youju, Administrator of An'de, was executed in the market for embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 幼舉弟之良，有幹用，位金部郎中。

translations.literal: Youju's younger brother Zhiliang had practical capacity and held the post of Gentleman of the Gold Department.
translations.idiomatic: Youju's younger brother Zhiliang had practical ability and served as Gentleman of the Gold Department.

sentences.zh: 之良弟幼廉，少寡欲，為兒童時，初不從人家有所求請。

translations.literal: Zhiliang's younger brother Youlian from youth had few desires; as a child he never asked anything from others' households.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiliang's younger brother Youlian had few desires from youth. Even as a child he never asked anything of other people's households.

sentences.zh: 嘗故以金寶授之，終不取，強付，輒擲之地。

translations.literal: Once someone deliberately gave him gold and jewels; he never took them; when forced upon him, he would always throw them to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Once someone deliberately offered him gold and jewels. He would never take them; when they were forced on him, he would throw them to the ground.

sentences.zh: 州牧以其蒙幼而廉，故以名焉。

translations.literal: The provincial governor, because he was young and yet upright, therefore gave him this name.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial governor, seeing that he was young and yet upright, gave him this name.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，累遷齊文襄驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: By nature intelligent and keen, he was repeatedly promoted to Chief Clerk of the Rapid Cavalry Establishment of Wenxiang of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent and keen by nature, he was repeatedly promoted to chief clerk of the Rapid Cavalry Establishment under Wenxiang of Qi.

sentences.zh: 文襄薦為濟州儀同府長史，又遷瀛州長史。

translations.literal: Wenxiang recommended him as Chief Clerk of the Establishment Equal to the First of Ji prefecture; he was later transferred to Chief Clerk of Ying prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang recommended him as chief clerk of the Establishment Equal to the First of Ji Prefecture, and he was later transferred to chief clerk of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊神武行經冀部，總合河北六州文籍，商榷戶口增損，親自部分，多在馬上征責文簿，指影取備，事非一緒。

translations.literal: Gao Huan traveled through Ji region, consolidated the registers of the six Hebei provinces, deliberated on increases and decreases in household registers, personally divided and assigned the work, often on horseback pressing for completion of documents, demanding readiness at a gesture—a matter not of one kind alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan traveled through the Ji region, he consolidated the registers of the six Hebei provinces and deliberated over increases and decreases in household counts. He personally divided the work, often on horseback pressing for the completion of documents and demanding readiness at a gesture—there was no end to the tasks.

sentences.zh: 幼廉應機立成，恆先期會，為諸州准的。

translations.literal: Youlian responded to each occasion and finished at once, always meeting deadlines ahead of time, and became the standard for all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Youlian responded to each occasion and finished at once, always meeting deadlines ahead of time. He became the standard by which all the provinces were measured.

sentences.zh: 神武深加慰勉，乃責諸人曰：「碎卿等諸人，作得李長史一腳指不！

translations.literal: Gao Huan deeply praised and encouraged him, then rebuked the others, saying: "Ground you all to pieces—you could not make even one of Director Li's little toes!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan praised and encouraged him deeply, then rebuked the others, saying, "Grind you all to powder—you could not make even one of Director Li's little toes!"

sentences.zh: 」是時諸人並謝罪，幼廉獨前拜恩，觀者咸歎美之。

translations.literal: At this time all the others apologized; Youlian alone stepped forward to bow in gratitude, and onlookers all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment all the others apologized, but Youlian alone stepped forward to bow in gratitude. Onlookers all sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 神武還并州，以告文襄，文襄喜謂人曰：「吾是知人矣！

translations.literal: Gao Huan returned to Bing province and told Wenxiang; Wenxiang said delightedly to others: "I truly know how to recognize men!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan returned to Bing Province and told Wenxiang, who said delightedly to others, "I truly know how to recognize men!"

sentences.zh: 」文襄嗣事，除霸府掾。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang succeeded to affairs, he appointed him staff officer of the Hegemonic Establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang succeeded to power, he appointed him staff officer of the Hegemonic Establishment.

sentences.zh: 時以并州王政所基，求好長史，舉者多不見納。

translations.literal: At the time, because Bing province was the foundation of princely administration, they sought a good chief clerk; many nominees were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, because Bing Province was the foundation of princely administration, they sought a good chief clerk, but many nominees were not accepted.

sentences.zh: 後因大集，謂陳元康曰：「我教你好長史處，李幼廉即其人也。

translations.literal: Later, during a great assembly, he said to Chen Yuankang: "I'll teach you where to find a good chief clerk—Li Youlian is the man."
translations.idiomatic: Later, during a great assembly, he said to Chen Yuankang, "I will show you where to find a good chief clerk—Li Youlian is the man."

sentences.zh: 」遂命為并州長史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Chief Clerk of Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Chief Clerk of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 常在文襄第內，與隴西辛術等六人，號為館客。

translations.literal: He was often within Wenxiang's mansion, and together with Xin Shu of Longxi and five others was called "Residence Guests."
translations.idiomatic: He was often in Wenxiang's mansion, and together with Xin Shu of Longxi and five others was known as the Residence Guests.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除太原郡太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed Administrator of Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed Administrator of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 文宣嘗與語及楊愔，誤稱為楊公，以應對失宜，除濟陰郡守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan once conversed with him about Yang Yin and mistakenly called him "Lord Yang"; for an improper reply he was demoted to Administrator of Jiyin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan once spoke with him about Yang Yin and mistakenly called him "Lord Yang." For an improper reply he was demoted to Administrator of Jiyin Commandery.

sentences.zh: 累遷太僕大司農二卿、趙州大中正、大理卿，所在稱職。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to the two ministries of the Grand Keeper of Steeds and Grand Minister of Agriculture, Senior Rectifier of Zhao province, and Minister of Punishments; everywhere he was called competent.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to the ministries of the Grand Keeper of Steeds and Grand Minister of Agriculture, made Senior Rectifier of Zhao Province, and appointed Minister of Punishments. Everywhere he served he was called competent.

sentences.zh: 後主時，和士開權重，百僚盡傾，幼廉高揖而已，由是出為南青州刺史。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Later Lord, He Shikai's power was heavy and all officials bowed low; Youlian merely gave a high salute, and for this reason was sent out as Inspector of Southern Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Later Lord, He Shikai's power was great and all officials bowed low. Youlian merely gave a high salute, and for this reason was sent out as Inspector of Southern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 主簿徐乾富而暴橫，曆政不能禁。

translations.literal: Registrar Xu Qian was wealthy and violently overbearing; successive administrations could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Registrar Xu Qian was wealthy and violently overbearing. Successive administrations could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 幼廉初至，因其有犯，收系之。

translations.literal: When Youlian first arrived, because he had committed offenses, he had him arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Youlian first arrived, he had Qian arrested and imprisoned for his offenses.

sentences.zh: 乾密通疏，奉黃金百挺、妓婢二十人，幼廉不受，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Qian secretly communicated through a memorial, offering a hundred ingots of gold and twenty singing girls and maidservants; Youlian would not accept and then had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian secretly sent a memorial offering a hundred ingots of gold and twenty singing girls and maidservants. Youlian refused to accept and then had him executed.

sentences.zh: 罷還鄴。

translations.literal: He finished his term and returned to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He finished his term and returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 祖孝征執政。

translations.literal: Zu Xiaozheng held power.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Xiaozheng held power.

sentences.zh: 求紫石英于幼廉，以其南青州所出。

translations.literal: He sought amethyst from Youlian because Southern Qing province produced it.
translations.idiomatic: He sought amethyst from Youlian because Southern Qing Province produced it.

sentences.zh: 幼廉辭無好者，固請，乃與二兩。

translations.literal: Youlian declined, saying there were none of fine quality; when pressed he gave only two ounces.
translations.idiomatic: Youlian declined, saying there were none of fine quality. When pressed, he gave only two ounces.

sentences.zh: 孝征有不平之言，或以告幼廉。

translations.literal: Xiaozheng had resentful words; someone may have told Youlian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozheng had words of resentment, and someone may have told Youlian.

sentences.zh: 幼廉抗聲曰：「李幼廉結髮從宦，誓不曲意求人。

translations.literal: Youlian raised his voice and said: "Li Youlian has served in office since tying his hair; I swear never to bend my will seeking favor from others."
translations.idiomatic: Youlian raised his voice and said, "Li Youlian has served in office since tying his hair. I swear never to bend my will to seek favor from others."

sentences.zh: 天生德於予，孝征其如予何？

translations.literal: Heaven has endowed me with virtue—what can Xiaozheng do to me?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has endowed me with virtue—what can Xiaozheng do to me?

sentences.zh: 假欲挫頓，不過遣向并州耳。

translations.literal: Even if he wished to humiliate me, at most he would send me back to Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: Even if he wished to humiliate me, at most he would send me back to Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 」時已授並省都官尚書，辭而未報，遂發敕遣之。

translations.literal: At the time he had already been appointed Minister of Punishments of the Bing Province Secretariat but had declined and not yet reported; an edict was then issued dispatching him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he had already been appointed Minister of Punishments of the Bing Province Secretariat but had declined and not yet reported. An edict was then issued dispatching him.

sentences.zh: 齊末官至三品已上，悉加儀同，獨不沾此例，語人曰：「我不作儀同，更覺為榮。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi, officials of third rank and above all received the added title Equal in Glory to the First; he alone did not share in this; he told others: "Not taking the title Equal in Glory to the First makes me feel more honored still."
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qi, officials of third rank and above all received the added title Equal in Glory to the First. He alone did not share in this and told others, "Not taking the title Equal in Glory to the First makes me feel more honored still."

sentences.zh: 」卒，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 義深族弟神威，幼有風裁，家業《禮》學，又善音樂，撰集樂書近百卷，卒于尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Yishen's clansman younger brother Shenwei from youth had integrity and judgment, inherited scholarship in the Rites, was also skilled in music, compiled and collected nearly a hundred scrolls of music books, and died while Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yishen's clansman younger brother Shenwei had integrity and judgment from youth, inherited scholarship in the Rites, and was also skilled in music. He compiled nearly a hundred scrolls of music books and died while serving as Left Assistant of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 又有李翥，字彥鴻，世居柏仁，弱冠以文章知。

translations.literal: There was also Li Zhu, styled Yanhong, whose family for generations resided in Bairen, known for his literary compositions from his capping at weak age.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Li Zhu, styled Yanhong, whose family had lived in Bairen for generations and who was known for his writing from the time of his capping.

sentences.zh: 仁齊，位東平太守。

translations.literal: He served Northern Qi and held the post of Administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He served Northern Qi and held the post of Administrator of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 後待詔文林館，除通直散騎常侍，聘于梁。

translations.literal: Later he was retained at the Forest of Literature Hall as awaiting-edict, appointed Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry, and went on embassy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was retained at the Forest of Literature Hall as awaiting-edict, appointed regular attendant of direct communication and cavalry, and sent on embassy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 晚節頗以貪酒為累。

translations.literal: In his later years he was much burdened by excess in drink.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was much burdened by excessive drinking.

sentences.zh: 貪無居宅，寄止佛寺中。

translations.literal: Poor without a dwelling, he lodged in Buddhist temples.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and without a dwelling, he lodged in Buddhist temples.

sentences.zh: 嘗著巾帔，終日對酒，招致賓客，風調詳雅。

translations.literal: He would wear a headcloth and kerchief, face wine all day, summon guests, his manner refined and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: He would wear a headcloth and kerchief, drink all day, summon guests, and carry himself with refined elegance.

sentences.zh: 翥從兄子朗，才辭翥之亞，兼有吏能，位中書舍人。

translations.literal: Zhu's clansman's son Lang was second only to Zhu in literary talent, also possessed administrative ability, and held the post of Drafting Secretary of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's clansman's son Lang was second only to Zhu in literary talent, also possessed administrative ability, and served as drafting secretary of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古人云「燕、趙多奇士」，觀夫李靈兄弟，並有焉。

translations.literal: Commentary says: The ancients said "Yan and Zhao produce many extraordinary men"; observing the Li Ling brothers, they all had this quality.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary says: The ancients said, "Yan and Zhao produce many extraordinary men." Looking at the brothers of Li Ling, they all had this quality.

sentences.zh: 靈則首應弓旌，道光師傅。

translations.literal: Ling was first to respond to the imperial summons, his conduct illumining his teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Ling was the first to answer the imperial summons, and his conduct illumined his teachers.

sentences.zh: 順則器標楝幹，一時推重。

translations.literal: Shun's talent marked him as a pillar beam, esteemed in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's talent marked him as a pillar beam, and his age held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 孝伯風範鑒略，蓋亦過人。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's bearing and discernment also surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's bearing and discernment also surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 各能克廣門業，道風不殞，余慶之美，豈非此之謂乎。

translations.literal: Each was able to broaden his family's enterprise; the Way's wind did not fade—the beauty of enduring blessings, is this not what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: Each was able to broaden his family's enterprise, and the wind of the Way did not fade. The beauty of enduring blessings—is this not what is meant?

sentences.zh: 至如元忠之倜儻從橫，功名自卒；

translations.literal: As for Yuanzhong's unconventional breadth, merit and fame came of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: As for Yuanzhong's unconventional breadth, merit and fame came of themselves;

sentences.zh: 季初之家風素業，昆季兼舉。

translations.literal: Jichu's family tradition of plain integrity, brothers all rising together.
translations.idiomatic: Jichu's family tradition of plain integrity saw brothers rising together.

sentences.zh: 有齊之日，雅道方振。

translations.literal: In the days when Qi existed, refined culture was just then flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: In the days when Qi existed, refined culture was just then flourishing.

sentences.zh: 憲之子弟，特盛衣纓，豈唯戚裏是憑，固亦文雅所得。

translations.literal: Xian's sons and younger brothers especially flourished in court ranks—is it only dependence on imperial kinship? It is also what refined culture obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The sons and younger brothers of Xian especially flourished in court ranks. Was it only dependence on imperial kinship? It was also what refined culture obtained.

sentences.zh: 安世識具通雅，時幹之良。

translations.literal: Anshi's knowledge was comprehensive and broadly refined—a fine talent of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi's knowledge was comprehensive and broadly refined—a fine talent of the age.

sentences.zh: 枿以豪俊達，鬱則儒博顯，謐之高逸，固可謂世有人焉。

translations.literal: Nie achieved eminence through bold excellence; Yu gained prominence through learned breadth; Mi's lofty reclusion—truly one may say the age had its men.
translations.idiomatic: Nie achieved eminence through bold excellence; Yu gained prominence through learned breadth; Mi's lofty reclusion—truly one may say the age had its men.

sentences.zh: 義深弟兄，人位兼美；

translations.literal: Yishen and his brothers—men and offices alike admirable;
translations.idiomatic: Yishen and his brothers—men and offices alike admirable;

sentences.zh: 子雄才官，不替門緒，茂矣。

translations.literal: Zixiong's talent and office did not fail the family's line—how flourishing!
translations.idiomatic: Zixiong's talent and office did not fail the family line—how flourishing!
